articles.title: 'A lot of the time, for emotional scenes, we would be playing the Requiem soundtrack' — Asobo Studio used A Plague Tale: Requiem's music during Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy mocap to help actors get into the 'sadder' and 'darker' scenes
articles.text:
Asobo Studio used the soundtrack from A Plague Tale: Requiem during Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy mocap to help the cast 'get into the sadder moments, the darker moments'
The game's original soundtrack was composed by Olivier Derivière
- Asobo Studio played A Plague Tale: Requiem's soundtrack while motion-capturing Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy
- The cast would listen to the game's music to get into the right headspace for emotional scenes
- SPEAKER 3 says it helped "get into the sadder moments, the darker moments"
Asobo Studio has revealed that it used A Plague Tale: Requiem's music while motion-capturing Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy, so the cast could get in the mood for the darker scenes.
Speaking in an interview with TechRadar Gaming during Gamescom, developers Valérian Robert (lead level designer) and Carol Ann Bañuls (lead writer), and the actor for the game's protagonist, Sophia, Anna Demetriou, discussed the design process for the game's atmosphere and the music that goes with it.
When asked how the team implemented audio and the game's score for the upcoming sequel, Anna Demetriou explained that Asobo played music tracks from A Plague Tale: Requiem to allow the actors to get into the right headspace for emotional scenes.
"A lot of the time, for emotional scenes, we would be playing the Requiem soundtrack to help us get into the sadder moments, the darker moments," Anna Demetriou said. "So it felt really like the beating [heart] of the [Plague Tale DNA] was still in the mocap room because we were using them and using this reference for some of the hard bits and stuff."
Resonance's score was composed by Olivier Derivière and sounds quite different from any of the prior games, with an emphasis on Greek culture, as the game's setting has moved from Middle Ages France to the Greek island of Crete.
"The incredible Greek soundtrack that has been done by Olivier, I had none of that at all," Demetriou continued, "So hearing it coming out, and the whole thing's on YouTube right now, I was sat on my laptop for the day, just listening to it all, just being like, 'I can't wait to play it because I I haven't connected what we've done with this with the music yet.'"
Bañuls added that Olivier also used choir vocals to give the soundtrack a more "authentic" feel for the time period, withRobert explaining that the music is also woven into the new gameplay systems and combat.

articles.title: Google Messages : vous pouvez enfin personnaliser vos conversations, mais à une condition
articles.text:
Google Messages : vous pouvez enfin personnaliser vos conversations, mais à une condition
Il est enfin possible d'appliquer des thèmes et des fonds d'écran à ses conversations sur Google Messages. Voyons comment faire, tandis qu'il faudra activer une option bien spécifique pour pouvoir en profiter.
Depuis de nombreux mois maintenant, Google met les bouchées doubles pour que son application de messagerie Google Messages rattrape WhatsApp, Signal et autres Messenger. La firme ajoute ainsi régulièrement des fonctionnalités généralement déjà disponibles ailleurs. C'est le cas en ce 27 août 2026, avec une nouveauté qui plaira aux personnes adeptes de personnalisation. Il est en effet enfin possible de personnaliser l'apparence de ses conversations de manière individuelle.
De la personnalisation dans Google Messages, toujours plus complète
Pas question pour Google de révolutionner la personnalisation des conversations. Il est ici proposé d'appliquer deux éléments de manière individuelle (et non de manière globale) aux conversations de son choix : un thème de couleurs et une image de fond d'écran. Vos choix ne sont visibles que pour vous, et non vos contacts.
Concernant le fond d'écran, il est possible de choisir sa propre image ou bien parmi des images rangées par catégories (animaux, paysages, espace...). Lorsqu'une image est sélectionnée, la couleur des bulles s'ajuste automatiquement. Il est cependant possible de choisir son propre thème de couleurs parmi les quelques palettes proposées.
Pour personnaliser l'apparence d'une conversation, c'est simple. Une fois celle-ci ouverte, appuyez au choix sur les trois points en haut à droite ou sur le nom du ou des destinataires en haut. Sélectionnez "Thème du chat" et faites vos choix. Ne reste plus qu'à appuyer sur "Appliquer".
Pour pouvoir profiter de cette nouvelle fonctionnalité, vous n'avez que deux choses à faire. La première, vous assurer de disposer de la dernière version de l'application, via le Play Store. La seconde, avoir activé le protocole RCS, qui utilise le WiFi ou le réseau de données mobiles pour envoyer des messages. Ce dernier l'est généralement par défaut. Sinon, direction Paramètres de Messages > Chats RCS > Activer les chats RCS.

articles.title: Google Tasks : cette fonction toute bête que l'on attendait tous pourrait enfin arriver
articles.text:
Pourtant très pratique pour gérer ses rappels ou ses todolists au quotidien, Google Tasks souffre d’un manque difficile à justifier : l’impossibilité de rechercher une tâche spécifique. Alors que des concurrents comme Todoist ou TickTick proposent cette option depuis belle lurette, l’outil du géant américain force encore ses utilisateurs à faire défiler leurs listes à la main. La situation pourrait heureusement bientôt changer.
Enfin une barre de recherche dans Google Tasks ?
Après la barre de recherche dans Google Keep, Google pourrait aussi en intégrer une dans son application Tasks. Une fois n’est pas coutume, c’est en analysant le code de l’application que l’on découvre plusieurs traces explicites d’une barre de recherche en cours de développement. On y retrouve ainsi la mention « Rechercher une tâche », mais aussi un fichier XML dédié à la mise en page et l’icône de recherche elle-même.
Même s’il a été impossible d’activer l’interface avant son lancement officiel, les éléments trouvés dans le code ne laissent aucun doute sur les intentions des développeurs. L’intégration s’appuierait sur le composant standard de la barre de recherche de Google pour s’insérer en haut des listes. Rien n’est encore déployé auprès du grand public donc, mais les bases sont prêtes dans l’application.
Un rattrapage tardif, mais indispensable
Au cours des derniers mois, Google a multiplié les efforts pour enrichir son gestionnaire de tâches. L’application a notamment récupéré l’importation des rappels issus de Google Keep ainsi qu’une meilleure gestion des dates limites. L’absence d’un simple moteur de recherche interne restait donc d’autant plus flagrante pour les utilisateurs réguliers qui accumulent des dizaines de notes.
Comme toujours, rien n’est garanti à 100 % tant que la fonctionnalité n’est pas déployée. Ceci étant dit, elle est tellement basique et attendue qu’on voit mal Google ne pas finir par la proposer. La vraie question est plutôt de savoir quand elle finira par arriver sur Google Tasks.

articles.title: Autonomie boostée et recharge rapide en série à 24 990 € : la Renault 5 réussit sa rentrée
articles.text:
Une rentrée réussie est synonyme de préparation. Renault a visiblement imposé les cahiers de vacances à la R5 pour lui donner toutes ses chances à la reprise. Dont acte : la citadine électrique révise ses fondamentaux et corrige ses faiblesses. Son équipement est ainsi enrichi, son autonomie est gonflée tandis que son offre de personnalisation s’élargit. Le prix, lui, ne bouge pas d’un iota, ce qui est une bonne nouvelle.
Autonomie en hausse : la R5 va un peu plus loin
Grâce à un travail d’optimisation sur l’électronique de la batterie combiné à un aérodynamisme plus léché obtenu par l’adoption de bas de caisse inédits et de rétroviseurs affinés, la R5 étend sans mal son rayon d’action. Le pack de 40 kWh passe ainsi de 312 à 315 km alors que l’accumulateur de 52 kWh bondit de 410 à 430 km sur le cycle WLTP. Le bonus apparaît un peu timide, mais c’est mieux que rien.
Là où les modifications sont les plus intéressantes, c’est indéniablement sur l’entrée de gamme Five. Cette dernière bénéficiera dans quelques semaines d’une polyvalence bien supérieure. Alors oui, la batterie passera de 40 à 36,5 kWh, ce qui entraînera une autonomie en légère baisse, en diminuant de 310 à 305 km, certes. Mais l’électromoteur, lui, prend des chevaux en sautant de 95 à 110 ch.
Finition Five : la correction majeure que tout le monde attendait
Et le plus pertinent concerne la recharge : en plus du chargeur embarqué AC de 6,6 kW, la R5 Five gagne en série un chargeur DC de 80 kW permettant enfin à la citadine d’aller sur l’autoroute. Certains clients avaient en effet la mauvaise surprise de constater que la charge rapide n’était pas disponible sur leur véhicule devant la borne… Renault semble avoir appris de ses erreurs sur ce point-là.
Il le faudra, car la Volkswagen ID. Polo, qui sera l’une de ses plus grandes concurrentes, intègre la recharge rapide en série. Ce que l’allemande rejette pour le moment est une offre de personnalisation étendue. La R5 en profite donc pour conquérir ce territoire avec les teintes Rouge Flamme et Gris Schiste que nous avons déjà évoquées il y a quelques jours pour le marché allemand.
Look, couleurs et IA : ce qui change à bord
Les jantes de 18 pouces de la finition Techno peuvent revêtir une finition dorée tandis que de nouveaux stickers de toit et d’aile font leur apparition. La sellerie de la version Iconic se veut plus sobre en troquant le jaune pour le bleu. Côté équipement, l’appel d’urgence est compatible avec les réseaux 4G alors que le chargeur de smartphone par induction est désormais ventilé.
Un nouveau mode de conduite Smart issu de la Clio s’invite à la fête. Celui-ci adapte le programme en fonction du style de conduite en basculant automatiquement entre les modes Eco, Confort et Sport. Enfin, l’assistant IA de Gemini permet de fluidifier les interactions entre l’utilisateur et son véhicule. La Renault 5 démarre toujours à 24 990 €, hors prime CEE.

articles.title: Nvidia reportedly acquires AI project hosting platform Hugging Face for $12.9B - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Nvidia reportedly acquires AI project hosting platform Hugging Face for $12.9B
Nvidia Corp. has reportedly bought Hugging Face Inc., a startup with a popular platform for hosting open-source artificial intelligence projects.
Reports that an acquisition was in the cards first leaked on Monday. Business Insider broke the news that Hugging Face had received interest from multiple prospective buyers. On late Wednesday, The Information reported that Nvidia clinched the deal for $12.9 billion. It’s believed the chipmaker joined the fray after Salesforce Inc. expressed takeover interest.
Hugging Face launched in 2016 with a chatbot service for teens. Two years later, it open-sourced a framework for building AI applications. The company launched its flagship product, a GitHub-like platform for hosting open-source AI models, in 2020.
The company currently hosts more than 2 million models. Developers can also access tens of thousands of free training datasets, user-created AI applications called Spaces and other technical assets. Nvidia is among the companies that use Hugging Face to host their open-source AI projects.
The startup generates revenue with a paid version of its platform. Hugging Face Hub, as it’s called, enables software teams to host their projects in private repositories. The offering also provides cybersecurity controls not available in the free version of Hugging Face.
Hugging Face offers a second paid service, Inference Endpoints, that developers can use to host inference workloads. The company says the offering avoids the weeks of work usually involved in setting up AI infrastructure. An autoscaling feature automates the task of adding hardware capacity when a model’s request volume grows.
Hugging Face not only hosts other companies’ open-source AI models but has also developed a few of its own. In 2025, it released a language model with 3 billion parameters that outperformed several similarly sized algorithms. Earlier, it used donated time on a French supercomputer to train an AI called BLOOM with 176 billion parameters.
The acquisition would buy Nvidia a presence in yet another part of the AI stack. More than 13 million developers rely on Hugging Face to access the models and datasets that power their AI applications. Following an acquisition, Nvidia could more closely align the platform’s feature roadmap with its business goals.
The deal could also create more competition for Stripe Inc. Last week, the company acquired AI model marketplace operator OpenRouter Inc. for a reported $7.5 billion. OpenRouter enables developers to access hosted versions of more than 400 AI models via a single interface. Hugging Face offers a similar capability as part of its platform.

articles.title: TikTok enfrenta multa de casi USD 30 millones en Brasil por datos de adolescentes
articles.text:
Brasil impuso a ByteDance, propietaria de TikTok, una multa de 153,7 millones de reales —equivalente a casi 30 millones de dólares— por irregularidades en el tratamiento de datos personales de menores de edad.
La sanción, emitida por la Agencia Nacional de Protección de Datos (ANPD), convierte a esta plataforma en el blanco más reciente de la ofensiva regulatoria que el país sudamericano despliega contra las redes sociales.
PUBLICIDAD
Las medidas que deberá adoptar TikTok
Además del pago de la multa, ByteDance deberá eliminar los datos recopilados de forma irregular y ejecutar un plan de cumplimiento orientado a reforzar la protección de niños y adolescentes dentro de la plataforma.
Entre los cambios operativos exigidos figuran la aplicación automática de configuraciones de privacidad más estrictas a las cuentas de menores de 16 años, el fortalecimiento de las herramientas de supervisión parental y la introducción de filtros de contenido más exigentes.
PUBLICIDAD
La ANPD detectó prácticas contrarias a la Ley General de Protección de Datos (LGPD) en dos modalidades de acceso a TikTok: mediante cuenta registrada y sin necesidad de registro. El organismo concluyó que los mecanismos implementados por la plataforma “no fueron suficientes para impedir, desde el principio, el tratamiento indebido de datos personales de niños y adolescentes”.
Para los usuarios que accedan a TikTok sin crear una cuenta, las medidas son aún más severas. La plataforma deberá suspender toda publicidad en Brasil, limitar los contenidos y restringir el tiempo de uso a 12 horas. Quienes naveguen sin cuenta tampoco podrán publicar contenidos ni ver emisiones en directo.
PUBLICIDAD
Un patrón regulatorio en ascenso
La sanción contra TikTok se inscribe en una serie de decisiones que reflejan el endurecimiento del marco regulatorio digital en Brasil, con foco en la protección de menores. Este mismo mes, la ANPD ordenó a la plataforma Discord suspender las emisiones en directo y las videollamadas, tras la presunta incitación al suicidio de una adolescente durante una retransmisión.
El Congreso brasileño también aprobó legislación que obliga a las plataformas a vincular las cuentas de menores de 16 años con las de sus padres y verificar la edad de los usuarios. El antecedente más contundente de esta postura data de 2024, cuando X —la red social propiedad de Elon Musk— permaneció bloqueada durante 40 días en el país hasta que acató las órdenes del Tribunal Supremo para retirar cuentas acusadas de difundir desinformación.
PUBLICIDAD
Un castigo económico reiterado
La multa brasileña llega días después de que TikTok alcanzara un acuerdo con el Departamento de Justicia de Estados Unidos para pagar 400 millones de dólares como compensación por una demanda que la acusaba de recolectar datos de menores de 13 años sin autorización parental.
El proceso judicial, iniciado en 2024, señalaba que tanto TikTok como su predecesora, Musical.ly, permitían la creación de cuentas por niños de esa edad y no eliminaban los perfiles ni los datos asociados cuando los padres lo solicitaban, en violación de la Ley de Protección de la Privacidad del Menor en Internet.
PUBLICIDAD
El acuerdo establece un pago de 300 millones de dólares de forma inmediata y otros 100 millones una vez que se retire la demanda contra Musical.ly. El Departamento de Justicia calificó la resolución como “una importante victoria para los niños y los padres estadounidenses” y señaló que, desde la presentación de la demanda, TikTok implementó cambios en su estructura de propiedad, gestión y políticas de privacidad.
El caso se enmarcó en un contexto de presión más amplia sobre la plataforma en territorio estadounidense. La Casa Blanca obligó a ByteDance a vender su filial local, con un pago de 10.000 millones de dólares y una participación del 20% sin poder de gestión. Bajo el nuevo esquema, los propietarios estadounidenses de TikTok deben compartir las ganancias generadas en el país con la empresa china.

articles.title: This is GTA 6: an 80-hour story, 3x bigger map than Red Dead 2, and cops that remember your face
articles.text:
TL;DR: Rockstar premiered a 26-minute Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay showcase on Netflix, then opened the floodgates on preview coverage from outlets flown to Rockstar North last month. The game is enormous: a map that's three times the size of Red Dead Redemption 2's, an 80-hour playthrough, more than 600,000 NPC animations, and gameplay design that aims to shift away from consequence-free sandbox chaos. The video hits YouTube tonight.
After three years of trailers and delays, Rockstar finally showed Grand Theft Auto VI actually being played. The unusual 26-minute "Extended Look" premiered on Netflix hours before it landed on YouTube (or watch Rockstar's embed below).
The footage was captured on a base PlayStation 5 and looks amazingly detailed. Alongside it, previews went live from journalists and creators who spent time at Rockstar North last month, and between the two there is more concrete information about GTA 6 than we have had since the game was announced in 2022. Here is what actually matters.
The scale
Co-studio head at Rockstar North, Rob Nelson, gave YouTuber TGG a set of figures during the preview event: the map is roughly twice the size of GTA 5's and three times the size of Red Dead Redemption 2's. Vice City alone is about twice the size of Los Santos. Rockstar maps have never been the biggest in gaming, but they have generally been the most detailed.
 – Synth Potato🥔 (@SynthPotato) August 27, 2026
Nelson also told The New York Times that his own recent playthrough took about 80 hours, covering the main story plus some optional objectives that carry narrative consequences. For reference, Red Dead Redemption 2's story runs roughly 50 to 60 hours. If that holds, GTA 6 is comfortably the longest game Rockstar has shipped.
Crime now has a paper trail
A most substantive change is that GTA 6 wants you to "think like a criminal" rather than a wrecking ball. The wanted system has been rebuilt around information. A crime has to be witnessed by an NPC or picked up by an alarm before police are alerted, and responding officers get a description: your face, your clothes, your vehicle.
The HUD shows separate indicators for which of those details the police actually know. Hollow wanted stars mean they are searching but do not have a description. Shedding heat means invalidating those descriptions. Changing your hairstyle clears your appearance. Putting on sunglasses or a different hat does not – you need a full outfit change, which is why trunk storage for spare clothes is now a functional system.
 – Synth Potato🥔 (@SynthPotato) August 27, 2026
Wearing a mask during the job and taking it off afterward can prevent the police from ever learning your face, even with CCTV present. Ditching a recognized car for another one lowers attention. If the cops know they are chasing a couple, Jason and Lucia can split up to divide the response.
The six-star wanted level is back after GTA 5 capped out at five. Escaping at three stars or higher inside Vice City is reportedly brutal because the streets are narrow and the traffic is dense.
The Criminal Profile
Rockstar's replacement for RDR 2's honor meter is called the Criminal Profile, and the distinction is professional versus sloppy. Nelson says the goal is for the player not to feel overpowered the way they did in previous games. The system can evaluate how you behave as a criminal, for example, robbing a store without killing anybody and escaping cleanly can raises your 'Criminal Profile' because you committed the crime professionally, while excessive violence lowers it.
Other people in Leonida are armed, dangerous and occasionally violent without provocation. You can also incapacitate enemies without killing them, by wounding a limb or shooting the weapon out of their hands.
Stealing cars is a system now, too. You cannot just press a button. Vehicles are sorted into security tiers, and a phone app called WAINK scans a car before you commit, reporting its value, lock status, alarm and whether it has a tracker.
Older cars open with a slim jim, while modern luxury vehicles need key-cloning hardware you unlock through story progression, meaning some cars are simply off-limits early on. Cars with GPS trackers phone your position to the police unless you outrun the signal or dump the vehicle.
Selling happens through specialized fences, Red Dead 2-style, and damaged cars are worth less. Money matters more broadly this time: some story progression requires raising specific amounts of cash first.
The world
Rockstar claims more than 600,000 NPC animations, against roughly 55,000 in GTA 5 and 300,000 in Red Dead Redemption 2. NPCs are individually art-directed rather than assembled procedurally, with a wider spread of body types, and animations scale to fit them.
The phone is now a physical object in the world rather than a HUD overlay. Snapmatic returns as the Instagram parody, but Jason and Lucia cannot post (they are fugitives avoiding a digital trail), so you browse and observe rather than participate. Fast travel is handled by a rideshare app called Ryde Me, and you can hold full conversations with other passengers.
Jason and Lucia's relationship is a genuine variable. They start out interested in each other, but the romance only develops if you invest in it – shopping, working out, exploring, robbing places together. Rockstar says a stronger romance grants no bonuses, which is a more confident design choice than it sounds. The story completes either way.
On the automotive side, the footage showed a convertibles, muscle cars, Japanese tuners straight out of The Fast and the Furious, an actual closed-circuit race with a full field, and dirt bike racing.
The performance question
Rockstar has yet to confirm frame rate targets or performance modes. Content creator Davy Jones, who attended the preview, says the base PS5 build currently runs at 30 fps, and the Extended Look footage appears to be consistent with that. Whether PS5 Pro gets a higher-frame-rate mode remains unknown.
GTA VI launches November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles at $80 for the base game and $100 for the apparently more popular Ultimate Edition. No PC version has been confirmed so far.

articles.title: Uber permite que pais monitorem corridas de adolescentes por vídeo • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Uber permite que pais monitorem corridas de adolescentes por vídeo
Uber Adolescentes terá transmissão ao vivo para pais e responsáveis. Funcionalidade chega a usuários nos EUA.
Uma nova ferramenta no app da Uber permitirá que pais assistam a viagem dos filhos em tempo real. A novidade pretende aumentar a segurança das corridas feitas por adolescentes, enquanto tenta tranquilizar os responsáveis durante o trajeto.
A atualização está em expansão nos Estados Unidos e não tem previsão para aparecer em outros mercados, como o Brasil. Como as contas destinadas a adolescentes na Uber já estão disponíveis por aqui, a funcionalidade pode ser introduzida no futuro.
A funcionalidade entra na lista de recursos de segurança ativados por padrão nas contas para adolescentes, que já incluem o código PIN aleatório, que deve ser apresentado ao motorista antes do início da corrida, e o U-Ajuda, que identifica possíveis situações incomuns durante o trajeto. Diferentemente da gravação de áudio, que pode ser ativada pelo usuário, a transmissão de vídeo dependerá da ativação do recurso nas configurações pelo motorista.
O compartilhamento de vídeo funciona através da câmera de selfie do próprio motorista. Os pais receberão uma notificação avisando a possibilidade de assistir a corrida e, caso aceitem, o motorista e a criança serão informados. A transmissão é encerrada automaticamente no encerramento da corrida.
De acordo com a Uber, apenas o responsável pela conta do adolescente poderá assistir a transmissão da viagem, que é “criptografada”, segundo a empresa.
O site TechCrunch nota, porém, que o serviço não especifica se o vídeo possui criptografia de ponta-a-ponta, que dificulta a intermediação do conteúdo por terceiros.
O perfil monitorado para adolescentes foi lançado em 2023 e traz recursos de segurança para jovens de 12 a 17 anos. A conta permite que os menores tenham uma conta independente na plataforma criada por um responsável através do Perfil Familiar.
Com o perfil vinculado, os pais recebem notificações sempre que o adolescente solicita uma viagem, com informações do trajeto e localização em tempo real.
O Uber Adolescentes começou a ser testado no Brasil no mesmo ano de lançamento nos Estados Unidos e expandiu em 2024. Atualmente, segundo o site do serviço, já está em 129 cidades, incluindo todas as capitais.

articles.title: Glass substrate roadmaps examined — Absolics in final qualification and a first product that keeps slipping
articles.text:
Glass substrate roadmaps examined — Absolics in final qualification and a first product that keeps slipping
Three years on, not much has happened.
Glass-core substrates, the replacement for organic chip packaging that Intel promised in September 2023 with more than $1 billion behind it, are now in final qualification. However, the product is still not in a single commercial product. SKC, a material manufacturer and chemical affiliate of the SK Group, said on its July 27 earnings call that embedded glass substrate samples from its Absolics plant in Covington, Georgia, are undergoing package-level reliability evaluation in Taiwan, with results possible before year-end.
Samsung Electro-Mechanics formalized a 482.1 billion won ($310 million) glass-core joint venture with Sumitomo Chemical's Dongwoo Fine-Chem on July 2, targeting first production in the second half of 2027. Intel, which started the race, has shifted to licensing its patents and showing demo vehicles, with its own deployment now pointed at around 2030. However, and rather predictably, every timeline in the segment has slipped. Absolics originally planned mass production for the first half of 2024, and reported claims that AMD would adopt glass substrates for CPUs between 2025 and 2026 have come and gone unfulfilled.
Why glass?
The technical case for glass core substrates leans heavily on numbers Intel published a while back, such as 10 times the interconnect density of organic substrates and a 50% reduction in pattern distortion. Glass cores can be tuned to a thermal expansion coefficient of roughly 3 to 10 ppm per degree Celsius against silicon's 2.6, which cuts warpage by about half compared with organic cores, and rectangular panels in the emerging 510mm x 515mm format use more than 75% of their area for large die against roughly 50% for round 300mm wafers. Through-glass vias have been demonstrated at six microns in diameter with aspect ratios beyond 15:1 at ECTC 2025, and Georgia Tech has shown stacked glass running at 220 GHz with 0.3 dB of loss.
Glass also chips and cracks at the edges during drilling and dicing, and MIT Technology Review reported in March that early Absolics production runs broke hundreds of panels every couple of days during early testing days. Edge-coating work has cut measured edge stress from 95 MPa to 49 MPa, and low-temperature dielectrics that cure below 180°C have been developed to reduce thermal stress during build-up, but metallizing vias below 10 microns and holding nanometer-scale flatness across half-meter panels remain open manufacturing problems.
Intel's program
Intel demonstrated a working system booting Windows on a glass-core substrate in early 2025, and Rahul Manepalli, Intel's VP of module engineering, told MIT Technology Review that the benefits of glass cores are "undeniable" and that Intel wants "to be one of the first ones who do it." The commercial plan around that engineering has changed shape, however. DigiTimes reported in late July that Intel is in early-stage talks with Chinese cover-glass maker Lens Technology about a packaging partnership, but there has been no solid agreement made to date.
At NEPCON Japan in January, Intel Foundry showed its first thick-core glass substrate with two EMIB bridge dies embedded directly in the glass: a 78mm x 77mm package with two 800-micron-class glass layers, 10 redistribution layers on each side, and around 1,716 mm2 of silicon on top, roughly two full reticles, with no micro-cracking reported in testing.
There’s currently no production time to this, however, with TrendForce placing Intel’s commercialization somewhere around 2030, alongside co-packaged optics prototypes built on glass at its Rio Rancho, New Mexico site. Meanwhile, Amkor, Intel's packaging partner on the optics work, put commercialization within three years at an industry event in Seoul in April.
Korea aiming for 2027
Samsung Electro-Mechanics moved its glass program from advanced R&D into a business-execution unit in February and has been sampling from a pilot line at its Sejong plant since late 2024. The GLASEM joint venture announced on July 2 splits ownership: 66% to Samsung Electro-Mechanics and 34% to Dongwoo Fine-Chem, with site production in Pyeongtaek, and targets an operating plant in the second half of 2027, with the joint venture making the drilled and metallized glass core that feeds Samsung's substrate line. Korean industry reporting says samples have gone to AMD and Broadcom, and also puts Samsung's overall glass maturity at 40 out of 100, a gap between marketing dates and process readiness worth keeping in mind.
Absolics' $600 million plant in Covington, Georgia, backed by $75 million in CHIPS Act funding plus a further $100 million through the government's advanced packaging R&D program with Georgia Tech, has a Phase 1 capacity of 12,000 m2 of substrate per year, enough for roughly two to three million H100-sized packages. The company produced mass-production samples in the first quarter, began customer qualification that reportedly includes AMD and AWS, and is targeting mass production by the end of 2026. LG Innotek runs a third Korean program from its Gumi plant, with prototypes delivered in 2024 and production targeted for 2027 to 2028.
TSMC and Japan
TSMC's CoPoS line in Chiayi, built around 310mm x 310mm rectangular panels, received tools in February, completed its pilot line around June, and is aiming for pilot production in 2027, with mass production in the second half of 2028. Equipment supplier SCHMID has described glass integration in that platform as under review, not committed, and TrendForce puts TSMC's commercial-scale glass-core production after 2030, meaning that the industry's biggest packaging operation is going panel-level first and glass later, if at all. TSMC revived glass substrate research a couple of years ago after earlier deprioritizing it, reportedly under pressure from Nvidia, whose accelerator packages are the main thing outgrowing current packaging.
Japan’s Dai Nippon Printing began phased operation of a TGV glass-core pilot line at its Kuki plant in Saitama in December 2025 on 510mm x 515mm panels, with sample shipments from early 2026 and full mass production targeted for fiscal 2028. Toppan's pilot line for glass cores and interposers at its Ishikawa plant was scheduled for commissioning in July, and Nippon Electric Glass has scaled its ceramic-reinforced GC Core panel to 515mm x 510mm at 1mm thickness. Rapidus is studying panel-level packaging on 600mm x 600mm glass as part of its 2nm program, with viability put at the late 2020s. China has its own entrants, led by display maker BOE, whose pilot line is sampling.
TrendForce estimates Nvidia's Rubin Ultra package at roughly 7,470 mm2, about nine reticles' worth of silicon and memory, against around 2,739 mm2 for Blackwell, and CoWoS interposer wafers cost on the order of $10,000 each, comparable to a processed 7nm wafer.
Organic substrates warp and lose dimensional stability at those sizes, and round interposer wafers waste a growing share of their area, which is what glass panels are meant to fix. SEMI's first dedicated market report on glass cores, published in May with Global Net, projects initial production around 2028 in select high-performance applications and a 67.2% compound annual growth rate from 2028 to 2040, while Yole puts the advanced IC substrate market at $31 billion by 2030 with glass cores among the drivers.
At the moment, no production design exists, and all customers that have been named or otherwise attached to the tech, including AMD, Broadcom, AWS, and Nvidia, come from wider industry reporting. Nothing has been confirmed officially. As for whether we might see more substantial progress next year, Absolics will need to publish some solid package-level reliability results by the end of this year, or a first officially named customer at any of the Korean manufacturers. We also need to hear from TSMC on whether glass cores will go into CoPoS or remain under review into the 2030s.
Luke James is a freelance writer and journalist. Although his background is in legal, he has a personal interest in all things tech, especially hardware and microelectronics, and anything regulatory.

articles.title: 16 things we learned from Grand Theft Auto 6's awesome 'Extended Look' video, based on real PS5 gameplay
articles.text:
16 new GTA 6 details we learned from the big Extended Look gameplay video, captured in-game on a PS5
Rockstar delivered with this awesome showcase
The Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look is finally live! Those tuning in for the Netflix premiere were treated to 26 minutes' worth of new content about the game ahead of its November 19 launch, including huge amounts of gameplay footage, cinematics, and a deeper look into the lives of Jason and Lucia.
If you don't have Netflix, you'll be able to watch on Rockstar's YouTube channel at 9PM ET / 6PM PDT / 2AM BST / 3AM CEST.
There is so much to unpack, from a revamped combat system, interactive gameplay mechanics, story hints, and more — but to make things easier, we've gone ahead and created a breakdown of the top things we learned in case you missed it.
Cinematics and gameplay blend right into each other
The extended look began with Lucia and Jason walking into an apartment block looking to pick up a package for someone named "Boobie." For this mission, it looks like Jason is the playable character as he guides Lucia through the building and encounters some incredibly detailed NPCs.
Here, and in several other instances, the gameplay appears to instantly shift into a cutscene before the action kicks back in again. Another instance happens later on; Jason and Lucia are fleeing from the police with a client, and Jason must shoot at them out the window while Lucia evades — the scene quickly transitions into something cinematic before going back into gameplay.
At the end of the extended look, Lucia and Jason get separated on a mission; as soon as he finishes shooting some guys under player control, it suddenly cuts to a cinematic scene showing him texting with Lucia, which then transitions to her point of view, and the end of the cutscene leads to you controlling her.
There will be quick time events
During a fight scene between Lucia and an enemy at the end of the extended look, the player is prompted with a quick time event, which is surprisingly old-school for this game. But there seems to be a choice in the matter — there are two options on-screen, and in the video she picks up her heel and nails the guy in the face, making a quip based on your choice of button to mash. We get the sense this will appear throughout the game.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
There will be slow-mo with enemy weak zones
Jason can be seen firing his weapon at some enemies and the gameplay suddenly slows down after he uses his his focus meter seen in the top left corner. During this same encounter, an enemy's body becomes highlighted showing red and yellow weak zones for the player — we're assuming red is a killshot and yellow will disarm or disable.
There will be disguises… lots of disguises
There were quite a few moments were we see Jason and Lucia on story missions wearing disguises with new identities when taking on certain clients, such as personal security for a party. The footage showed changing outfits being a mechanic, and we see lots of different hairstyles on Lucia — it seems like it'll be necessary, not just fun.
There's a six-star Wanted system
Unlike GTA 5, which has a five-star Wanted system, GTA 6 will have six stars. What does this mean? Well, it's one higher, isn't it?
The gun handling is better than GTA 5
Picking up and swapping out weapons looks incredibly slick; Jason and Lucia have their own weapons they can pull out on their respective weapon wheels, but they can quickly swipe up downed-enemies' weapons mid combat, too.
You can race cars in an actual track
Driving around Leonida looks amazing, but players will also be able to take part in races on an actual race track, with cars and bikes, if you want a high-speed challenge.
Lots of water activities
Players will be able to drive fanboats, jetskis and canoes, and explore bodies of water across Leonida. Admittedly, the fanboat looks a little less high-octane than some sections of the video…
You can base jump
As shot near the end of the extended look shows the player guiding Lucia to run and jump off a skyscaper before pulling out her parachute and getting an incredible view of Vice City.
Environmental destruction
During police chases, Jason and Lucia can shoot out the tires of their pursuers, which will lead to police cars flipping and crashing, causing dynamic environmental destruction that looks incredibly cinematic.
A wide range of people will hire you for jobs
While we don't know specific story details yet, it seems that Jason and Lucia have their own business going on where they'll work for an assortment of clients. They'll rob banks and stores, protect clients, deliver goods, and more. Standard GTA stuff, but it's the first time we've seen what this will look like.
You can pet the dog
It's the main thing some of us care about.
An improved HUD
The game's HUD looks way cleaner than GTA 5's, and quicker to access; switching between Lucia and Jason is as quick as pressing one button, and the weapon wheel is minimal and fast to use.
Switching between Lucia and Jason is really fast
As I just mentioned, switching between both co-protagonsits is unbelieavably fast. In one moment, you see Lucia base jumping and when the player switches to Jason, it takes just a couple of seconds — there's flash, the camera zooms into the sky, pans across the city, then zooms down into a building and we're with Jason again. And that's running on the base PS5!
You can scuba dive (and regular dive)
Players will be able to dive into bodies of water to swim, but also scuba dive to see all the pretty fish below the surface!
The weapon icon from GTA 4 returns
During combat, the equipped weapon icon from GTA 4, can be seen in the top right corner, under the Wanted stars and ammo. It was missing in 5, but 4 stans will feel a warm, familiar feeling.

articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (August 28, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Friday, August 28, 2026.
From Flipkart and Meesho riding the Rakhi wave to developments in the EV sector, YourStory brings you today’s headlines and the latest news across sectors.
Latest news
Ola Electric launches S1Z, deliveries to begin in December
Ola Electric has launched its new electric scooter, the S1Z, at a starting price of Rs 79,999. The company said it has opened bookings for the scooter and deliveries is expected to begin in December.
Bhavish Aggarwal, Chairman and Managing Director of Ola Electric, announced the launch on X, "As India's electrification ramps, today we’re setting a new benchmark for the industry. More than just a metal body with a fancy name."
Ather share price up 7% after Hero MotoCorp increases stake
The shares of electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy rose by over 7% on Friday in response to the news about Hero MotoCorp increasing its stake in the company.
Ather Energy's share price was trading at Rs 1603.10 on Friday, at the time of writing this article, against Thursday’s close of Rs 1495.30.
Meesho sees 36% rise in Rakhi orders as non-metro India drives festive shopping
Ecommerce platform Meesho recorded a 36% year-on-year growth in orders during the Raksha Bandhan shopping season, with consumers in non-metro markets accounting for nearly three-fourths of the platform’s festive orders.
Meesho said its gross merchandise value grew 38% compared with the corresponding Rakhi shopping cycle last year. Non-metro India accounted for around 73% of all Rakhi orders, highlighting the growing contribution of smaller towns to festive ecommerce.
Flipkart Minutes sees 3X festive shopping spike during Raksha Bandhan
Quick-commerce platform Flipkart Minutes says it has recorded a threefold increase in festive shopping during Raksha Bandhan this year, reflecting a growing shift towards digital channels for last-minute gifting.
According to the company, Gen Z shoppers accounted for more than 40% of customers during the festive period. Rakhi were the fastest-growing category, registering 20X growth, while maang tikkas recorded 4X growth. Other popular categories were precious earrings, gold and silver coins and bars, and pooja thaali sets.

articles.title: GTA 6 en Netflix: Rockstar muestra gameplay detallado con misiones, historia y personajes
articles.text:
La espera parece más corta tras conocer finalmente los detalles de lo que viviremos en GTA 6. El juego de Rockstar reveló gran parte de su jugabilidad e historia a través de un tráiler publicado en Netflix.
Después de una espera de 13 años, los fans de la saga de Grand Theft Auto tendrán una nueva entrega el próximo 19 de noviembre en PlayStation 5 Xbox Series X|S, con un juego mucho más ambicioso con mayores interacciones con los NPC (personajes no jugables), cambios entre los dos protagonistas en tiempo real y un alto nivel de personalización.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué mostró GTA 6 en Netflix
Durante los 26 minutos que dura el tráiler, Rockstar nos mostró diferentes momentos del juego. El primer impacto es el alto nivel de detalle visual, con animaciones fluidas, iluminación y las reacciones de los personajes.
En el video también destacaron la fuerte relación que tendrán los dos personajes principales, Jason y Lucía, tanto en su relación de pareja como en su trabajo en equipo para realizar asaltos y su diferentes misiones. Aunque también hubo énfasis en lo que cada podrá hacer por separado.
PUBLICIDAD
En lo relacionado con la jugabilidad, vimos el funcionamiento del sistema de disparos, en el que hay bases de lo que fue Max Payne 3 y el peso de las armas de Red Dead Redemption 2, diferente a lo que muchos criticaron de GTA 5 por la falta de precisión.
El cambio de personajes también se siente fluido como en la última entrega, en el que cada uno está haciendo cosas diferentes por el mapa. Aunque también habrá momentos para cambiar con ellos en medio de las misiones.
PUBLICIDAD
Otro punto interesante son las referencias satíricas a la realidad actual, como el funcionamiento del a publicidad excesiva, las redes sociales y la televisión. Un sistema que clave será la alimentación y el ejercicio, así que vimos cómo es posible elegir la comida y otros aspectos externos a las misiones con actividades ajenas como carreras y combates.
Un cambio clave a nivel narrativo será el manejo de la relación de Jason y Lucía, ya que en las anteriores entregas nunca hubo una historia romántica y aquí ese será un punto clave, al ser dos personajes con una química marcada, pero en medio de diferentes situaciones como la posibilidad de ser los encargados de la seguridad de la presidente de una compañía.
PUBLICIDAD
Más detalles de cómo será el mundo de GTA 6
Además del contenido de Netflix, Rockstar le dio acceso a la revista Dozed al juego de manera anticipada, por lo que tenemos más novedades de la jugabilidad.
Por primera vez, portar armas a la vista genera reacciones inmediatas: los NPC muestran miedo, huyen o avisan a la policía, que responderá con mayor rapidez ante amenazas. La narrativa gira en torno a Jason Duval y Lucía Caminos, una dupla inspirada en “Bonnie y Clyde”, cuyas decisiones y relación afectan el desarrollo de la historia y las interacciones con el entorno.
PUBLICIDAD
El mundo abierto de Vice City y el estado de Leonida destaca por su diversidad cultural y social. El equipo de Rockstar realizó investigación con exdelincuentes, policías y habitantes locales, logrando un ecosistema urbano creíble. La variedad de NPCs, estilos y productos refleja la vida real de Miami y alrededores.
La personalización física vuelve ampliada: alimentación, ejercicio y hábitos alteran el aspecto y las capacidades de los protagonistas, incluso su percepción por otros personajes. El cansancio, el estrés y los excesos dejan marcas visibles en Jason y Lucía, impactando la jugabilidad y la narrativa.
PUBLICIDAD
Dónde ver el tráiler de GTA 6
Aunque Netflix tuvo la exclusividad de esta mirada extendida, Rockstar confirmó que el contenido se podrá ver en otros plataformas seis horas después de la publicación en la aplicación de streaming.
Por lo que el tráiler extendido de GTA 6 también estará disponible en YouTube y en la página oficial del juego desde cualquier parte del mundo desde las las 9:00 p.m. (ET), 10:00 p.m. de Argentina y 7:00 p.m. de México

articles.title: Carburant : que signifie cette nouvelle mention apparue sur les pompes à essence ?
articles.text:
Depuis le jeudi 27 août, certaines pompes à essence affichent une information inédite pour les automobilistes. Un arrêté publié au Journal officiel la veille impose une nouvelle mention obligatoire, directement visible au moment de faire le plein.
Une mention obligatoire pour les additifs métalliques
Publié au Journal officiel le 26 août, le texte touche le gazole, mais aussi les essences E5 et E10 (vendues à la pompe sous les noms SP95-E5, SP98 et SP95-E10). Il s’applique dès le lendemain de sa parution.
Pour les automobilistes, difficile de rater le changement une fois à la pompe : dès lors qu’un supercarburant sans plomb contient des additifs métalliques, l’appareil de distribution doit désormais l’indiquer noir sur blanc, de façon « visible et lisible ». La mention à repérer : « Contient des additifs métalliques. »
Une limite chiffrée sur le manganèse
Au-delà de cette mention, le texte fixe une teneur maximale en manganèse de 2 mg par litre, ce qui concerne les supercarburants sans plomb (là encore, le SP95-E5, le SP95-E10 et le SP98). Plusieurs autres paramètres techniques des carburants sont également actualisés dans la foulée, sans changement visible pour l’automobiliste cette fois.
Le gazole concerné aussi, mais en coulisses
Le texte va au-delà de cette seule mention à la pompe. Il adapte la réglementation française aux normes européennes NF EN 590 pour le gazole et NF EN 228 pour l’essence sans plomb, toutes deux mises à jour par le Comité européen de normalisation en juillet 2025. Trois arrêtés distincts, relatifs au gazole et aux essences E5 et E10, sont ainsi modifiés en même temps.
Pour le gazole spécifiquement, une nouvelle exigence porte sur le nombre de particules autorisées au point de certification, plafonné à 10 000 particules d’au moins 4 micromètres. Cette limite ne s’applique toutefois qu’au moment où le carburant est certifié, pas aux étapes suivantes de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, une précision qui vise avant tout les metteurs sur le marché plutôt que les automobilistes eux-mêmes.
Au final, pour le grand public, l’essentiel du changement se résume à cette phrase susceptible d’apparaître sur certaines pompes dans les prochains jours ou semaines : « Contient des additifs métalliques. »

articles.title: Windows 11 : à raconter n’importe quoi sur la RAM, Microsoft crée de la frustration et des déchets électroniques en masse
articles.text:
Windows 11 : à raconter n’importe quoi sur la RAM, Microsoft crée de la frustration et des déchets électroniques en masse
En pleine crise de la RAM, Microsoft ne cesse de changer son positionnement sur la quantité de mémoire vive minimum pour faire tourner Windows 11 sans peine. Au risque de créer des problèmes très concrets pour celles et ceux qui ont économisé pour s’acheter une nouvelle machine.
4, 8, 16 ou 32 Go ? Selon l’endroit et l’instant auquel vous demandez à Microsoft, chacune de ces configurations en mémoire vive est la plus appropriée pour faire tourner Windows 11 correctement. Comme tout le monde, l’entreprise est bousculée par la crise de la mémoire provoquée par le boum de l’IA et obligée de s’adapter. Mais du fait de sa position un peu particulière sur le marché, la firme de Redmond à une responsabilité plus importante que les autres dans ce grand micmac.
En effet, Windows est le système d’exploitation le plus répandu au monde sur les PC grand public. Résultat, quand Microsoft se sent morveux, c’est l’industrie toute entière qui se mouche. De plus, la firme est également l’une des plus actives dans le financement du secteur de l’IA, qui siphonne justement toutes les barrettes de RAM disponibles sur le marché.
Autrement dit, l’entreprise a la main à la fois sur le poison et le remède et distribue en parallèle des conseils contradictoires pour gérer au mieux la situation. Et au milieu de tout ça, les consommateurs et consommatrices se retrouvent à devoir faire des choix qui ne sont bons ni pour leur portefeuille ni pour la planète.
Un grand flou
Rembobinons un instant. Au moment de la présentation de Windows 11, Microsoft avait indiqué que 4 Go de RAM était le minimum absolu pour faire tourner le nouvel OS. L’entreprise avait aussi égrené une longue liste de prérequis assez stricte qui prenait déjà le risque de créer des millions de tonnes de déchets électroniques. Ces 4 Go minimum sont toujours d’actualité, mais, au fil des mises à jour, il est apparu évident que cela ne suffisait pas pour assurer une expérience fluide.
Est intervenue ensuite la drôle de danse de Microsoft sur le sujet. 8 Go de RAM était alors largement considéré comme un seuil minimum, mais l’entreprise poussait les machines 16 Go pour profiter de l’expérience "Copilot+" et a même brièvement conseillé de s’équiper de 32 Go de RAM pour jouer "sans se poser de questions".
Sauf que la pénurie est passée par là entre-temps et que le prix de la mémoire vive a quadruplé, obligeant Microsoft à faire preuve d’humilité et à assurer que 8 Go était suffisant pour "une expérience fluide et réactive pour les tâches de tous les jours". Point de mention des configurations avec 4 Go au passage, ces dernières ont, semble-t-elle, été abandonnées en rase campagne.
Le spectre Copilot+
Quiconque a tenté d’opérer une transition entre Windows 10 et Windows 11 ces dernières années avait donc de quoi y voir flou. Au moment de la fin programmée de Windows 10 en 2025, Microsoft poussait toute sa clientèle à embrasser le monde de l’IA avec un PC Copilot+ (encourageant ouvertement les personnes équipées de PC non compatible à racheter de machines neuves). Après tout, c’était la moindre des choses, puisque Windows allait devenir un OS "agentique" et que tel était le sens de l’histoire.
Un an plus tard, celles et ceux qui ont abandonné leurs machines avec 8 Go de RAM ont de quoi se sentir légèrement floué face au changement de braquet de Microsoft. Surtout qu’entre temps, l’entreprise a repoussé non pas une, mais deux fois la fin du support logiciel de Windows 10 grâce à la mobilisation de la société civile. Que ce soit du point de vue logiciel ou matériel, cette transition a donc provoqué pas mal de casse.
Une imprévisibilité qui coûte chère
De la casse symbolique d’abord, dans la confiance accordée à Microsoft pour opérer cette transition proprement. Mais aussi de la casse proprement matérielle aussi, puisque l’abandon des anciennes machines pas éligible à la mise à jour représente déjà "58 millions de tonnes de CO2" émis et "26 000 tours Eiffel de matière première" mise au rebut. Ajoutez à ça les machines perçues comme obsolètes à cause de ce cafouillage et vous obtenez une montagne de PC inutilement abandonnés.
Enfin, et ce n’est pas négligeable, elle a aussi provoqué de la casse économique. Sans même compter les plus précaires qui ne peuvent tout simplement pas s’acheter de machines Windows 11, celles et ceux qui ont cru bon de changer de PC pour coller aux recommandations plus ou moins officielles de Microsoft ont aisément déboursé plusieurs centaines dans l’opération. Tout ça pour que Microsoft se décide finalement à faire le nécessaire pour faire tourner Windows 11 correctement sur les machines avec 8 Go de RAM.
Certes, Windows 10 n’a pas été officiellement mis au rebut, certes, la nouvelle version de l’OS peut techniquement tourner sur des PC avec 4 Go de RAM. Mais les décisions tardives de Microsoft sur ces problématiques ont sans doute déjà poussé de nombreuses personnes à changer de PC alors qu’elle n’en avait pas nécessairement besoin. Vendre un avenir rendu inaccessible par ses propres agissements relève soit d’une impréparation critique, soit d’un cynisme certain.

articles.title: DDN, Solidigm and Supermicro on joint AI storage solution - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
The AI storage stack gets an inference-era rethink
Artificial intelligence is changing what storage and data management platforms look like.
In collaboration with Super Micro Computer Inc. and Solidigm, DataDirect Networks Inc. has introduced DDN Enterprise AI HyperPOD, built on Nvidia Corp.’s AI Data Platform. The goal is to simplify the storage, scaling and deployment of AI inference for enterprise workloads.
“Customers are preferring best of breed, but that can often result in complexity,” said Andrew Murphy (pictured, right), senior director of product management at DDN. “The question is how can we help to offload that complexity from our customers so they can focus on what’s most important, which is taking their data that they’ve been generating over the years … [and] add context so that it can be ready for their AI factories.”
Murphy, alongside Michael Ang (left), director of storage solutions at Supermicro, and Pompey Nagra (center), products and ecosystems lead at Solidigm, spoke with theCUBE’s Rob Strechay for the Supermicro Open Storage Summit interview series, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed the collaboration and new trends in enterprise AI. (* Disclosure below.)
One unified storage solution
While customers traditionally buy individual storage, networking and compute platforms and build their own solutions, that strategy often takes far too long, according to Ang. The better method, he argues, is to have one unified solution that enables organizations to start monetizing their data immediately.
“The number one challenge is [customers] still have the mindset of having to buy individual — compute, storage, networking — and put it together, but that takes a long time,” Ang said. “In order to help them be successful in this area, the customer should focus on how do they get the right solutions with the right platforms such that … they can start utilizing it and start doing the AI workloads.”
The HyperPOD collaboration can employ different types of flash memory to meet different AI tasks, Nagra added. Because solid-state drives reuse AI workloads without the need for recomputation, customers get more utilization out of their graphic processing units.
“We see the platforms change from being compute bound to storage bound, where LLMs need more data to more storage to enable the [key-value] cache data,” Nagra said. “The SSD storage becomes a great value as it’s capacity bound versus the [high-bandwidth memory] or primary memory, which requires greater amounts of recomputation for the same workload.”
DDN worked closely with the Nvidia AI Data Platform reference design to offer a turnkey solution that reduces complexity for customers and can be deployed on premises, giving organizations greater control over security, governance and data residency. The technology also supports multi-tenancy, which means that multiple teams can share compute, networking and storage but keep their environments separate.
“Most of the time the GPUs are sitting there idle, waiting for the data,” Murphy said. “That’s really what we’re focused on from a DDN perspective … how do we make sure that we provide a fast path to fully utilize GPUs so that way customers can get the most out of their investments, they can get the most out of their data to further their initiatives.”
Sovereign AI puts data control in focus
Companies and government organizations are increasingly seeking private or sovereign AI solutions, according to the panel. Nvidia’s secure reference design offers that privacy and security, while still giving customers the opportunity to be flexible with how they handle their data.
“If you take a look at organizations, they’ve always wanted to have control of their data, the IP, most importantly their costs,” Nagra said. “Being able to control all these elements enables greater flexibility … and at the end of the day, lets them live in their governance that they’ve orchestrated, whether it be on prem with the platforms provided by DDN and Supermicro, as well as in hybrid environments.”
In addition to offering environmental flexibility, HyperPOD can also scale up as necessary, which minimizes cost exposure. Rather than having to commit to large numbers of expensive GPUs, customers can try out the solution with one rack and then add more when needed.
“We are able to design this complete AI data platform solution that allows the customer to expand from small, medium, large,” Ang said. “Meaning they can continue to run the business when they see there’s a need for additional GPUs and storage utilizations. They can just pop in another rack next to it, connect the network cables, power it on, then continue online and serve customers.”
Stay tuned for the complete video interview, part of SiliconANGLE’s and theCUBE’s coverage of the Supermicro Open Storage Summit interview series.

articles.title: Plaud Unveils Plaud One Explorer Edition, the Wearable AI Earbuds Built for the Agent Era
articles.text:
Thursday, August 27th 2026
	
	
	
	
Plaud Unveils Plaud One Explorer Edition, the Wearable AI Earbuds Built for the Agent Era
Plaud today unveiled the Plaud One Explorer Edition for professionals ready to put a new human-AI interface to work. Every era of computing has had a defining interface. We typed on keyboards. We tapped on screens. Yet today's AI remains separated from the place where human intent is formed: conversation. The agent era needs an interface that is natural to humans, rich in context, and always ready. In the agent era, just speak.
Plaud One is the first expression of that interface. It captures the live conversation, understands intent in real time, and acts across your tools proactively. Plaud One pairs advanced hardware with its latest Plaud Intelligence platform to capture, understand, act, and compound human intelligence.The Post Screen Era Interface
Human work starts with conversation. Every great idea, decision, and shared meaning begins in conversation. We use our senses to listen, speak, see, think, and remember. But we also forget and get distracted. For generations, we've adapted to interfaces, not the other way around. We scatter our work behind screens.
In the AI era, conversation becomes the interface. Plaud builds the wearable interface between humans and agents. It captures the upstream, lossless, source-of-truth conversational context—becoming the system of record for the agent era. Then it turns understanding into action; it proactively initiates, executes, and gets things done.
Designed to Capture, Understand, Act, and Compound Human Intelligence
Worn as earbuds or used through its standalone case, Plaud One captures calls, online meetings, in-person conversations, and ideas on the go.
Built-in eSIM with 4G LTE connectivity keeps Plaud One connected without relying on a phone, automatically uploading conversations for transcription and summarization as work happens. This creates an always-current context layer that agents can use to connect decisions across meetings, prepare follow-ups, generate reports, and take action across connected tools—so users can stay focused and present.
Plaud One runs on Plaud Intelligence, the conversation intelligence platform built to capture, understand, and execute on human intent. The redesigned platform goes further than before, bringing deeper memory, persistent context, and real workflow execution to every interaction.
At its center is Plaud Agent, which understands the context and intent behind your conversations, then acts on them end to end.
Nathan Xu, CEO and Co-founder of Plaud"AI agents become truly useful when they understand the context in which human intent is formed," "That context lives in conversation. Plaud One brings agents closer to the real-world work people do every day, while Plaud Intelligence gives them the context and capabilities to act. We are opening the Explorer Edition because interfaces are proven in the field, and shaped by the people who put them to work."
These new Plaud Intelligence capabilities will become available across all Plaud products through the Plaud App 4.0 update. The update will introduce a completely redesigned interface, providing seamless navigation across Plaud Intelligence features.
Designed for People Whose Work Lives in Conversation
A sales leader can walk out of a client meeting and ask Plaud One to draft the follow-up before the next meeting starts.
An executive can ask for a briefing on the last conversation with a client while walking into the room. A consultant can turn a workshop into a findings report.
A chief of staff can set a Monday routine that reviews the prior week's conversations and sends a structured briefing before the day begins.
Availability
The Plaud One Explorer Edition is priced at US$249.99 and is available to pre-order in selected markets at 9am EDT, 27th Aug, 2026.
Plaud One works out of the box, and Plaud's existing plans work with Plaud One the same way they do across Plaud devices today. Each Explorer Edition includes US$200 in Plaud Credits, which power Plaud Intelligence's upcoming agent capabilities and other AI features.
Shipments are expected to begin in Q4 2026, Plaud App 4.0 will begin rolling out across all Plaud products in Q4.

Plaud One works out of the box, and Plaud's existing plans work with Plaud One the same way they do across Plaud devices today. Each Explorer Edition includes US$200 in Plaud Credits, which power Plaud Intelligence's upcoming agent capabilities and other AI features.
Shipments are expected to begin in Q4 2026, Plaud App 4.0 will begin rolling out across all Plaud products in Q4.

articles.title: Starlink homologa antena menor e mais leve para uso no Brasil • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Starlink homologa antena menor e mais leve para uso no Brasil
SpaceX teve a antena do kit Starlink V5 para internet via satélite aprovado pela Anatel. Novidade indica lançamento iminente no Brasil.
Em julho deste ano, a SpaceX anunciou o kit Starlink V5, que inclui uma antena muito mais leve e menor em relação ao kit atual, o Starlink V4. À época, não ficou claro quando e se o novo kit chegaria ao Brasil. Mas, recentemente, a nova antena passou por homologação na Anatel, o que sugere que a sua disponibilidade no mercado brasileiro está próxima.
Na documentação que o Tecnoblog obteve junto à Anatel, a nova antena é identificada como UTA-262. Até o momento, não há nenhum documento público da Starlink que associa esse nome à nova antena. Porém, ao fazer unboxing do kit Starlink V5, o youtuber Jesse Nowlin encontrou justamente o código “UTA-262” na traseira do dispositivo (a partir de 6:20 no vídeo).
Levemos em conta também que as fotos do produto na homologação condizem com as imagens divulgadas pela SpaceX.
Começa pelas dimensões, que tornam a antena do kit Starlink V5 quase 50% menor em relação ao kit Starlink V4. Como mostra a tabela comparativa a seguir, o peso também diminuiu sensivelmente. Esses fatores devem facilitar o transporte e a instalação da antena:
|  | Starlink V5 | Starlink V4 | 
|---|---|---|
| Dimensões | 384 x 306 x 34 mm | 594 x 383 x 39,7 mm | 
| Peso | 1,1 kg | 2,9 kg | 
| Consumo | 35-50 W | 75-100 W | 
| Download | +375 Mb/s | +400 Mb/s | 
A tabela deixa claro ainda que o consumo de energia da nova antena diminuiu praticamente pela metade. Por outro lado, a taxa de download máximo caiu em 25 Mb/s (megabits por segundo) no kit Starlink V5, mas essa é uma diferença tão pequena que, provavelmente, não será notada pelos usuários.
Só não está claro quando a Starlink começará a oferecer a nova antena no mercado brasileiro. Mas, como a homologação na Anatel já foi concluída e é um passo essencial para isso, eu apostaria em novidades ainda para 2026.

articles.title: Authorities arrest 2 alleged members of prolific hacking group TeamPCP
articles.text:
Authorities in Australia said Wednesday that they arrested two men accused of participating in cybercrimes for TeamPCP, a prolific group of hackers that, over nine months, has carried out a relentless series of supply-chain attacks that infected more than 1,000 organizations worldwide.
In a statement, the Australian Federal Police said the two men were arrested and charged with 14 offenses. The statement said the men were members of TeamPCP, which by the authorities’ count, compromised more than 1,000 organizations worldwide. The statement didn’t identify the men, except to say they lived in the Western Australian towns of Cottesloe and Mandurah. KrebsOnSecurity, citing a lengthy investigation, provided what it reports to be both defendants’ names, along with an extensive background of their lives and the mistakes that led to their downfall.
The hacks that keep on hacking
TeamPCP has vexed law enforcement officials and security personnel around the world since it emerged in December. The group is best known for a sustained series of supply-chain attacks that laced open source software with malware that self-propagated from one package to another. The viral infections worked by targeting organizations’ CI/CD pipelines, which are used to rapidly develop, update, and deploy software.
Once a package or tool was compromised, Shai-Hulud, as the worm was dubbed, attached itself to future package updates. When developers downloaded the compromised packages and ran them through their own CI/CD platforms, their software was also compromised.

articles.title: Nvidia expects to sell $20 billion of Vera Rubin systems in Q3 as shipments begin — figure would account for 20% of its data center revenue mix, marks fastest ramp in company history
articles.text:
Nvidia expects to sell $20 billion of Vera Rubin systems in Q3 as shipments begin — figure would account for 20% of its data center revenue mix, marks fastest ramp in company history
20% of data center revenue.
Nvidia expects sales of the Vera Rubin platform to account for around 20% of its data center revenue in the third quarter of its fiscal year 2027, which will make it the company's fastest-ramping data center product in history. As Nvidia projects its revenue to be around $108 billion in Q3 FY2027, sales of Vera Rubin hardware alone will total around $20 billion in just one quarter.
"We see Vera Rubin accounting for about 20% of data center revenue in Q3," said Colette Kress, chief financial officer at Nvidia, during the company's earnings conference call with financial analysts and investors. "Having already received purchase orders from every major hyperscaler, AI cloud, and system OEM, we expect Vera Rubin to mark the fastest product ramp in Nvidia's history."
Data center revenue has accounted for around 92% of Nvidia's quarterly sales in recent quarters, so as long as Nvidia meets its $108 billion earnings projection in Q3, its data center revenue will reach around $99.36 billion, meaning that sales of its Vera Rubin platform hardware will be around $19.872 billion.
Nvidia began to ramp up production of Vera Rubin components — that include Vera CPUs, Rubin GPUs, BlueField 4 DPUs, and other units — this spring and commenced first revenue shipments of actual VR200 NVL72 racks in August, with Microsoft being the first to deploy commercial systems (at least according to Satya Nadella).
Normally, companies ramp up production and sales of their data center platforms for several quarters. Ramping up a data center platform from effectively no production revenue in Q2 FY2027 to 20% of revenue ($20 billion in this case) in just one quarter is a record not only for Nvidia, but perhaps for the whole industry, given Nvidia's scale. However, there is a catch: actual unit shipments do not look truly breakthrough.
Exact volumes of Vera Rubin units that Nvidia plans to ship in the third quarter of its fiscal 2027 are unknown. However, if Nvidia ships only VR200 NVL72 rack-scale systems, depending on their actual price and configuration (estimated from $5 million to $7.8 million per unit), Nvidia will supply from roughly 2,550 to approximately 3,975 machines containing 91,700 – 143,100 Vera CPUs as well as 183,500 – 286,100 Rubin GPUs.
These numbers are, of course, very rough since the company will sell a boatload of MGX servers and even Vera CPUs and Rubin GPUs separately, meaning that actual unit shipment volumes of these key components will be higher. Nonetheless, we are still talking about hundreds of thousands, rather than millions, of CPUs and GPUs, which is not particularly many. Still, given the stellar prices of leading-edge AI hardware, even relatively limited volumes of these components can generate tens of billions of dollars in revenue.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.
