articles.title: Amazon is shutting down Mechanical Turk after more than 20 years
articles.text:
Bots Matter: A new alert warns that Amazon Mechanical Turk will cease to exist a month from now. Amazon has not provided a specific reason for the change, but Mechanical Turk has been steadily losing ground to newer competitors and AI-based platforms.
After being in the crowdsourcing market for more than two decades, Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk) will permanently shut down on September 30, 2026. Amazon said it regularly evaluates its tools, programs, and services, and MTurk is clearly being left behind as other ventures have emerged as AI-focused training initiatives.
Amazon Mechanical Turk originally launched in 2005, providing a platform for companies to hire remote workers – known as Turkers – to perform menial, on-demand tasks. Operated under the Amazon Web Services brand and inspired by the original Mechanical Turk machine, MTurk offered Turkers a way to earn a few dollars per week by validating or tagging data, moderating content, answering surveys, and more.
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos once called MTurk the "artificial artificial intelligence" service, referring to the platform's ability to outsource tasks that computers found difficult to perform compared with humans. Over time, MTurk grew enough to "employ" more than 500,000 remote Turkers from over 190 countries. However, according to the data-worker advocacy group Turkopticon, the platform has been in decline for years.
In recent years, MTurk has faced competition from modern alternatives such as Scale AI, Mercor, and Prolific. These companies recruit workers to help train large AI models. A 2023 study questioned the quality of data coming from MTurk, highlighting how a significant number of Turkers (46 percent) were using generative AI and chatbots to complete the platform's tasks.
MTurk has also been criticized for how the platform exploited human labor. Computer scientist Jaron Lanier said that the service was designed to turn people into software components for larger business initiatives. MTurk was known for attracting people in precarious economic conditions, leaving them with little bargaining power in the event of billing disputes.
In fact, Amazon started winding down MTurk last month by no longer accepting new customers. Now, the latest message clearly explains that Turkers and companies will soon be unable to access the platform. The company has also prepared an FAQ explaining how workers can resolve their remaining billing issues with the platform.

articles.title: Rocket Report: Europe splashes some cash on launch startups; Pallas-1 nears debut
articles.text:
Welcome to Edition 9.08 of the Rocket Report! Some major news this week from the state of Louisiana, previously associated with space due to NASA’s aging Michoud Assembly Facility near New Orleans. Now the state has a chance to become the epicenter of SpaceX’s Starship program as the company plans to invest up to $100 billion to construct factories and multiple launch pads for the super heavy lift rocket. It would utterly transform coastal Louisiana.
As always, we welcome reader submissions, and if you don’t want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar.
ESA announces big launch challenge contracts. The European Space Agency said Thursday it signed contracts with a handful of European launch startups to help them continue development of their vehicles. “The European Launcher Challenge is ESA’s initiative to expand European launch service supply and ensure more robustness in Europe’s access to space,” the space agency said of the award, which supports the development and operation of small launch vehicles in Europe. For some of these firms, the funding will provide a key lifeline.
And the winners are … Rocket Factory Augsburg, based in Germany and developing the RFA One rocket, received 186.9 million euros and is mainly funded by Germany, with a contribution by the United Kingdom. PLD Space, based in Spain and developing the Miura 5 rocket, received 158.9 million euros and is mainly funded by Spain with a contribution by Germany. Isar Aerospace, based in Germany and developing the Spectrum launcher, received 197.8 million euros and is mainly funded by Germany, with contributions by Austria and Norway. Another contract award process with MaiaSpace is nearing completion, the agency said.
Skyroot is great, but India needs more. Jatan Mehta writes some of the most insightful articles about India’s space program, and we wanted to highlight his six-part series on what he calls “India’s launch vehicle crisis.” Part six of this series was published on Sunday, and it explains why, despite the recent success of Skyroot and its Vikram-1 rocket, India’s growing gap in orbital launch capacity will remain unresolved. “Even if we hope and assume that the thousand-plus people of Skyroot bag a commendable place in the small-lift launch market, that does not in itself solve India’s space access crisis,” Mehta writes.
India’s government needs to be proactive … He notes that the country faces major constraints in spaceports, suppliers, and especially medium- and heavy-lift rockets. “Skyroot’s success with the first flight of Vikram-1 is only the least worst case scenario for India’s launch vehicle crisis,” Mehta says. “It’s not at the peak alongside people’s emotions but at the bare minimum level to cater to but a fraction of India’s needs in space.”
The Ars Technica Rocket Report
The easiest way to keep up with Eric Berger’s and Stephen Clark’s reporting on all things space is to sign up for our newsletter. We’ll collect their stories and deliver them straight to your inbox.
Japanese startup wins launch contract. A Japanese radar-imaging startup has signed an agreement to launch its first demonstration satellite on Space One’s Kairos rocket, Space News reports. Space One and Sarmony announced on August 25 that they signed a memorandum of understanding regarding the launch of Sarmony’s first SAR DiskSat spacecraft on a Kairos rocket in 2028.
A bold choice … Kairos has launched three times to date, in each case failing to reach orbit. On the most recent launch in March, the vehicle broke apart a little more than a minute after liftoff. A Space One representative said the company is completing the investigation into the failure and plans to release more details soon. The company has not announced a schedule for the next Kairos launch.
Falcon 9 Starlink launches from Florida end. It’s the end of an era in Florida, Ars reports. A Falcon 9 launch early Tuesday was the last planned Starlink mission from Cape Canaveral until SpaceX begins flying Starship missions from Florida, according to Kiko Dontchev, the company’s vice president of launch. “From here on, Starlink missions out of Florida will fly on Starship,” Dontchev said. “The West Coast team will continue regularly launching Starlink from Vandenberg.”
A real workhorse … SpaceX launched around 260 Starlink missions on Falcon 9 from Florida, but all future Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy launches from Florida will carry external customer payloads. The next one is scheduled for August 30, when a Falcon Heavy rocket will lift off from Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy Space Center with NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Officials eventually plan to phase out the Falcon 9 in favor of Starship, at least for commercial missions, raising concerns among SpaceX customers about the availability of reliable launch services after 2028.
Pallas-1 rocket nears debut. Chinese commercial firm Galactic Energy is ready for a first orbital launch attempt with its Pallas-1 liquid propellant launch vehicle, Space News reports. Newly published airspace warnings now indicate a launch window of between 9:52 pm ET on August 31 and 12:09 am ET on September 1 (01:52–04:09 UTC, September 1). While the rocket is designed for reusability, no recovery attempt of the first stage is expected for the first flight. No payloads have so far been announced ahead of launch.
Solidly a medium-lift vehicle … Pallas-1 is Galactic Energy’s two-stage liquid launch vehicle, with an optional Eros upper stage for extended missions. It has a 3.35 meter-diameter body, a 4.2 meter-diameter fairing, a liftoff mass of 283 tons, and liftoff thrust of 350 tons, according to Galactic Energy’s webpages. While payload capacity stats have fluctuated during development, the firm states a maximum payload capacity of 7,000 kilograms to low-Earth orbit.
New federal policy calls for additional spaceports. A new national space transportation policy signed by President Donald Trump calls for the development of more spaceports to support more than 1,000 launches and reentries per year by 2030, Ars reports. The most notable updates to the national space transportation policy focus on increasing the country’s ability to enable those lofty forecasts. The Trump administration calls on the Pentagon and NASA to “prioritize and coordinate on infrastructure investments” to boost launch and reentry capacity and flexibility at federal launch and reentry ranges.
Finding additional launch facilities … The policy document supports more efficient range scheduling criteria at federally owned spaceports, balancing the needs of commercial users and US government missions. It also directs the military and NASA to “regularly publish range schedules to ensure transparent allocation of resources and optimize launch capacity.” Today, the schedules for most rocket launches are not public until a few days or weeks in advance. The government will also identify potential locations for additional launch facilities in the United States, improve integration of space launch and reentry operations into airspace and air traffic control modernization efforts, and designate “priority airspace for critical space launch corridors.”
Ariane 6 set for first geostationary launch. On Thursday, Arianespace is scheduled to launch the MTG-I2 meteorological satellite with the Ariane 62 configuration from Europe’s Spaceport in French Guiana. According to Arianespace, the MTG-I2 mission will mark the fourth Ariane 6 launch of the year and the rocket’s first to a geostationary orbit.
Flying high, for now … In addition to these milestones, this will be the ninth overall launch by the Ariane 6 program, which was developed by the European Space Agency and is now operated by Arianespace. From a technical standpoint, Europe’s workhorse rocket continues to perform well, but there are questions about its long-term viability.
SpaceX plans massive Starship launch site in Louisiana. Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry said Tuesday that SpaceX will commit $100 billion to develop Starship factories and launch pads in the state’s coastal areas. In doing so, the company seeks to replicate the Starbase facility it has built over the last decade in southern Texas on a larger scale, Ars reports. Gwynne Shotwell, the president and chief operating officer of SpaceX, said the “Starbase Louisiana” facility would become a self-sustaining spaceport with propellant production, power generation, deep-water shipping capabilities, vehicle processing facilities, and an airport on site.
It will be much larger in scale … The Starbase Texas site encompasses only about 350 acres, and SpaceX also must maintain public access to Boca Chica Beach as much as possible along a single roadway. By contrast, SpaceX is expected to have unfettered access to about 125,000 acres in southern Louisiana, in an area generally referred to as Pecan Island. SpaceX plans to begin construction of the first launch facilities in 2027 and is targeting an initial launch from Louisiana by 2029. Eventually, the company may build as many as a dozen Starship launch towers at the location.
China delays key lunar launch. China’s “Manned Space” program issued a terse announcement on Sunday regarding its much-anticipated Chang’e 7 lunar exploration mission, Ars reports. The agency stated: “In keeping with the principle of proceeding prudently and reliably, and ensuring absolute success, after a comprehensive assessment it has been determined that the Chang’e 7 mission does not meet the conditions for launch and therefore cannot be carried out during the planned launch window this year.”
A key step in the race back to the Moon … Consisting of a lunar orbiter, lander, rover, and a mini-hopper probe, the mission was due to launch as early as Sunday on a Long March 5 rocket. It is intended to land at the south pole of the Moon. Although official Chinese sources have provided no confirmed information, there has been social media chatter indicating that another suitable launch window may not open until next February or March. Why so long? It’s likely a combination of factors, including sunlight conditions in polar landing zones and the mission plan, which requires a 90-day lunar orbit reconnaissance before landing.
Nearly time for Roman to fly. NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope arrived Tuesday at the SpaceX hangar at Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, just days before its scheduled liftoff on a Falcon Heavy rocket, the US space agency said. NASA, Roman, and SpaceX teams will host a Launch Readiness Review on Friday to conduct the final “go/no go” poll ahead of the planned 7:26 am ET launch on August 30, from Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy.
A far-seeing instrument … Launching nine months ahead of schedule, Roman is expected to transform the way we see the Universe and settle essential questions about some of the biggest mysteries out there. Roman has a wide field of view that will rapidly capture huge swaths of sky full of stars and galaxies once it reaches the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point 2, or L2.
Next three launches
August 27: Ariane 6 | MTG-I2 | Guiana Space Centre, French Guiana | 20:10 UTC
August 30: Falcon Heavy | Roman Space Telescope | Kennedy Space Center, Florida | 11:25 UTC
August 31: Electron | Own Around the World | Māhia Peninsula, New Zealand | 12:05 UTC
Eric Berger is the senior space editor at Ars Technica, covering everything from astronomy to private space to NASA policy, and author of two books: Liftoff, about the rise of SpaceX; and Reentry, on the development of the Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon. A certified meteorologist, Eric lives in Houston.

articles.title: Flipkart Minutes cashes in on last-minute festive shopping, sees 3X spike during Raksha Bandhan
articles.text:
Flipkart Minutes cashes in on last-minute festive shopping, sees 3X spike during Raksha Bandhan
Gen Z shopper accounted for 40% of customers during the festive period. Rakhis, maang tikkas, precious earrings, gold and silver coins and bars, and pooja thaali sets were the popular categories on the quick-commerce platform.
Quick-commerce platform Flipkart Minutes says it has recorded a threefold increase in festive shopping during Raksha Bandhan this year, reflecting a growing shift towards digital channels for last-minute gifting.
According to the company, Gen Z shoppers accounted for more than 40% of customers during the festive period. Rakhi were the fastest-growing category, registering 20X growth, while maang tikkas recorded 4X growth. Other popular categories were precious earrings, gold and silver coins and bars, and pooja thaali sets.
The festive shopping momentum was visible across both major cities and smaller markets, the company said. Among metros, Ahmedabad, Mumbai and Kolkata witnessed good demand, while Aurangabad, Madurai and Nawada were the key non-metro markets.
Flipkart Minutes’ dedicated 'Rakhi Store' served consumers making last-minute purchases. The platform sold more than 2,000 rakhis every minute during the period, according to Flipkart. Mobile handsets, true wireless earbuds, gold coin bars, and smartwatches were among the leading gifting categories.
In the run-up to Raksha Bandhan, shopping peaked between 4 pm and 10 pm yesterday, while mobile phones recorded the highest number of gifting orders in a single hour.
Consumer preferences also extended beyond traditional Raksha Bandhan gifts. Accessories such as fashion brooches, mobile tripods, and watch combos recorded 3.5X growth. Searches for traditional sweets, including besan laddus and rasmalai, as well as chocolates and personalised Rakhi gift hampers, also gained traction.
Ethnic wear emerged as another strong last-minute category, with orders for men’s kurtas rising 87% year-on-year during this period.
These trends highlight the growing role of quick commerce in catering to both planned purchases and eleventh-hour gifting needs, as consumers combine traditional celebrations with personalised gifting.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Amazon Ring annonce une « mise à jour de sécurité majeure » pour ses sonnettes connectées
articles.text:
Ring a annoncé le déploiement d’une nouvelle norme en matière de chiffrement vidéo baptisée TAKE. Afin de proposer certaines fonctionnalités IA, TAKE crée une clé temporaire de chiffrement pour accéder à une vidéo et la supprime dans la foulée. Inévitablement, cette nouvelle norme soulève une question de confidentialité. Dans la foulée, Ring a annoncé deux nouvelles fonctionnalités IA pour les utilisateurs français.
Ring va introduire une nouvelle norme de confidentialité… au détriment du chiffrement ?
Pour l’instant, les vidéos enregistrées par les caméras Ring (Amazon) sont chiffrées lorsqu’elles transitent vers le cloud et lorsqu’elles y sont stockées. Ce système permet un haut niveau de confidentialité, mais présente dans le même temps certaines limites : lorsque le chiffrement de bout en bout (E2EE) est activé, Ring n’a pas accès aux vidéos pour exécuter certaines fonctionnalités IA. Pour contourner ce blocage, Ring va prochainement déployer une nouvelle norme en matière de chiffrement vidéo baptisée TAKE (Throw Away the Key Encryption), que l’on peut traduire littéralement par « Jeter la clé de chiffrement ». Concrètement, pour pouvoir proposer certaines fonctionnalités IA, Ring doit pouvoir déchiffrer les vidéos. Pour y parvenir, une clé de chiffrement temporaire est créée, puis supprimée sitôt la fonctionnalité IA exécutée. Ring assure ainsi que cette clé de déchiffrement est temporaire et rapidement supprimée.
La norme TAKE sera déployée progressivement pour tous les utilisateurs Ring à partir de septembre. À noter que le chiffrement de bout en bout classique (l’E2EE) restera en option. Dès lors, ceux qui désactiveront la norme TAKE perdront l’accès à certaines fonctionnalités IA. Ceux qui garderont la norme TAKE pourront en bénéficier, mais ils devront accepter que le chiffrement de bout en bout ne soit plus maintenu pendant certaines opérations, même si Ring promet une clé temporaire rapidement supprimée. Maintenir une confidentialité totale ou profiter de certaines fonctionnalités IA : tel est le dilemme.
Deux nouvelles fonctionnalités IA pour les utilisateurs français
Dans la foulée, Ring a annoncé avoir étendu deux fonctionnalités IA au marché français. Celles-ci sont disponibles « en fonction des abonnements souscrits ». La première permet de bénéficier de descriptions textuelles de vidéos lorsqu’un mouvement est détecté. Ainsi, une notification fait état d’un événement, ce qui permet à l’utilisateur de ne pas ouvrir l’application. La seconde fonctionnalité IA est capable de regrouper plusieurs événements semblables en une seule notification. Ainsi, si des feuilles bougent, l’application Ring vous enverra une seule notification, et non dix.

articles.title: Runable raises $21M to realize small businesses' growth vision using AI agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Runable raises $21M to realize small businesses’ growth vision using AI agents
Runable Inc., a platform that uses artificial intelligence to help businesses build, run and grow, announced Wednesday that it has raised $21 million in early-stage funding to scale its operations and reach more enterprise outfits.
Susquehanna Venture Capital and Nexus Venture Partners co-led the Series A funding round, alongside continued support from existing investors Together Fund and Array VC.
Founded in 2025, Runable uses AI agents to form what it calls a single platform to help build and grow business operations. Its platform shares context and memory across tasks, assists with shipping products, works across surfaces – including websites, mobile and internal apps – and builds pitch decks and marketing videos. Users can also use it to quickly spin up applications with auth and payments.
Once live, it supports day-to-day operations and growth by running paid advertising campaigns across ChatGPT Ads, Meta, Google, LinkedIn and TikTok. It works with users to generate a schedule for social content, cold email contacts, direct messaging and voice calls. It also tracks competition and brand sentiment, with an eye for search engine optimization, the emerging field of answer engine optimization, and overall customer support.
“Building software stopped being the hard part,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Umesh Kumar. “Nobody starts a business because they want a landing page. They start it because they want customers and revenue. Software creation got automated. Everything after it didn’t. That’s what Runable is for.”
The company calls itself “the operating system for small business,” and aligns itself not as yet another website/app builder but as something that can adapt and grow as business needs change and expand.
Runable is betting that generative AI is at the center of the revolution for taking what small business executives know about their own industry and turning it into operational growth. In an era where AI is making starting a business as easy as writing a prompt, organizing that into a working framework where people, operations, customer outreach and marketing all live is the gap the company wants to close.
From the outset, the company’s platform offers something people already know: a chatbot-like interface similar to ChatGPT. Business executives describe what they need and Runable does the work. It builds landing pages, internal apps, mobile apps, pitch decks, market analysis, prospect lists and so on.
Where Runable wants to make its bone is in growth. That’s where the paid ads happen – no ad account needed – the platform grows plans, launches and manages ad campaigns with little to no prior knowledge required. It also grows and builds the company’s brand across social media, including Instagram, LinkedIn, X and TikTok, by creating content, scheduling it and posting based on what the company’s market slice is interested in.
The company believes this is where AI can sit: a layer that reduces operational toil and combines automation with industry and marketing data to scale presence.
Runable noted that most of its 1.5 million users are small business owners with only two people in the agency, consultancy or company. Its platform currently assists customers worldwide, including the United States, United Kingdom, Japan and Brazil.
The company said it will use the new funding to expand its growth capabilities across more channels, with deeper measurement and campaign management that agents can automate on their own. It’s also hiring within its engineering, machine learning, growth and support teams.
“There are millions of small businesses outgunned by companies with bigger teams and bigger budgets. Not better ideas,” Kumar added. “We think that’s a tooling problem, and we think it’s solvable.”

articles.title: Many talks between data center developers and local governments are wrapped in secrecy behind non-disclosure agreements — residents question the need for NDAs, but developers argue it’s important to avoid ‘running afoul of insider trading rules’
articles.text:
Many talks between data center developers and local governments are wrapped in secrecy behind non-disclosure agreements — residents question the need for NDAs, but developers argue it’s important to avoid ‘running afoul of insider trading rules’
People have the right to know.
Researchers from the University of Mary Washington in Virginia found that of the 31 localities with an existing, approved, or proposed data center, 25 of them have non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) that make it difficult, if not impossible, for their citizens to find information about these projects. According to NPR, these NDAs have left the questions of many residents unanswered, making them feel left out of the decision process and increasing their distrust of their leaders.
Many officials defended signing these secrecy agreements, saying that this is standard practice among tech companies, and that they could lose the potential business and revenue that data center projects could bring to their jurisdiction if they fail to sign the NDA. Louisiana Economic Development Secretary Susan Bourgeois even told the publications that NDAs are “fundamental for economic development” as they allow the state to compete with other states and territories for the data centers’ business. “The last thing that they want to have happened in the beginning of the discussion, or in any part of the discussion, is for their information that they’re sharing to be disclosed publicly. So, without NDAs, our work, frankly, just doesn’t happen,” the agency secretary said to NPR. She also added, “The irony is that we, we use NDAs not to be more cloaked, we use NDAs to be more forthcoming.”
NDAs aren’t only limited to Louisiana, as other towns across the U.S. have signed these secrecy agreements even before they started talks with potential data center projects in their regions. Some Wisconsin citizens raised a similar issue in early 2026, when at least four municipalities reportedly signed NDAs with Microsoft and Meta as they negotiated with the two companies. These confidentiality agreements are some of the things that drive the heated debate between elected officials and ordinary citizens, with the latter often feeling betrayed and sold out by the former when they belatedly find out that a data center will be put up in their community.
However, West Feliciana Parish proved that it could get a data center deal without keeping its details top secret. Parish President Kenny Havard said that economic development does not require NDAs. “I don’t think NDAs are necessary unless they’re going to bring you in a room and share some proprietary information. When you’re talking about land sales, tax incentives, those sorts of things that affect the citizens, it should be out in the open. It should be transparent,” Havard told the outlet. He also said, “We’re proud that we did it without having to sign NDAs. And I think it just shows that you can do these projects without keeping the people in the dark.”

articles.title: Nvidia posts another record quarter, predicts explosive AI-driven growth will last through 2028
articles.text:
The takeaway: Nvidia this week reported blockbuster results for the quarter ending in July 2026 and issued ambitious revenue guidance that topped Wall Street consensus estimates. The company's stock jumped more than 7% in early trading on Thursday after Nvidia confirmed that it expects demand for high-end AI accelerators to remain strong in the near future.
According to Nvidia's official filing with the SEC, quarterly revenue for the three-month period ending in July 2026 reached $96.22 billion, beating the $91.90 billion expected by Wall Street. Net income more than doubled to $53.95 billion, up from $24.76 billion in the previous quarter. Adjusted earnings came in at $2.22 per share, higher than the $2.08 expected by analysts.
In the current quarter, Nvidia expects revenue to reach around $108 billion. The projection is largely in line with analyst estimates, with most banks and brokerage firms forecasting sales between $105.2 billion and $110 billion. In fiscal 2028, the company expects revenue to grow by around 70%, significantly higher than the 45% projected by analysts.
Speaking to reporters during a post-earnings conference call, Nvidia CFO Colette Kress claimed that demand for AI accelerators is seeing an uptick among data center customers, despite warnings from many institutional investors about a potential AI bubble. "Customers' forecasts point to our growth doubling next year," she added.
During the same conference call, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang noted that the company's next-generation AI accelerator, codenamed Vera Rubin, is now in production. The so-called AI "Superchip" was officially unveiled at CES 2026 in Las Vegas in January after being showcased at the company's GPU Technology Conference (GTC) in Washington last October.
The ambitious projections and assurances from Nvidia's top executives regarding continued demand for AI hardware appear to have eased some investor concerns about a potential AI bubble. However, uncertainties remain over the supply constraints faced by Nvidia's main contract manufacturer, TSMC, as well as the rising cost of high-bandwidth memory.
Nvidia made its name as a GPU designer for gaming PCs and professional workstations, but its recent pivot to AI chips has propelled its market capitalization to more than $5 trillion. The company is now preparing to expand its AI hardware business beyond data centers and into the consumer market by teaming up with Perplexity to launch the "Portable Computer" AI agent, which is designed to run locally on PCs and workstations.

articles.title: Samsung apresenta monitor gamer Odyssey de 1.100 Hz • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Samsung apresenta monitor gamer Odyssey de 1.100 Hz
Empresa revelou novos monitores da linha Odyssey, com opções de frequência maiores e combinações para diferentes tipo de jogo.
Resumo
- A Samsung apresentou o monitor gamer Odyssey G6 de 27 polegadas com taxa de atualização de 1.100 Hz.
- O Odyssey OLED G9 de 49 polegadas tem resolução DQHD e taxa de atualização de até 720 Hz, com tecnologia QD-OLED e brilho de 1.300 nits.
- Os monitores Odyssey OLED G8 e G7 também foram atualizados com novas versões.
A Samsung levou à feira de jogos eletrônicos Gamescom a próxima geração de monitores Odyssey, focando principalmente em altas taxas de atualização e tempos de resposta baixos. O destaque fica por conta do Odyssey G6 (G60H), de 27 polegadas, que chega a 1.100 Hz no modo Full HD.
O modelo supera os 1.040 Hz demonstrados pela empresa na CES 2026 e mais que dobra a frequência de 500 Hz da versão anterior, lançada no ano passado.
Além dele, a empresa apresentou novos monitores Odyssey OLED para 2027, incluindo versões ultrawide com diferentes combinações de resolução e frequência. A Samsung ainda não divulgou os preços nem a data de lançamento dos modelos.
Vale lembrar que altas taxas de atualização e baixos tempos de resposta estão entre as especificações mais procuradas pelo público gamer, especialmente em jogos competitivos. Na semana passada, a Samsung Display apresentou painéis OLED QHD e 4K com suporte a até 300 Hz de taxa de atualização durante a exposição IMID 2026.
Odyssey G6 ultrapassa os 1.000 Hz
O novo G6 usa um painel IPS de 27 polegadas, resolução nativa Quad HD (2560 x 1440) e tempo de resposta de 1 ms. A taxa de 1.100 Hz, porém, só está disponível quando a resolução é reduzida para Full HD. Ela é voltada a jogos competitivos, em que a fluidez tem prioridade.
Ao usar todo o potencial de resolução do painel, a taxa de atualização cai para 600 Hz, número ainda muito superior ao padrão atingido em monitores gamers nos últimos anos, entre 120 Hz e 240 Hz. A
Samsung ainda não informou o preço, mas afirma que o Odyssey G6 chegará ao mercado até o fim desse ano e deve concorrer com LG UltraGear 25G590B, um monitor Full HD de 24,5 polegadas que também promete 1.000 Hz de velocidade.
OLD G9 chega a 49 polegadas e 360 Hz
O maior modelo da nova linha é o Odyssey OLED G9 (G95SJ), com tela de 49 polegadas e proporção ultrawide. Ele é primeiro com esses números com resolução DQHD e taxa de atualização de 360 Hz, segundo a Samsung, chegando a até 720 Hz.
O Painel do Odyssey OLED G9 usa tecnologia QD-OLED, tem resolução de 5120 x 1440 pixels e mantém o tempo de resposta da versão anterior, de 0,03 ms, além de pico de brilho de 1.300 nits.
Assim como o novo G6, o modo de operação com a maior taxa de atualização exige uma resolução menor, aqui, cai para HD (2560 x 720). A geração anterior do Odyssey OLED G9 de 49 polegadas chegou ao Brasil custando R$ 11.999.
OLED G8 e Odyssey G7 ganham novas versões
O Odyssey OLED G8 de 32 polegadas também receberá uma nova versão com três combinações diferentes de resolução e frequência:
- UHD (4K): 360 Hz
- QHD: 520 Hz
- FHD: 680 Hz.
O monitor usa painel QD-OLED de quinta geração, tempo de resposta de 0,03 ms e também traz recursos voltados à redução de reflexos. Ele inclui uma conexão USB-C com carregamento de até 98 W. Lembrando que a fabricante lançou no Brasil, neste mês, o Odyssey G8 6K, que chega a uma taxa de atualização de 330 Hz derrubando a resolução pela metade.
Já na sequência da linha, a Samsung resolveu não trazer grandes mudanças nas tecnologias de exibição. O Odyssey OLED G7 seguirá com resolução 4K e taxa de atualização de 165 Hz, mas numa tela maior: sai das 37 polegadas do modelo anterior, lançado em janeiro no Brasil, para 42 polegadas.

articles.title: Anthropic's new hardware standard lets AI agents control the physical world
articles.text:
For all the interest in and uptake of agentic AI systems over the past year or so, the world of automated AI has thus far been primarily limited to text, images, code, and other data and actions that take place inside a computer. Anthropic is now aiming to change that somewhat with what it’s calling the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a set of standardized drivers designed to let AI agents easily interface with and control arbitrary devices.
For now, the “research preview” of the MHS effort is being sold mainly as a way to help scientists streamline the arduous process of creating the custom software integrations that are often needed to get disparate components of an experiment working in concert. MHS can provide a common interface and common format for data sharing between these devices, Anthropic says, allowing them to talk to each other across a network “without needing a bespoke ‘translator’ program in between.” The standardized system could reduce weeks or months of exacting experimental setup down to “hours or minutes,” Anthropic writes.
In a video posted alongside the announcement, Anthropic Technical Staffer Alek Kemeny says the MHS effort was inspired by observing neuroscientist Arco Bast work through an experiment on memory formation in the brain at the HHMI Janelia Research Campus in Ashburn, Virginia. Kemeny said Bast had worked out an interface to get the rotating laser beams, microscopes, cameras, and myriad other components of the experiment to coordinate through a common interface. “This idea could be used to have AI run any science experiment in the world,” Kemeny recalls thinking at the time.
Your new robotic lab assistant?
There’s nothing about a common machine interface language that requires the use of AI models, of course. And Anthropic says MHS devices can be controlled directly in real time via command-line prompts and API code files. But integrating an MHS system with an AI model through the Model Context Protocol lets scientists interact with devices using natural language, and lets models “reason through each step in an experiment, update parameters in real time, and, in some cases, recover from hardware errors without intervention,” Anthropic writes.

articles.title: Microsoft "Resolves" Windows 11 Crashing Games with a Registry Hack
articles.text:
Thursday, August 27th 2026
	
		
	
	
	
Microsoft "Resolves" Windows 11 Crashing Games with a Registry Hack
Late last week, we reported that the Windows 11 August update was causing gameplay issues such as forced crashes, random freezing, errors, and unexpected device restarts. The company investigated the problem and discovered that the interaction between games and RGB peripherals was the root cause. They released a workaround involving a registry hack and marked the issue as resolved, even though no proper update was provided. Microsoft has pointed to the existence of RGB peripherals as problematic, shifting the blame to these devices and stating that the only solution is to block the inpoutx64 driver from loading, rather than offering a complete fix.
MicrosoftThis issue is resolved by a block that prevents the inpoutx64 driver from loading. The block targets devices with this specific driver enabled and the game ARC Raiders installed. This resolution disables the inpoutx64 driver and displays a message window with information about the disablement. Following this message, the game will launch as normal.
As a workaround, the company recommends disabling the driver through the Windows registry:
		
		Source:
				Microsoft			
	
	
	
		
	
		
MicrosoftThis issue is resolved by a block that prevents the inpoutx64 driver from loading. The block targets devices with this specific driver enabled and the game ARC Raiders installed. This resolution disables the inpoutx64 driver and displays a message window with information about the disablement. Following this message, the game will launch as normal.
- Navigate to the key HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\inpoutx64. This can be done using the folders on the left side of the window, or by typing the path into the address bar at the top of the window.
- On the right side of the window, find the registry value named Start. Double-click this key and enter the number 4 in the field titled Value data.
- Close the window and restart your computer.

articles.title: New EPA proposal could give states more control over pollution status
articles.text:
New EPA rules mean polluting US data centers can now keep their output secret from neighbors
President Trump backs America's data center expansion
- EPA wants states to decide whether residents receive pollution permit notices
- Data centers could face less public scrutiny under the proposed changes
- Minor pollution permits would no longer require federally mandated public notice
A newly proposed rule from the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) would eliminate federal requirements for public notice on many minor pollution permits.
The change specifically concerns so-called minor New Source Review permits issued under the Clean Air Act framework across the country.
Critics argue the shift could let power-hungry data centers avoid scrutiny while running on-site gas turbines near residential neighbourhoods.
State regulators would gain control over public notice
Under the proposal, state and local air quality authorities would decide whether communities are told about new pollution sources.
This would replace a long-standing federal requirement that mandated advance disclosure and public comment periods for minor-source industrial air permits.
EPA says the change would reduce administrative burdens while allowing authorities closer to affected communities to decide appropriate public participation requirements.
The agency also says existing pollution standards would remain applicable, meaning the proposal does not itself remove emission limits.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
However, the Environmental Protection Network (EPN), a group formed by former EPA employees, has formally opposed this proposed rule change in public comments.
“By eliminating the long-standing federal requirement for public notice, this proposal continues efforts by the current administration to turn its back on the fundamental EPA principle of transparency,” said Mike Koerber, a former deputy director of EPA’s Office of Air Quality Planning and Standards.
He argued that the change shows a wider retreat from the agency's own transparency commitments made publicly earlier this year.
EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin said "the public must be able to trust our work," and he called for “the fullest possible public participation in our decision making.”
Nevertheless, critics claim that the new proposal directly contradicts that same memorandum's earlier promise to maximize citizen input in all agency decisions.
Data center pollution debate intensifies amid AI boom
This debate arrives as data center construction accelerates rapidly nationwide, driven largely by demand tied to artificial intelligence development.
Developers often choose on-site gas turbines for power instead of waiting years for traditional utility grid connections to become available.
These turbines can emit nitrogen oxides along with several other pollutants, raising real air quality concerns among residents living near new facilities.
A recent Gallup survey found that more than 70% of Americans would oppose a similar facility near their own home.
Despite that opposition, the Trump administration has continued backing data center expansion, with Trump linking the industry to lower taxes.
“Taxes are going to go way down because this is a tremendous source of income,” said President Donald Trump.
He made those remarks after criticizing a decision by Texas officials to temporarily halt new approvals letting data centers connect to the power grid.
The EPA did not immediately respond to a detailed request for comment regarding the proposed changes described in this report.
Administrator Zeldin, however, reiterated that authorities closer to each region are better suited to judge local water, air, and electricity conditions.

articles.title: Meesho sees 36% rise in Rakhi orders as non-metro India drives festive shopping
articles.text:
Meesho sees 36% rise in Rakhi orders as non-metro India drives festive shopping
Non-metro locations accounted for 73% of all Rakhi orders this season for Meesho.
Ecommerce platform Meesho recorded a 36% year-on-year growth in orders during the Raksha Bandhan shopping season, with consumers in non-metro markets accounting for nearly three-fourths of the platform’s festive orders.
Meesho said its gross merchandise value (GMV) grew 38% compared with the corresponding Rakhi shopping cycle last year. Non-metro India accounted for around 73% of all Rakhi orders, highlighting the growing contribution of smaller towns to festive e-commerce.
The fastest growth came from Tier III and Tier IV markets. Dadri in Uttar Pradesh led the growth with a 105% year-on-year increase in orders, followed by Nabarangapur in Odisha, Kasganj, Dhamtari and Nainpur in Madhya Pradesh.
The trend points to the increasing adoption of online shopping beyond India’s major cities, as consumers in smaller towns turn to ecommerce platforms for festive purchases.
Payment behaviour also showed a shift during the season. Around 58% of Rakhi orders on Meesho were placed through prepaid payment modes, suggesting growing customer comfort with digital transactions on the platform.
The festive season also attracted more sellers to the marketplace. The number of sellers offering Rakhi-related products on Meesho increased 72% year-on-year. The company said small businesses and entrepreneurs used the occasion to expand their product catalogues and reach customers across the country.
While traditional products remained central to Rakhi shopping, personalisation emerged as another important trend. A bracelet-style Rakhi set bundled with greeting cards was the season’s best-selling product. At the same time, demand for personalised name Rakhis increased sharply, reflecting consumers’ growing preference for customised gifts.
The Rakhi shopping trends underline the expanding role of ecommerce in India’s smaller markets, with rising order volumes, greater seller participation and increasing adoption of prepaid payments strengthening the festive shopping ecosystem.

articles.title: El gasto en la App Store ha caído en EEUU por primera vez. No es dinero desaparecido, es dinero que ha dejado de pasar por Apple
articles.text:
El gasto de los clientes estadounidenses de la App Store ha caído un 6% interanual en el segundo trimestre, según los datos que Sensor Tower ha compartido con el Financial Times. Es la primera caída en diez años. No porque hace diez años ya hubiese otra caída, sino porque es cuando empezaron estos registros.
En el resto del mundo la tienda sigue creciendo, aunque al 3% frente al 13% de hace un año.
En cifras. Tres fuentes distintas, midiendo cosas distintas, apuntan hacia lo mismo:
- -6% en gasto de los usuarios estadounidenses en el segundo trimestre (Sensor Tower), frente al +9% de un año antes.
- -18% en los ingresos por comisión de Apple en Estados Unidos desde enero (Appfigures), con caídas también en Brasil y Japón tras sus nuevas regulaciones.
- -0,6% en ingresos netos de la App Store a nivel mundial hasta mediados de agosto (Morgan Stanley).
Entre líneas. Ese 18% no mide cuánto gastan los usuarios, sino cuánto se queda Apple. Desde abril de 2025, la sentencia del caso Epic obliga a permitir que las aplicaciones enlacen a pagos externos en Estados Unidos, sin comisión.
Cuando alguien paga una suscripción de una aplicación desde el navegador en vez de hacerlo dentro de la aplicación, ese dinero sigue existiendo, pero desaparece de los ingresos de Apple y de los paneles de Sensor Tower. La propia Apple lo ha admitido ante la SEC: esas transacciones "pueden no ser elegibles para comisión". Parte de la caída es demanda que se ha enfriado, y parte es dinero que se ha ido del radar.
El otro factor. Los juegos han dejado de tirar del carro tanto como antaño: sus ingresos caen un 4,5% global. Los juegos son la categoría que ha sostenido una gran parte de la tienda durante muchos años. El resto crece cerca de un 15%, pero casi todo viene de las aplicaciones de IA generativa (+108%), donde ChatGPT concentra el 60% de los ingresos.
Una tienda con más de dos millones de aplicaciones ahora mismo depende de que una sola siga vendiendo suscripciones para seguir creciendo.
El contraste. Esto ocurre en el momento de mayor abundancia de su historia. Con Claude Code y herramientas similares, publicar una aplicación se ha vuelto muchísimo más sencillo que antes, así que se ha disparado la cantidad de propuestas en la App Store. Las descargas, sin embargo, no suben al mismo ritmo.
Lo que está llegando son sobre todo clones y wrappers de IA, aplicaciones construidas para existir más que para usarse. Nadie paga por la enésima y es difícil ser realmente diferencial. Posiblemente haya más valor en la posibilidad de crear pequeños productos muy personalizados que en seguir inundando las tiendas de aplicaciones sin nada que aporte algo realmente nuevo o distinto.
Sí, pero. No es que Apple esté en problemas: cerró el segundo trimestre del año con 109.400 millones de dólares en ingresos, un 16% más, y el iPhone creciendo un 22%. Lo que se erosiona es el margen. Las comisiones del 15% al 30% son la parte más rentable de Servicios, y la valoración actual de Apple descansa en buena parte sobre lo mucho que ha crecido Servicios.
Y ahora qué. Europa lleva dos años por delante en esto y el resultado ha sido el contrario.
- La DMA obligó a Apple a abrir la App Store antes que ningún tribunal estadounidense.
- En abril de 2025 le costó una multa de 500 millones de euros por impedir que las aplicaciones informasen de precios mejores fuera de la tienda.
- El mismo día en que el FT publicaba estos datos, Apple anunciaba su nuevo esquema de comisiones para la Unión Europea, en vigor desde el 1 de octubre.
La diferencia con Estados Unidos está en el porcentaje, no en el principio: un desarrollador español que saque al usuario a pagar en su web seguirá dejando un 15% a Apple, y un 5% si distribuye la app fuera de la tienda. En Estados Unidos, en ese mismo escenario, Apple no cobra nada.
Ahí está la explicación de por qué la caída aparece en las cuentas estadounidenses y no en las europeas. Bruselas ha forzado a Apple a competir; el juzgado de California le ha quitado la comisión.

articles.title: Windows 11 : oublier d'éteindre son PC ne sera bientôt plus un problème grâce à votre smartphone
articles.text:
Oublier d’éteindre son PC avant de partir travailler, ou se rappeler en plein trajet qu’une mise à jour Windows attend d’être installée : ce genre de désagrément pourrait bientôt appartenir au passé. Du code repéré dans l’application Android Lien avec Windows laisse entrevoir une fonctionnalité inédite, encore invisible pour le grand public.
Des commandes cachées dans le code, pas encore actives
En fouillant dans le paquet d’installation de l’application, des chaînes de texte inutilisées font référence à un composant baptisé RemoteControlManager. Un indicateur technique daté du 25 août 2026, isRemotePcControlsV2Enabled, reste réglé sur « désactivé », preuve que la fonction existe bel et bien dans le code, mais n’a été activée pour personne, pas même pour les testeurs habituels.
Cinq commandes se dessinent à travers ces chaînes de texte. Deux libellés visent le redémarrage et l’extinction pure et simple du PC. Deux autres, plus surprenants, associent ces actions à une mise à jour Windows : « Mettre à jour et redémarrer » et « Mettre à jour et éteindre ». De quoi transformer ces boutons en véritables outils de gestion plutôt qu’en simples interrupteurs à distance.
Une mise en veille avec un vrai piège
Une option de mise en veille complète le tableau, assortie d’un avertissement sans équivoque : une fois endormi, le PC coupe sa connexion réseau, impossible de le réveiller à distance, il faudra revenir physiquement devant la machine. Un détail qui distingue clairement cette fonction du simple verrouillage à distance déjà disponible.
Les scénarios impliquant une mise à jour en cours affichent, eux, un message plus appuyé encore : tout travail non sauvegardé dans les applications ouvertes serait définitivement perdu, sans possibilité de le récupérer à distance depuis le téléphone.
Une avance sur Apple, pour l’instant
Microsoft avait déjà ouvert la voie fin 2025 avec le verrouillage à distance du PC depuis un smartphone Android. Cette nouvelle étape irait nettement plus loin. À titre de comparaison, Apple ne propose actuellement aucune fonction équivalente entre iPhone et Mac pour un usage grand public, seuls des outils de gestion d’entreprise permettant ce type de contrôle à distance côté écosystème Apple.
Rien ne garantit pour autant que ces commandes seront un jour activées telles quelles. Mais leur niveau de détail, jusqu’aux messages de confirmation distincts selon le type d’action demandée, laisse penser qu’il s’agit d’une fonctionnalité proche d’être déployée plutôt que d’un simple brouillon abandonné en cours de route.
Une application qui continue de combler ses manques
Cette découverte s’ajoute à une série d’améliorations récentes pour Lien avec Windows. Microsoft avait notamment ajouté cet été la possibilité de supprimer définitivement les PC fantômes de la liste des appareils appairés, un problème qui traînait depuis longtemps. Samsung a de son côté tenté de concurrencer l’application avec sa propre offre Galaxy Connect, élargie récemment à tous les PC sous Windows 11, mais avec des résultats jugés nettement moins fiables sur des tâches aussi simples que le copier-coller entre appareils.

articles.title: 350 Go en 5G+ à 9,99€/mois : le forfait Free pensé pour la rentrée des foyers connectés
articles.text:
La rentrée est souvent l'occasion de faire le tri dans son budget, forfait mobile compris. Free ajuste le prix de son forfait 5G+ 350 Go pour les abonnés Freebox, une offre que nous avons passée au crible pour voir à qui elle profite vraiment.
À l'approche de la rentrée, revoir son forfait mobile fait partie des réflexes budgétaires les plus simples à activer. Le Forfait Free 5G+ 350 Go, habituellement facturé 19,99 €/mois, redescend à 9,99 €/mois pour les abonnés Freebox Pop, une réduction qui pèse sur la durée puisque aucun engagement n'est requis. Ce tarif s'adresse en priorité aux foyers déjà équipés d'une Freebox Pop et qui n'ont pas encore rattaché leur ligne mobile à leur abonnement internet.
Les non-abonnés Freebox peuvent tout de même souscrire ce forfait à son tarif standard, qui reste stable dans le temps puisque Free annonce ne plus l'avoir augmenté depuis 2012. Un repère utile au moment de comparer les offres avant la rentrée, quand plusieurs opérateurs ajustent leurs grilles tarifaires.
Voici le Forfait Free 5G+ 350 Go à 9,99 €/mois au lieu de 19,99 €/mois chez Free !
Pourquoi choisir le Forfait Free 5G+ ?
- Prix réduit : 9,99 €/mois au lieu de 19,99 €/mois pour les abonnés Freebox Pop, avec passage en data illimitée.
- Volume de data généreux : 350 Go en 5G/5G+ en France métropolitaine, illimité pour les abonnés Freebox Pop.
- Sans engagement : résiliable à tout moment, avec prise en charge des frais de résiliation jusqu'à 10 €.
Un forfait pensé pour les usages intensifs de la rentrée
Avec 350 Go de data en 5G/5G+, ce forfait couvre large les usages du quotidien : streaming vidéo en haute définition, visioconférences professionnelles, partage de connexion pour les enfants en période de rentrée scolaire ou navigation intensive en télétravail nomade. Dans son comparatif des meilleurs forfaits mobiles, la rédaction de Clubic attribue à Free Mobile une note de 8,1/10, saluant l'équilibre entre enveloppe data généreuse, services inclus et stabilité tarifaire. Le forfait embarque également Free mVPN, une option de protection de la navigation directement intégrée au réseau mobile, ainsi que l'option eSIM Watch pour les montres connectées compatibles. Pour les foyers multi utilisateurs, cette combinaison de volume de data et de services intégrés limite le recours à des applications tierces payantes.
Face aux autres forfaits Free, où se situe le 5G+ 350 Go ?
Comparé à la Série Free à 150 Go, ce forfait mise sur une enveloppe data plus large et une stabilité tarifaire dans la durée plutôt que sur un prix d'appel limité à un an, ce qui évite la bascule automatique vers un forfait supérieur douze mois plus tard. Il reste toutefois moins généreux que le Forfait Free Max, qui propose une data illimitée à tous sans condition de Freebox, mais à un tarif plus élevé et sans la remise liée à l'abonnement Freebox Pop.
✅ Les points forts
- Un tarif divisé par deux pour les abonnés Freebox Pop, ramené à 9,99 €/mois.
- Un passage en data illimitée pour les abonnés Freebox Pop, sans surcoût.
- 35 Go de data utilisables dans plus de 115 destinations à l'étranger.
- Free mVPN et option eSIM Watch inclus sans supplément.
- Aucun engagement de durée et prix stable dans le temps.
❌ Les limites
- Le tarif à 9,99 €/mois et la data illimitée sont réservés aux abonnés Freebox Pop, les autres restent au tarif standard.
- Sans Freebox, le tarif reste à 19,99 €/mois, plus élevé que certaines offres data seule du marché.
- Le débit est réduit au delà des 350 Go pour les abonnés hors Freebox Pop.
- La compatibilité 5G+ dépend du smartphone utilisé, tous les modèles ne l'exploitent pas.
Le Forfait Free 5G+ 350 Go à 9,99 €/mois reste à vérifier directement chez Free avant la rentrée !
Ce forfait s'adresse avant tout aux foyers déjà abonnés à une Freebox Pop qui souhaitent regrouper leurs factures fixe et mobile sans complexité ni engagement. Le passage en data illimitée en fait une option particulièrement pertinente pour la rentrée, au moment où les usages mobiles liés aux trajets, au télétravail ou aux enfants connectés repartent à la hausse.
Les foyers sans Freebox, ou ceux qui consomment peu de data, trouveront sans doute un rapport plus adapté du côté d'une offre plus légère comme la Série Free. Pour les autres, ce forfait mérite d'être vérifié directement auprès de Free avant de finaliser son budget de rentrée.

articles.title: Suivre n'importe quel train en direct comme un avion : le site qui fait le buzz en France a un problème
articles.text:
Suivre n'importe quel train en direct comme un avion : le site qui fait le buzz en France a un problème
TrainTracker24 promet de suivre les trains comme Flightradar24 suit les avions. Sauf qu'en France, la position GPS des rames n'est pas rendue publique, et un site gratuit propose déjà le même service.
Suivre son TGV sur une carte comme on piste un vol Paris-Tokyo sur Flightradar24. L'idée fait fantasmer les passionnés de rail depuis des années. TrainTracker24, ouvert au public le 26 août 2026, promet exactement cela, avec une couverture France, Belgique et Espagne. Le site a immédiatement généré un afflux massif d'intérêt sur les réseaux sociaux. Mais un thread publié le 27 août par le compte ferroviaire BB27000, vu plus de 164 000 fois en quelques heures, a sérieusement douché l'enthousiasme.
1/ Il y a actuellement une petite polémique avec le site @traintracker24_ .
Ce site propose de suivre les train en temps réel sur une carte.
C’est dans l’idée du fameux site, très populaire, qui suit les avions dans le monde entier via leurs GPS embarqué. #FlightRadarhttps://t.co/TuJyKOe45i
Ce que TrainTracker24 montre vraiment sur sa carte
Le reproche est technique, et il est documenté. Contrairement à l'aviation, où les avions diffusent leur position via le protocole ADS-B, le ferroviaire français ne dispose d'aucun équivalent public. La SNCF partage en open data les horaires, les retards en gare et les informations d'infrastructure, mais la géolocalisation des rames reste absente du périmètre. La raison tient autant à des contraintes techniques qu'opérationnelles : le programme de recherche TECH4RAIL, lancé en 2017 par la SNCF, visait à développer un système de géolocalisation ferroviaire fiable par satellite, capable de fonctionner en tunnel et d'atteindre le niveau de fiabilité requis pour la sécurité des passagers.
TrainTracker24 ne prétend d'ailleurs pas le contraire. Le positionnement repose sur une extrapolation : horaires théoriques, retards déclarés en gare, profils de vitesse estimés. Selon BB27000, seuls les trains espagnols bénéficient d'un suivi GPS réel.
	
Tant que les trains ne seront pas suivis en direct, aucun site ne fera une réelle plus-value. Et vous pouvez attendre un moment : si ces données ne sont pas ouvertes, c'est pour des questions de sécurité nationale.
La SNCF n'a jamais confirmé publiquement cette explication, mais le contexte la rend plausible : les sabotages coordonnés qui ont paralysé le réseau TGV le matin du 26 juillet 2024, quelques heures avant la cérémonie d'ouverture des JO de Paris, ont rappelé la vulnérabilité de l'infrastructure ferroviaire.
Pourquoi la polémique dépasse le simple gadget cartographique
Au-delà de la promesse technique, c'est le modèle économique qui crispe certains. TrainTracker24 propose des abonnements payants pour des fonctions avancées. Or le site Cartotchoo, développé par Nicolas Wurtz, professionnel du ferroviaire, propose un fonctionnement rigoureusement identique, fondé sur les mêmes données publiques, en accès totalement gratuit. Cartotchoo pousse d'ailleurs l'exploration plus loin, avec tunnels, passages à niveau, électrification et cartes de chaleur des retards.
TrainTracker24 remplit honnêtement sa fonction d'estimation et le précise d'ailleurs bien dans sa documentation. La déception vient de l'écart entre la promesse marketing, calquée sur Flightradar24, et la réalité d'un secteur où la géolocalisation des trains demeure un chantier technique ouvert.

articles.title: Vulnerability-free container image startup Echo acquires Minimus - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Vulnerability-free container image startup Echo acquires Minimus
Echo Software Ltd., a startup that’s using artificial intelligence agents to secure container images, today announced it’s acquiring the assets of Minimus Inc. following the company’s wind-down.
The core proposition of Echo is that it uses AI agents to replace vulnerable upstream open-source components before they’re slotted into production. It does more than simply scan and generate fixes; it completely rebuilds software artifacts to lock them down with vetted repairs, creating a secure supply chain.
The company distributes containerized software images, alongside associated software bill of materials, signatures and attestations. The company provides critical vulnerability-free containers, libraries, operating system packages, virtual machines and Helm charts that act as trusted sources.
Containers are central to software distribution both on-premises and in the cloud. They are lightweight, portable packages that bundle everything software needs to run in production, including application code, runtime, libraries and dependencies. If vulnerabilities or bugs exist in a container or its downstream dependencies, an attacker can exploit them to break into secure systems.
Founded in 2022, Minimus provided cloud-application security through a catalog of minimal, hardened containers. Each of these containers maintained a purpose-built image constructed with only the runtime dependencies needed by an application, omitting anything ancillary such as package managers, shells, compilers or other tooling in order to flense away potential attack surfaces.
“Minimus built meaningful technology around a problem we both believe is fundamental: organizations shouldn’t have to inherit unnecessary security risk simply because they depend on open-source software,” said Echo co-founder and Chief Executive Eilon Elhadad. “When it became clear that Minimus was going to close, we saw an opportunity to make sure that work didn’t disappear.”
Echo notes that its hardened containers and underlying technology work across Linux distributions. Through the acquisition of Minimus, the company said it will be able to expand the number of distributions it can support, becoming a truly distro-agnostic approach to hardened software.
The company said it will add Minimus’s technology and relevant data to its current foundation of AI agents that investigate vulnerabilities, develop and validate patches, and maintain that hardened ecosystem for customers. AI agents depend on fresh, high-quality data to operate accurately, and increasing the width and breadth of that data will give Echo’s agentic AI fleet additional inputs to improve automated vulnerability research and remediation.
“When we made the decision to end operations, our priority was finding the right home for the technology we built and, most importantly, the right path forward for our customers,” said Minimus co-founder and CEO Ben Bernstein. “Echo shares our belief that software should be secure by default, and has built the platform and engineering capabilities to take that vision even further.”
This acquisition follows Echo’s $35 million Series A funding in December, led by N47. Similar companies competing in the same market include Chainguard Inc., which also supplies hardened containerized images and repository scanning.
The open-source software ecosystem continues to suffer under the burden of complex dependencies and vulnerable containers. Black Duck Software Inc.’s 2026 Open Source Security and Risk Analysis report found that 87% of audited commercial codebases contained at least one open-source vulnerability, with an average of 581 vulnerabilities per codebase. The report also noted that 65% of surveyed organizations reported a software supply-chain attack in the preceding year, including attacks involving dependency confusion and hijacked packages.
By providing continuously updated, hardened containers, packages, and libraries, Echo reduces exposure to known-vulnerable and unvetted components. Compromises are costly. According to IBM Corp.’s Cost of Data Breach Report 2026, the global average cost of a data breach hit $4.99 million this year, led by a 56% increase in AI-driven attacks.

articles.title: Primera batería cuántica: se puede cargar en menos de un segundo y ya funciona
articles.text:
Han creado el primer prototipo funcional de batería cuántica, un dispositivo capaz de absorber energía más rápido cuanto más grande es y de entregar corriente eléctrica.
La batería cuenta con la capacidad de cargarse por completo en femtosegundos (cuatrillones de segundo).
Integrar un batería cuántica, por ejemplo, a un computador de este mismo tipo, podría acelerar el desarrollo de medicamentos. El líder del proyecto, el investigador James Quach, dijo en conversación con The Guardian que se podría instalar en un dron y cargarla mientras está en vuelo.
PUBLICIDAD
“Una vez que la tecnología madure… ya no sería necesario detener el coche en una gasolinera para cargarlo; se podría cargar sobre la marcha”, agregó.
Una batería cuántica sirve para cargar y descargar energía de una manera distinta a la de los sistemas habituales. Su utilidad aparece sobre todo en entornos donde un sistema necesita pulsos de energía muy rápidos o una administración extremadamente precisa.
PUBLICIDAD
En una batería convencional, la energía se obtiene mediante reacciones electroquímicas que sostienen el flujo de grandes cantidades de electrones a través del dispositivo alimentado.
El proyecto está liderado por CSIRO, la Organización de Investigación Científica e Industrial del Commonwealth, en colaboración con la Universidad de Melbourne y RMIT.
Cómo funciona la batería cuántica
La batería cuántica propuesta por Quach recurre a efectos de la mecánica cuántica en lugar de apoyarse en reacciones químicas. Ese cambio de principio físico es el que abre la posibilidad de una carga más rápida a medida que se agregan más unidades activas.
PUBLICIDAD
El dispositivo se basa en una microcavidad óptica formada por dos espejos diminutos separados por 100 nanómetros (328 pies), un espesor alrededor de mil veces menor que el de un cabello humano. En ese espacio, los investigadores colocan moléculas de un tinte orgánico y las excitan con un láser.
Con ese método, la luz y las moléculas pueden acoplarse con fuerza y formar estados híbridos de luz y materia. Ese acoplamiento potencia la absorción y el almacenamiento de energía mediante un fenómeno conocido como superabsorción.
PUBLICIDAD
La diferencia central con la física clásica es que las moléculas dejan de comportarse como unidades independientes y pueden actuar en conjunto. El efecto práctico es directo: la tasa de absorción crece con el número de moléculas, de modo que cuantas más participan, más rápido se carga el sistema.
La distancia respecto de una aplicación cotidiana sigue siendo grande. Por ahora, el dispositivo solo retiene una cantidad muy pequeña de energía, del orden de unos pocos miles de millones de electronvolts, y solo durante nanosegundos.
PUBLICIDAD
Esa limitación impide pensar en alimentar computadoras portátiles, vehículos eléctricos u otros aparatos de uso común. Para eso haría falta almacenar mucha más energía y conservarla durante lapsos mucho más largos.
Quach afirmó que ya avanzó en un nuevo diseño y que trabaja en un artículo científico para publicar esos resultados. Cabe agregar que las interacciones con el entorno pueden degradar los efectos cuánticos y reducir tanto el rendimiento como la posibilidad de escalar la tecnología.
PUBLICIDAD
Esta limitación ya había sido planteada por la Universidad de Tokio. Un equipo de esa institución realizó un experimento de laboratorio con láseres, lentes y espejos para recrear, a gran escala, el comportamiento de una batería cuántica.
“Una batería cuántica utiliza partículas microscópicas, como conjuntos de átomos”, explicó Yuanbo Chen, autor del estudio. “A diferencia de las baterías químicas, que obedecen las leyes clásicas de la física, estas partículas se rigen por la mecánica cuántica, lo que abre la puerta a usos que desafían —e incluso pueden quebrar— nuestras intuiciones sobre lo que ocurre a escalas muy pequeñas”.
PUBLICIDAD
En una carga convencional, el proceso suele dividirse en varias etapas que se ejecutan de manera consecutiva.
En este caso, los investigadores recurrieron a un fenómeno cuántico llamado “orden causal indefinido” (ICO): al llevar el sistema a un estado de superposición, el orden de los pasos puede existir en dos direcciones a la vez, haciendo posible que esas etapas operen de forma simultánea en lugar de secuencial.
PUBLICIDAD
Chen agregó que le interesa especialmente cómo las partículas cuánticas pueden poner en tensión una experiencia tan básica como la percepción del tiempo.
Con ICO, señaló, demostraron que el modo en que se carga una batería formada por partículas cuánticas podría modificar de manera drástica su rendimiento.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Roblox is cracking down on games that reward kids for doomscrolling
articles.text:
What just happened? Roblox is once again trying to restrict potentially abusive behavior that could harm kids. Some developers have attempted to force players to doomscroll through TikTok videos, but the practice is now officially considered inappropriate for younger gamers.
After going viral and attracting around half a million concurrent players, the Roblox experience "Steal an Egg" is now facing brand-new restrictions. The widely popular user-generated gaming platform is prohibiting younger players from accessing SAE and similar experiences because they are supposedly designed to encourage kids to watch endless streams of media content through reward-based gameplay mechanics.
Roblox's official alert does not expressly mention SAE, but the new policy is most certainly targeting the viral game first and foremost. The company said games that reward ongoing media consumption are now unavailable to players with a Roblox Kids (ages 5 to 8) or Roblox Select (ages 9 to 15) account. The policy will affect games designed to combine media feeds, autoplay, infinite scrolling, and systems that reward players for doomscrolling through TikTok videos of questionable value.
"Steal an Egg" fits perfectly into this new category. The game tasks players with raising eggs, but they can also steal eggs from other NPCs. Players are incentivized to increase their characters' speed either by spending in-game currency (Robux) or by watching a video feed on a virtual treadmill. "Steal an Egg" was recently removed from Roblox but is now back in the store without its troublesome video-feed feature.
The company explained that rewarding users for TikTok doomscrolling – which mostly means watching massive amounts of AI slop and brainrot-inducing clips these days – is not an appropriate gaming experience for younger users. Roblox Kids and Select accounts include several restrictions on access to the platform's chat feature and certain types of mature content.
Roblox also highlights that the new anti-doomscrolling restriction does not apply to the rewarded video ads feature, which rewards players for watching a short clip but does not include autoplay or other infinite-scroll-like design choices.
The new policy will certainly fuel the ongoing debate about the safety of millions of kids who access Roblox on a daily basis. Authorities across the globe are targeting the platform for allegedly trying to exploit younger players, turning a virtual chatroom into a safe haven for sexual predators and enabling other forms of child exploitation. So far, the company has tried to improve safety by implementing several age-related restrictions and AI-based identification procedures.

articles.title: Pasos para limpiar el aire acondicionado: evita facturas de energías costosas y resfriados en verano
articles.text:
La limpieza del aire acondicionado es una tarea clave para garantizar su buen funcionamiento, evitar consumos excesivos de energía y proteger la salud durante el verano.
El mantenimiento adecuado debe contemplar una serie de pasos, algunos sencillos que puede realizar el usuario en casa, y otros reservados para la intervención de un técnico acreditado.
PUBLICIDAD
El usuario puede encargarse de tareas preventivas como la limpieza de filtros y revisiones visuales de las unidades, mientras que el profesional debe centrarse en el diagnóstico y la reparación de averías complejas.
Ignorar este proceso puede derivar en averías costosas, menor eficiencia y riesgos sanitarios, sobre todo en hogares con personas vulnerables a resfriados o enfermedades respiratorias.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuáles son los pasos clave para limpiar el aire acondicionado en casa
Realizar una puesta a punto básica del aire acondicionado es una labor que no suele superar los 30 minutos y puede marcar una gran diferencia en la vida útil del aparato, según recalca Endesa.
El primer paso consiste en asegurarse de que el electrodoméstico no haya estado inactivo durante varios meses antes de encenderlo. Ponerlo a funcionar sin limpiar puede liberar al ambiente la suciedad y bacterias acumuladas en los filtros, siendo un riesgo para la salud respiratoria.
PUBLICIDAD
Para limpiar los filtros correctamente, se debe abrir la tapa del Split, extraer los portafiltros y retirar el polvo superficial con una aspiradora. Si los filtros presentan suciedad persistente, se pueden sumergir en agua fría con jabón antibacteriano, evitando siempre el agua caliente para no deformar las fibras.
Tras enjuagar con agua abundante, los filtros deben secarse por completo en una zona sombreada antes de volver a colocarlos. Esta operación asegura que el aire circule sin obstáculos y sin contaminantes.
PUBLICIDAD
Por qué es importante limpiar el Split y las rejillas interiores del electrodoméstico
La limpieza de los filtros por sí sola no es suficiente para un mantenimiento efectivo. Endesa sugiere que, con los filtros fuera, se debe limpiar la zona interior del Split y los tubos que quedan detrás.
Un paño humedecido con agua y jabón es suficiente para eliminar bacterias y restos de polvo, mientras que las rejillas requieren especial atención por la facilidad con la que el polvo se adhiere por la condensación.
PUBLICIDAD
Secar bien todas las superficies al finalizar es esencial para evitar la aparición de hongos y malos olores. Un Split limpio no solo mejora la calidad del aire, sino que reduce los riesgos de infecciones respiratorias y asegura que el aparato funcione a pleno rendimiento.
Estos pasos pueden repetirse al menos dos veces al año o cada vez que se perciban síntomas de suciedad acumulada, como disminución del flujo de aire o presencia de olores inusuales.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué debe revisarse en la unidad exterior y en el sistema de drenaje del aparato
El mantenimiento no termina en la unidad interior. La revisión visual de la unidad exterior es clave para comprobar que las entradas de aire no estén obstruidas por hojas, polvo o suciedad.
Si es posible, debe limpiarse la batería de intercambio utilizando un cepillo suave o aire a presión, facilitando así la expulsión eficiente del calor generado.
PUBLICIDAD
Respecto al drenaje, conviene asegurarse de que el tubo de desagüe no esté taponado. Una obstrucción en este conducto puede causar la acumulación de agua en la bandeja interna, lo que genera goteos molestos y la aparición de malos olores por el agua estancada.
Cuáles tareas de cuidado son del usuario y cuáles requieren intervención técnica
Distinguir entre higiene doméstica y reparación técnica es clave para evitar riesgos y garantizar la seguridad de la instalación. Endesa especifica que la limpieza de filtros, la higiene de la unidad interior y la inspección visual pueden realizarse en casa, siempre que se sigan las pautas del fabricante y se utilicen productos adecuados.
PUBLICIDAD
Si tras la limpieza el electrodoméstico sigue sin enfriar o persisten los fallos, conviene recurrir a un profesional autorizado. El técnico debe encargarse de la revisión de circuitos eléctricos, recarga de gases o reparación de componentes internos.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Elon Musk’s xAI used child porn to train Grok models, lawsuit says
articles.text:
xAI has now been accused of training Grok on child sex abuse materials (CSAM), as regulators and courts continue to probe how far the problem goes, and some Grok users have been arrested.
In a complaint filed on Wednesday, a plaintiff known as Jane Doe explained that she was preschool-age in the early 2000s when adult men repeatedly raped her to create CSAM to sell to pedophiles online. Since then, Doe’s images have been hashed by groups like the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) and the Canadian Centre for Child Protection (CCCP).
For her safety, Doe has opted to receive alerts from the US Department of Justice Victim Notification System any time she may be a victim in a new criminal investigation. Although she has received countless alerts, she was shocked when the CCCP notified her that it had identified AI-generated CSAM on xAI that depicted her. This re-traumatized Doe, whose complaint alleged that messages were found on online forums “between offenders chatting about creating AI generated CSAM of Plaintiff and other similarly situated known, legacy, victims of CSAM.”
Now, Doe fears that xAI has not only made it easier to make more violative images of the most distressing time in her life, but also that xAI allegedly has stored the images that Grok generates and uses those outputs to further train Grok. Because of this, she believes that Grok has been trained on both the initial set of images that have haunted her for more than 20 years and the more recent AI-generated ones.
