articles.title: Nvidia aurait racheté la plateforme d'IA Hugging Face pour 12,9 milliards de dollars
articles.text:
Fin 2025, la plateforme Hugging Face avait refusé une proposition d’investissement de 500 millions de dollars de Nvidia, redoutant qu’un investisseur aussi puissant puisse influencer ses décisions à l’avenir. Aujourd’hui, le média The Information annonce que Hugging Face a été racheté par Nvidia pour un montant de 12,9 milliards de dollars. Même si ce rachat n’a pour l’instant pas été confirmé, l’été fou de la plateforme ne semble pas encore terminé.
Nvidia aurait racheté Hugging Face pour un montant de 12,9 milliards de dollars
Selon le média The Information, Nvidia a racheté la plateforme Hugging Face pour un montant de 12,9 milliards de dollars. De son côté, Business Insider affirme qu’aucun accord définitif n’a été trouvé à ce stade. Ni Nvidia ni Hugging Face n’ont commenté l’information. Pour rappel, Hugging Face a été fondé en 2016 par trois Français : Clément Delangue, Julien Chaumond et Thomas Wolf. Cette plateforme, spécialisée dans l’intelligence artificielle, permet principalement aux chercheurs, aux développeurs et aux entreprises de partager, découvrir et utiliser des modèles d’IA, notamment open source. On y trouve notamment des modèles capables de générer du texte, de comprendre des images, de traduire des langues ou encore de créer du contenu audio.
En 2023, lors de sa dernière levée de fonds, Hugging Face avait été valorisée à 4,5 milliards de dollars. Si ce rachat se confirme, Nvidia aurait donc mis sur la table un montant près de trois fois supérieurs à la valorisation établie en 2023. Il faut dire qu’Hugging Face s’est considérablement développé en l’espace de trois ans, passant notamment de 450 000 modèles hébergés fin 2023 à 3 millions en août 2026, tout en consolidant sa position d’infrastructure centrale de l’IA open source. De son côté, l’entreprise Nvidia a continué à exploser son chiffre d’affaires grâce au développement de l’intelligence artificielle, même si Samsung est parvenu à la devancer lors du second trimestre 2026. En réalité, 12,9 milliards de dollars représente un montant relativement modeste pour Nvidia.
Pourquoi Nvidia veut racheter Hugging Face
Dire que la concurrence sur le marché des puces dédiées à l’IA s’intensifie relève de l’euphémisme. Google, Samsung, Amazon, Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic et SpaceXAI développent désormais leurs propres puces ou accélérateurs IA. Et il ne s’agit là que de quelques exemples. Même si Nvidia reste pour l’instant le leader de ce marché, la concurrence est là, et elle ne semble pas vouloir rigoler.
L’entreprise Nvidia en est consciente et cherche désormais à diversifier ses activités dans l’IA, notamment en renforçant sa présence dans le cloud et les services liés à l’IA, avec le rachat de Hugging Face. Par ailleurs, ce rachat permettrait à Nvidia de renforcer son emprise sur l’écosystème logiciel de l’IA. En mettant la main sur une plateforme incontournable de l’IA open source, Nvidia pourrait ainsi se rapprocher des développeurs et favoriser l’utilisation de ses propres technologies, au-delà de ses seules puces. Il reste maintenant une question : si ce rachat est confirmé, la plateforme Hugging Face pourra-t-elle conserver son indépendance et sa neutralité sous l’égide de Nvidia ?
En 2025, lors de la proposition d’investissement de 500 millions de dollars de Nvidia, les craintes de Hugging Face de voir un géant américain influencer sur ses décisions à venir ne devaient pas être sans fondement. Voir maintenant une plateforme française en plein essor passer potentiellement sous la direction d’un groupe américain comme Nvidia soulève inévitablement des questions de souveraineté numérique. Si ce rachat est confirmé, la plateforme Hugging Face devrait rester française, mais sous quelles influences ?

articles.title: Plaud unveils wearable earbuds with built-in agentic AI interface - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Plaud unveils wearable earbuds with built-in agentic AI interface
Plaud Inc., the maker of artificial intelligence-enabled note-taking devices, today introduced the Plaud One Explorer Edition, a pair of earbuds and a charging box that connect people to AI agents for work and everyday digital tasks.
Both the Plaud One earbuds and the case can act as listening devices to record nearby conversations, and the buds act as a mobile interface between humans and AI chatbots and agents. With the press of a button or a voice command, either can capture conversation.
Earbud users are already used to carrying a charging case. With Plaud One, the case acts as a charger, a recording interface and a wireless connection. It includes a built-in eSIM with 4G LTE to keep itself and the earbuds connected without relying on a smartphone. Users can use it or the earbuds to upload conversations automatically from anywhere.
The earbuds look similar to Apple AirPods, all white, with a long flange that lets them sit in the ear. While wearing the earbuds, users can have Plaud listen in on conversations, take notes or speak directly with the company’s AI agent, Plaud Agent. It can be hooked up with native integration tools such as Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion and Slack to maintain a full view of a person’s needs.
Or users can connect the earbuds to a third-party agent such as Anthropic PBC’s Claude or OpenAI Group PBC’s ChatGPT.
“AI agents become truly useful when they understand the context in which human intent is formed,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Nathan Xu. “That context lives in conversation. Plaud One brings agents closer to the real-world work people do every day, while Plaud Intelligence gives them the context and capabilities to act.”
The charging case is larger than the usual case, shaped like a small box. It contains a microphone that gives it a fair listening range. That means it can be placed in the middle of a table during a meeting to capture an entire group conversation for a team meeting or a client update.
Afterward, a user could pop in the earbuds, call up Plaud Agent, and ask it to produce first drafts of deliverables for the internal team or clients. For example, it could produce a summary of the meeting, email it to the appropriate people who might have missed it in person, or draft reports based on metrics that need to be sent to upper management or the client by end of day.
Pluad is betting this in-the-moment interface will let users quickly get up to speed while they’re in the hallway, between meetings and their workstation. It allows them to let their agents get to work so that they can sit down and look at drafts, update them to their liking and then get going.
A lot of information and context is lost between meeting notes and the keyboard. Plaud provides a contextual memory of what was said, what people needed and what they want. It also gives users a way to connect quickly with their AI agents discreetly, get updates and put AI bots to work.
The company offers numerous other AI-enabled note-taking devices. These include the Note, a wallet-sized form factor that attaches to the back of a smartphone, and the NotePin, a pill-like microphone device that attaches to a lapel or lanyard.
The company said the Plaud One Explorer Edition is available for pre-order starting today for $249.99 and includes $200 in credits, which power the company’s upcoming AI agent capabilities and other features. Although the company offers a free subscription for note-taking and many AI features, credits come through monthly paid subscriptions. Shipments will begin in the fourth quarter of 2026.

articles.title: Ver Barcelona vs Athletic en Fútbol Libre o Roja Directa expone el dispositivo a malware y es ilegal
articles.text:
En la búsqueda por acceder a transmisiones deportivas sin costo, varios usuarios recurren a páginas piratas como Fútbol Libre o Roja Directa para ver encuentros de La Liga española, incluyendo partidos de alto perfil como Barcelona vs Athletic.
Esta práctica, aunque común, implica riesgos para la seguridad digital y puede acarrear sanciones legales. Según la Organización Internacional de Policía Criminal (INTERPOL), el acceso a contenidos piratas expone a los dispositivos a malware y coloca al usuario ante posibles acciones judiciales.
PUBLICIDAD
De acuerdo con INTERPOL, la descarga o visualización de material protegido mediante sitios no autorizados afecta la integridad de celulares, computadoras y televisores, aparte de involucrar a los usuarios en actividades ilícitas, con posibles multas o penas de prisión.
Qué tipo de malware puede afectar los dispositivos al visitar páginas piratas
Según INTERPOL, las investigaciones recientes revelan que muchos sitios web y redes P2P que distribuyen transmisiones piratas alojan malware o virus capaces de dañar el dispositivo del usuario o sustraer información personal.
PUBLICIDAD
Este software malicioso puede instalarse de manera inadvertida al ingresar a estas páginas o al descargar archivos asociados con las transmisiones deportivas. Las consecuencias incluyen la pérdida de datos personales, el acceso no autorizado a cuentas bancarias y la posibilidad de que el malware se propague en redes corporativas o familiares.
INTERPOL señala que estos ataques no solo comprometen la información del usuario, sino que pueden transformar el dispositivo en un punto de acceso para actividades criminales, como el robo de identidad o la falsificación de información confidencial.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo pueden los usuarios de páginas piratas ser víctimas de fraude financiero
La autoridad advierte que los métodos de pago usados en sitios piratas suelen carecer de seguridad, lo que incrementa la probabilidad de fraudes con tarjetas de crédito y otras estafas financieras.
La adquisición de accesos a servicios ilegales requiere la introducción de datos bancarios en plataformas sin garantías mínimas de protección, lo que deja expuesta la información sensible del usuario.
PUBLICIDAD
Asimismo, algunos de estos sitios utilizan tácticas de phishing, donde el usuario es engañado para entregar contraseñas personales que luego pueden utilizarse para vaciar cuentas bancarias o realizar compras no autorizadas.
Qué consecuencias legales hay por ver partidos en plataformas ilegales
INTERPOL subraya que la descarga o distribución de material protegido por derechos de autor sin permiso puede derivar en sanciones legales.
Las leyes internacionales de propiedad intelectual permiten que los titulares de derechos persigan judicialmente a quienes acceden, reproducen o comparten contenido de manera ilícita. Las penalizaciones varían según la jurisdicción, pero pueden incluir multas y, en casos graves, penas privativas de libertad.
PUBLICIDAD
La organización internacional agrega que, en ocasiones, los usuarios pueden ser investigados por el uso de servidores proxy que han facilitado ataques informáticos previos, lo que complica aún más la situación legal y expone al usuario ante procedimientos judiciales prolongados.
Cómo se puede identificar un sitio web pirata
Uno de los principales consejos de INTERPOL para evitar riesgos consiste en identificar servicios de transmisión ilegítimos. Las señales de alerta incluyen:
- La oferta de grandes cantidades de contenido a precios muy bajos o de manera gratuita.
- La ausencia de información sobre licencias oficiales.
- La falta de atención al cliente.
El precio es otro indicador relevante. Según los servicios legales suelen ser más costosos, pero garantizan una experiencia segura, estable y ajustada a la normativa vigente. Consultar siempre el sitio oficial de la empresa de contenidos ayuda a verificar la autenticidad del servicio ofrecido y evita caer en fraudes.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué otras actividades delictivas financian las páginas piratas
El impacto de utilizar sitios como Fútbol Libre o Roja Directa no se limita al usuario individual. Según INTERPOL, los responsables de estas páginas pueden pertenecer a organizaciones criminales que utilizan las ganancias obtenidas para financiar delitos como el juego ilegal en línea, la explotación sexual y el tráfico de drogas.
La pauta principal es optar por proveedores oficiales, mantener el software actualizado y utilizar programas de antivirus y firewall para proteger la información personal y corporativa.

articles.title: Son nuestras costumbres y hay que respetarlas: las élites españolas llevan 3.200 años practicando el noble arte de la endogamia
articles.text:
Había una copistería frente a la facultad de ciencias que tenía colgadas en la pared, una tras otra, todas las orlas de una de las ingenierías más salvajes de todo el sistema universitario español. Solía mirarlas mientras esperaba. Y sé que puede parecer aburrido, pero no había nada más fascinante que ver cómo las personas del claustro iban cambiando, pero los apellidos no.
Sí, sí. Es una exageración, un estereotipo fácil. Pero además es verdad. Y no sólo en la universidad: la endogamia es uno de esos fenómenos recurrentes de la vida social de nuestro país.
Una larga historia
Como explicaban hace unos años el catedrático Javier Barnes y el economista Fernando Faces, "que en España las reglas del juego para los concursos y adjudicaciones de contratos se basen en normas de hace un siglo y medio, de 1870, nos da una idea de lo mucho que necesitamos renovarnos". No es un bug, es una feature.
Como cada vez es más evidente, se trata de una tecnología antropológica muy conocida para reforzar el poder de un grupo de personas. Y es por eso que no solo afecta a los ayuntamientos, las empresas o la universidad: la endogamia llegó a provocar la extinción de la rama de la dinastía Habsburgo. Lo que no sabíamos es que era algo tan antiguo.
Espera, espera, pero ¿Cuándo se inventó la endogamia? No lo sabemos, pero estamos cerca de descubrirlo. Tras analizar 24 individuos enterrados en la necrópolis zaragozana de Los Castellets II, un equipo internacional de especialistas ha encontrado una posible respuesta a todo esto.
Y es que hasta dos tercios de los individuos estaban emparentados entre sí. Pero no solo había padres e hijos, había parentescos de quinto y sexto grado. Eso significa que el túmulo de Mequinenza se utilizó como mausoleo de una familia extensa, como una especie de nodo funerario central de una tupida estructura de filiación.
Es la primera evidencia directa de prácticas endogámicas a finales de la Era de Bronce en la Peninsular. ¿Qué significa esto? Que los peninsulares de aquella época estaban descubriendo la versión más básica de la endogamia: líderes que consolidan su estatus casándose entre ellos.
"Tales niveles de consanguinidad no se habían registrado en periodos anteriores de la prehistoria ibérica", dicen los investigadores. Y son tan altos que, en realidad, no podemos descartar que la práctica excediera a las élites y se extendiera por toda la sociedad (por todo el Mediterráneo, de hecho).
Y luego vino el gran cambio
Los metales, siempre han sido lo metales. "La Prehistoria es el periodo de la historia de la humanidad desde nuestros orígenes hasta la aparición de los primeros estados burocráticos", explicaba el arqueólogo Rodrigo Villalobos. Y lo que estamos viendo en Mequinenza es cómo esos estados empiezan a tomar forma.
Esto nos permite saber cosas sobre la endogamia, claro. Nada nuevo en términos etnográficos, pero sí algo clave que nos afecta hoy en día.
Aunque, claro, eso da problemas a largo. La endogamia sigue viva porque es un método extremadamente eficaz de asegurar la estabilidad de las estructuras sociales. Tiene costes asociados, pero son costes a largo plazo. A medio plazo, suelen ser más que asumibles.
Pero más allá: lo interesante es que, como avala la investigación, las prácticas endogámicas son sensibles a prácticas "sistemas legales y las prácticas administrativas". No es una maldición irreformable. Esto nos lleva a una pregunta más profunda: ¿realmente queremos cambiarlo?

articles.title: Apple confirms September 9 event, where its first foldable iPhone and iPhone 18 Pro are expected
articles.text:
Something to look forward to: Apple will hold its next product event on September 9, when it is expected to unveil new Pro iPhones and could introduce its first foldable iPhone. A foldable model would put Apple into a maturing hardware category, while a revised release schedule could reshape how the company rolls out new iPhones.
The event starts at 1 pm ET at the Steve Jobs Theater at Apple Park. Apple sent invitations on Wednesday with the tagline, "Surprise and shine." The presentation will also be streamed on Apple's website.
The foldable iPhone would be the event's biggest announcement. Apple has been linked to the product for years, but recent reports and an apparent dummy unit have provided more details about its possible design. The device appears to use a wide, book-style format, similar to Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold 8, that unfolds into a larger display.
That design would put Apple directly into a category that Samsung and other Android phone makers have been developing for several years. Foldable phones have improved in areas such as hinge construction, display durability, and software support for larger internal screens. Apple's entry would test whether the company can bring its hardware-and-software approach to a market it has so far watched from the sidelines.
Apple is also expected to update its Pro and Pro Max models. If it maintains its current naming convention, the devices would be called the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max. The updates are expected to be less extensive than the redesign Apple introduced with the iPhone 17 Pro Max last year.
 – Greg Joswiak (@gregjoz) August 26, 2026
The standard iPhone 18 may not appear at the event. Apple is reportedly planning to launch that model next year instead. The company is also rumored to be preparing an iPhone 18e and a second-generation iPhone Air for 2027.
If those reports are accurate, Apple would be moving away from its usual approach of launching its main iPhone lineup simultaneously each fall. Instead, the company could spread releases throughout the year while using its September event to focus on higher-end devices and new form factors.
The event will also be the first major Apple presentation led by John Ternus. The former hardware chief is scheduled to become CEO on September 1, replacing Tim Cook.
For Ternus, the September 9 event may offer an early indication of Apple's future hardware priorities. A foldable iPhone, new Pro models, and a different release schedule would mark a notable shift in the company's iPhone business.

articles.title: Só hoje: Motorola Edge 60 (512 GB) despenca 51% no Mercado Livre • Tecnoblog

Só hoje: Motorola Edge 60 (512 GB) despenca 51% no Mercado Livre
Edge 60 (512 GB) tem câmeras de 50 MP e tela POLED de 120 Hz; celular da Motorola sai por menos da metade do preço no Pix com cupom válido só hoje (27)
O Motorola Edge 60 de 512 GB está saindo por R$ 1.709 no Pix com cupom COMPRABOA no Mercado Livre. O celular da Motorola, com câmeras de 50 MP e tela POLED de 120 Hz, alcança o 2.º menor preço já divulgado pelo Achados, com um desconto de 51% sobre o preço original de R$ 3.499.
Mas corra, pois esta promoção acaba nesta quinta-feira (27).
O kit de câmeras do Edge 60 traz uma wide com OIS e uma ultrawide de 122º, que captam belas situações com grandes ângulos, e uma frontal que tira ótimas selfies, todas de 50 MP. A telefoto de 10 MP traz zoom óptico de 3x para proporcionar fotografias com muitos detalhes. Todas filmam em 4K.
Seu chip MediaTek Dimensity 7300 e os 12 GB de RAM expansíveis até 24 GB via RAM Boost suportam reprodução de apps em multitarefa e alguns recursos do Moto AI. Os 512 GB de armazenamento oferecem espaço interno de sobra para quem adora filmar e fotografar.
A tela POLED de 6,7″ possui taxa de 120 Hz e brilho de 4.500 nits, combinação capaz de reproduzir imagens com cores fiéis e alta fluidez nas transições em apps e games, além de ter visibilidade garantida em qualquer lugar. O vidro Gorilla Glass 7i protege-a contra quedas e pancadas.
O corpo do Edge 60 conta com as certificações IP68/IP69 e militar MIL-STD-810H, que conferem proteção em uma série de cenários extremos, como poeira intensa, mergulhos acidentais, altas temperaturas.
Sua bateria de 5.200 mAh suporta carregamento ultrarrápido de 68 W via USB-C e permite injetar uma carga para um dia inteiro de uso em apenas 8 minutos, segundo a fabricante. Assim, o gadget resiste a longos períodos longe de tomadas, uma característica excelente para usuários com agendas corridas.
O Edge 60 de 512 GB (R$ 1.709 no Pix com cupom COMPRABOA) será atualizado apenas até o Android 18 e possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.4 e NFC.

articles.title: Samsung Display Elevates Gaming Immersion with QD-OLED at Gamescom 2026
articles.text:
Thursday, August 27th 2026
	
		
	
	
	
Samsung Display Elevates Gaming Immersion with QD-OLED at Gamescom 2026
Samsung Display will showcase the gaming performance advantages of QD-OLED through collaborations with global game companies at gamescom 2026, the world's largest gaming exhibition. The company also announced plans to begin mass production of 24.5-inch QD-OLED panels optimized for eSports and FPS games by the end of this year, underscoring its technology leadership in the gaming monitor market.
Highly anticipated titles from CAPCOM, KRAFTON and CD PROJEKT RED take the stage at gamescom with QD-OLED displays
Samsung Display announced on August 27 that it will partner with global game companies including CAPCOM, KRAFTON, and CD PROJEKT RED at gamescom 2026, taking place in Cologne, Germany, from August 26 to 30. New and flagship titles from each company will be showcased on gaming monitors featuring Samsung Display's QD-OLED panels, demonstrating the outstanding picture quality of QD-OLED to gamers from around the world.At CAPCOM's booth, visitors can get hands-on experience with 'Onimusha: Way of the Sword,' a new title marking the return of the Onimusha franchise after more than 20 years, as well as 'Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen,' an expansion for action RPG 'Dragon's Dogma 2.' Other playable titles include 'PRAGMATA,' 'Street Fighter 6' and 'Mega Man: Dual Override.' A total of 90 QD-OLED gaming monitors, including the EVNIA '32MN8900,' GIGABYTE 'MO32U24,' and MSI 'MAG 321UP QD-OLED X24,' will be used for hands-on gameplay.
KRAFTON will showcase three of its five upcoming titles featured at this year's gamescom on 85 Alienware QD-OLED gaming monitors, including the 'AW2725Q (4K),' 'AW3225QF (4K),' and 'AW2726DM (QHD).' Visitors will have an opportunity to preview the multi-team tactical arena game 'Project ZETA,' the two-player cooperative adventure 'Age Twisters' and the action RPG 'TARAE: The Unbound' ahead of their official release. A video introducing QD-OLED Penta Tandem, Samsung Display's premium technology brand for its five-layer stacked QD-OLED structure, will also be shown at the KRAFTON booth.
At the CD PROJEKT RED booth, a trailer for 'Songs of the Past,' the third expansion pack for 'The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt,' will be shown on eight QD-OLED TVs. Visitors can also watch gameplay demonstrations on three monitors equipped with QD-OLED displays. Samsung Display will authentically showcase the immersive dark fantasy world of 'The Witcher' through QD-OLED's high contrast ratio based on true blacks and rich color reproduction.
With games spanning a wide range of genres, from action RPGs and FPS titles to adventure games, visitors can experience firsthand the differentiated gaming performance of QD-OLED across genres. With response times of approximately 0.03 ms, QD-OLED displays deliver sharp, dynamic visuals, while true blacks enabled by their self-emissive technology and the high color purity and wide color gamut of quantum dots bring out everything from fine details in dark scenes to vibrant colors, maximizing gaming immersion and enjoyment.
QD-OLED expands to 24.5-inch displays, a key size for eSports and FPS gaming, with mass production set to begin by year-end
Samsung Display announced at gamescom 2026 that it plans to begin mass production of 24.5-inch FHD QD-OLED panels by the end of this year, targeting the FPS and eSports markets. As several global PC manufacturers unveiled plans at the event to launch new products featuring Samsung Display's 24.5-inch QD-OLED displays, Samsung Display will begin supplying 24.5-inch FHD QD-OLED displays in response to customer demand.
The 24.5-inch format is widely used in the FPS and eSports markets, as its compact screen size allows players to quickly take in the entire display - an important advantage in games where split-second decisions and precise control matter. It has become a preferred choice among competitive gamers and is emerging as a key segment of the gaming monitor market.
Samsung Display plans to further strengthen QD-OLED's proven technological leadership in the market by responding promptly to customer demand, including for 24.5-inch displays. According to market research firm Omdia, Samsung Display shipped approximately 2.5 million QD-OLED panels for monitors last year, accounting for nearly 75% of the overall self-emissive monitor panel market.
"Gaming is one of the areas where consumers can most directly experience a display's fast response times and picture quality," said Brad Jung, Vice President and Head of the Large Display Marketing Team at Samsung Display. "Through a wide range of gaming content, we will showcase the unique gaming experience offered by QD-OLED displays and further strengthen our leadership in the premium gaming market by expanding our product lineup to include the 24.5-inch segment."

articles.title: Hugging Face MicroDuck robot is the first educational robot I've wanted in a very long time — even if I do have to program some of the cuteness
articles.text:
Forget Disney’s BDX Droid — the $399 Hugging Face Microduck robot is even more adorable and versatile thanks to Lidar, NFC and, yes, roller skates
It'll cost you $399
- Microduck is Pollen Robotics' new programmable robot
- It looks like a cute robo-duck, and has some adorable, pre-baked interactions
- It's up for pre-order priced at $399, and it should ship in time for Christmas
If the measure of a successful robot is cuteness, Microduck could be the most successful bot in ages. Unveiled this week by Pollen Robotics (a division of AI company Hugging Face — yes, that Hugging Face), Microduck is a 25-centimeter-tall educational robot that appears to arrive with surprising mobility, balance, and personality.
Pre-orders, which kicked off today (August 27) promise a $399 (that's the introductory price), roughly 1.7lb pre-built duck-like robot complete with a mouth that doubles as a gripper, a voice —duck calls, it seems — 15 degrees of freedom (basically a measure of the number of ways all the motors let it move), and motors that let it walk, waddle, move its head and, thanks to a pair of IMUs (inertial movement unit), stay upright even when pushed around.
There's a single-eye camera paired with a Lidar system for navigating its environment and, perhaps, recognizing its owner. Pollen Robotics has yet to specify the camera's megapixels. There are also speakers for voice, and microphones for it to hear. The robot runs on a relatively low-power Rockchip RK3566 ARM chip that's backed by 1GB of RAM and 32GB of on-board storage. There's on-board Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, NFC, and a smallish 2,600mAh battery that promises roughly one hour of operation.
These are not killer specs, but the teaser videos show a highly engaged and undeniably adorable little bot. I was particularly taken with how it can recover and stand back up after a fall (or being pushed over). Microduck will arrive with a lot of pre-programmed interactions, but much of the cuteness may come via its open-source platform and your programming skills.
The Microduck kit will ship with an SDK that includes virtual training environments, along with training scripts and tools, and "a tested sim-to-real workflow." The idea, obviously, is that while you might grow to love Microducks' baked-in personality, it's what you can build with your kids that will really matter. This is an educational robot, after all.
It's almost familiar
It's also worth mentioning Microduck's obvious resemblance to another extremely cute, though entirely unattainable robot: Disney's and Star Wars' BDX Droid. Both robots are bipedal with a somewhat squat posture and cute, oversized heads, and as with the BDX-Droid, it's hard to believe the Microsoduck can stay upright. But that's where the similarities end. That semi-autonomous/remote-controlled BDX Droid is much larger, probably far more expensive, and is currently only wandering around Disney World. Plus, there are currently no plans to bring it to consumers.
The $399 Microduck is just the base package, and Pollen Robotics also plans to ship an optional charger pack for $39, a dev pack that includes spare motors, cables, and batteries for $119, and an accessory pack that includes a laser pointer (perhaps for Microduck to chase), roller skates(!) that Microduck can wear and ride, and 10 NFC tags. One wonders if those tags might be used to trigger certain Microduck actions.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Microduck is Pollen Robotics' second edu-robot, the first being the Reach Mini, an almost equally cute but more or less stationary desk companion robot. Pollen Robotics claims it sold 10,000 units.
Microduck's success will likely depend on just how many of those endearing qualities are on display out of the box, and how much we have to code ourselves. Initially, you can fake some of it, since Microduck can be remote-controlled with a gaming controller; but the real fun happens when it starts to respond in unexpected ways.
The other X factor is how many people are willing to pay almost $400 for a plastic and semi-autonomous robot duck. I know I'm intrigued, and wouldn't mind trying to program it to create the duck-bot of my dreams.
Microduck is expected to ship by Christmas, and is available in Cream, Graphite. Lavender, and Sky.

articles.title: The iconic T-38 jets flown by astronauts just got a spiffy new look
articles.text:
For the first time in decades, NASA has rolled out one of its iconic astronaut training aircraft with a bold, new look.
The space agency debuted a new livery on one of its T-38 jets in celebration of its program to return astronauts to the Moon. The Artemis design retains nods to what made the “white rocket” immediately recognizable, but adds a new colorway and painted graphics to make clear where NASA is headed.
“This new ‘Artemis’ livery has a black and white paint scheme with blue and red stripes that separate those two paint schemes,” said Sean Brady, who proposed and designed the new livery while serving as the T-38 project pilot in NASA’s Aircraft Operations Division (AOD), part of the Flight Operations Directorate at Johnson Space Center in Houston. “The Artemis program logo in the back and a picture of the Moon is on the left and right side of the rear fuselage.”
The Northrop T-38 “Talon” two-seat supersonic trainer has been in use by NASA since 1962, when the first jets were loaned to the agency by the US Air Force. Flown today to familiarize new astronauts with working in a high-stress, dynamic environment and maintain pilots’ flight proficiencies, Johnson Space Center currently has a fleet of 14 active T-38 jets stationed out of nearby Ellington Airport.
All but one is adorned with the classic blue stripe livery that has been associated with most of NASA’s aircraft over the past five decades.
“Shiny new toy”
The Artemis jet, referred to by NASA by its tail number N924NA (or 924 for short), stands out now due to its new look but was only selected because it was next in line to be repainted as part of AOD’s regular maintenance of its aircraft.

articles.title: Alienware AW3926QW 39-inch WUHD OLED gaming monitor review: Premium play and imagery in a large format
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
Aside from a minor gamma issue, the Alienware AW3926QW is nearly perfect. It provides addictive gaming and a gorgeous image with reference-level color accuracy. And it’s a unique and useful size with lots of screen area and an immersive quality.
Pros
- +Bright, sharp and colorful image
- +Smooth motion processing with low input lag
- +Accurate out of the box, no calibration needed
- +Multiple eSports modes with 165 and 330 Hz refresh rates
- +Lots of screen real estate
- +Premium styling and build quality
- +Decent value
Cons
- -Slightly light gamma
- -Gamma options are only available in one picture mode
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
What gives a product flagship status? Some might say price, and that is sometimes true. But in the computer monitor world, a flagship is something that stands apart from the rank and file.
I’ve reviewed many 34-inch ultra-wide panels. These 21:9 aspect ratio curved displays can cover the user’s peripheral vision almost as well as a pair of VR goggles. When using them, I have often wished for a little more vertical space. The easiest way to achieve this is with a 39-inch size.
Alienware’s latest flagship delivers that very thing to the best gaming monitors category. The AW3926QW is a 39-inch, 21:9 1500R curved OLED panel with Tandem RGB Stripe technology, 5120x2160 (WUHD) resolution at 165 Hz, eSports modes that run at 330 Hz, Adaptive-Sync, HDR10, Dolby Vision, VESA DisplayHDR 500 and wide gamut color. Let’s take a look.
Alienware AW3926QW Specs
| Panel Type / Backlight | Organic Light Emitting Diode (OLED) Tandem RGB Stripe | 
| Screen Size / Aspect Ratio | 39 inches / 21:9 | 
| Row 2 - Cell 0 | Curve radius: 1500mm | 
| Max Resolution and Refresh Rate | 5120x2160 @ 165 Hz | 
| Row 4 - Cell 0 | 2560x1080 @ 330 Hz | 
| Row 5 - Cell 0 | FreeSync and G-Sync Compatible | 
| Native Color Depth and Gamut | 10-bit / DCI-P3 | 
| Row 7 - Cell 0 | HDR10, Dolby Vision | 
| Row 8 - Cell 0 | VESA DisplayHDR 500 True Black | 
| Response Time (GTG) | 0.03ms | 
| Brightness (mfr) | 300 nits full screen | 
| Row 11 - Cell 0 | 1,300 nits 3% window | 
| Contrast | Unmeasurable | 
| Speakers | None | 
| Video Inputs | 1x DisplayPort 2.1 | 
| Row 15 - Cell 0 | 2x HDMI 2.1, 1x USB-C | 
| Audio | 3.5mm headphone output | 
| USB 3.2 | 1x up, 3x down (2x A, 1x C) | 
| Power Consumption | 58w, brightness @ 200 nits | 
| Panel Dimensions WxHxD w/base | 36.2 x 18.2-22.5 x 9.6 inches (919 x 462-572 x 244mm) | 
| Panel Thickness | 5.1 inches (130mm) | 
| Bezel Width | Top: 0.35 inch (9mm) | 
| Row 22 - Cell 0 | Sides: 0.43inch (11mm) | 
| Row 23 - Cell 0 | Bottom: 0.59 inch (15mm) | 
| Weight | 22.6 pounds (10.25kg) | 
| Warranty | 3 years, incl. burn-in | 
This isn’t my first foray into Tandem RGB Stripe tech. I saw it in Asus’ recent PG32UCWM as well. It brings two important advantages: higher brightness with lower power consumption and wide gamut color without the addition of a Quantum Dot layer. The AW3926QW easily tops 500 nits in HDR mode for a 25% window pattern and can fill the screen at over 300 nits. Alienware claims 1,300 nits for a 3% window, and I have no reason to doubt that. It doesn’t quite have the color volume of a QD display, but my sample covered more than 100% of DCI-P3. It also came out of the box with reference-level color accuracy and a pro-worthy sRGB mode.
The AW3926QW also has higher pixel density than typical 34-inch ultra-wides. Most of them are 3440x1440, which means 109ppi, equivalent to a 27-inch 16:9 QHD panel. A 39-inch panel at 5120x2160 pixels delivers a 4K level density of 144ppi. That’s a clearly visible difference. The AW3926QW is super sharp with no fringing or other clarity-reducing artifacts.
Gaming performance is high thanks to Adaptive-Sync, FreeSync, and G-Sync support, and a 165 Hz refresh rate. For eSports applications, there are multiple resolution and refresh modes that go up to 330 Hz in full screen, 25, 27, and 32-inch formats. These can be switched with a single click thanks to a programmable joystick that controls a comprehensive OSD. Alienware also provides its AlienVision feature with its designable aiming points and sniper aids. And you get a frame counter, timer, and screen alignment marks.
On the outside, the AW3926QW sports AlienFX lighting with colored LEDs for the power button and the Alien Head on the back. These can be controlled in the OSD or with the Alienware Command Center app. Also included are the latest video inputs, DisplayPort 2.1 and HDMI 2.1, along with USB-C for a total of four ports. And there are USB upstream and downstream connections with KVM control.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
With everything included except for internal speakers, you’d expect the AW3926QW to cost a lot, but it’s opening at $1,100, which makes it competitive with many other premium OLED ultra-wide displays. On paper, Alienware is delivering everything a flagship should have without an extreme price. Let’s see how it performs.
Assembly and Accessories
Alienware’s packaging is completely recyclable, even down to the paper tape that seals the clamshell carton. The panel, upright, and base assemble without tools. Included cables are IEC power, two USBs, DisplayPort, and HDMI. The power supply is internal.
Product 360
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The AW3926QW maintains Alienware’s latest styling aesthetic with a thin bezel and the cool floating upright that appears to be detached from the small-footprint base. Everything is solid, with metal cores and heavy plastic coverings finished in a matte texture. On the back is a lozenge-shaped vent ring that provides effective fanless cooling. Inside it is the Alien Head and a polished logo. The stand unsnaps to reveal a 100mm VESA mount with fasteners included if you want to use an arm.
The stand provides a 4.3-inch height range plus 5/21 degrees tilt and 20 degrees swivel. The base remains stationary while the stand pivots upon it. There is no portrait mode, but you can tweak the panel with five degrees of yaw if your desk isn’t level. Movements are firm and sure and befit a flagship product.
The screen curve is 1500R, which in the scheme of things is fairly subtle. There’s just enough wraparound effect to bring the sides of the screen into your vision cone when sitting around three feet away. You can sit closer if you like since pixel density is tight, but then you’d have to turn your head to see the whole image. The screen coating is shiny, but a polarizing layer keeps reflections from affecting the picture.
There are inputs aplenty for video, four in all. You get two HDMI 2.1, a DisplayPort 2.1, and USB-C, which functions as DP Alt and delivers 90 watts of power. There’s a 3.5mm headphone jack plus more USBs: two on the bottom of the panel edge (C and A) and an A and B on the I/O panel. They can be bound to video inputs using the KVM wizard in the OSD.
OSD Features
The AW3926QW’s OSD appears when you click the joystick. First up is a quick menu with signal info at the top, then an up-click opens the full menu, which is quite extensive, which is why there are 12 photos below.

The little quick menu at the bottom of the first screen is programmable by the user. You can put almost any monitor function into the five slots provided. You can also program the four joystick directionals for a total of nine options. This makes it easy to change picture modes, refresh modes, call up aiming points, or whatever. That’s all controlled in the Personalize menu, photo 11 above.
The first menu is Game, and it has everything a gamer could want. There are 12 picture modes in total. Three of them have color temp and dark stabilizer settings, called Game 1-3. Custom Color also has color temp gain and offset sliders along with color management. Creator is where you’ll find gamma presets and colorspace options like sRGB. Standard is the default mode, and it’s visually perfect out of the box.
Game Enhance Mode has a timer, frame counter, and alignment marks. For the aiming points, go to AlienVision where you’ll see a cool reticle editor that includes settings for sniper aids. You can create up to three configurations for later recall.
The eSports modes are where you can change the refresh rate and image size. I’m not sure why they aren’t all in one menu, but between the two sections, you’ll find 25, 27, 32, and 39-inch settings. All but the 32 run at 330 Hz. The 32-inch gives you 4K at 165 Hz and puts black bars on the sides of the image. That one is handy because it doesn’t change the pixel density like the others. The 25- and 27-inch options can be moved up or down from the center if you prefer.
AlienFX Lighting refers to the power LED and Alien Head’s color and effect options. You can customize them to a variety of colors and movements.
For HDR signals, there’s a Dolby Vision option along with eight modes for HDR10 content. Custom Color HDR includes grayscale calibration. Of the listed modes, the brightest one is True Black, and the one with the best luminance tracking is Peak 1300 Bright.
The USB menu is where you’ll find the KVM options. There, you can bind the HDMI and DisplayPort inputs to specific USB ports which means you can use one keyboard, monitor and mouse for multiple systems like a PC and a console.
Personalize is where you can program the quick menu and joystick directionals, as well as toggle the power delivery of the USB ports.
For panel maintenance, the AW3926QW has pixel refresh, which runs automatically when the panel health indicator goes red. That’s determined automatically by internal software. Alienware backs the AW3926QW with a three-year warranty that includes burn-in.
Alienware AW3926QW Calibration Settings
The AW3926QW doesn’t need calibration in its Standard picture mode. I noted slightly light gamma, but the color gamut and temperature are visually perfect out of the box. To adjust the grayscale, I used Custom Color mode, which has both gain and offset sliders. If you want to change the color space, Creator mode has that option along with gamma presets. The three Game modes also have grayscale adjustments. My recommended SDR settings are below. For HDR, there are eight modes available plus Dolby Vision. I suggest trying Peak 1300 Bright and True Black to see which you prefer. They look similar, but the latter is a tad brighter while the former has more accurate luminance tracking.
| Picture Mode | Custom Color | 
| Brightness 200 nits | 80 | 
| Brightness 120 nits | 45 | 
| Brightness 100 nits | 34 | 
| Brightness 80 nits | 23 | 
| Brightness 50 nits | 6 (min. 40 nits) | 
| Contrast | 75 | 
| Color Temp User | Red 100, Green 100, Blue 98 | 
Gaming and Hands-on
A few days with the AW3926QW proved its flagship status beyond a doubt. It excelled as a gaming monitor and workday display in equal measure.
For gameplay, my test PC with its GeForce RTX 4090 was more than enough to drive it at 165 Hz at full 5120x2160 resolution. That’s 11 megapixels in case you’re counting, about 23% more than Ultra HD. The video processing here is good enough that I didn’t wish for 240 Hz. And I had little need for the 330 Hz modes. I can see their use in competition or with lesser video cards to keep the action smooth. But I saw nothing but perfect motion resolution and hyper precision. Aiming and moving became an extension of my brain as control inputs were instantly translated.
Image quality was also superb, with lush bright color and deep contrast. Playing in SDR mode with the full color gamut was excellent, but HDR games were even better. The AW3926QW is a superb HDR display. And don’t forget to try Dolby Vision with its dynamic tone mapping. I didn’t have any DV games, but I watched content from a Blu-ray player that looked stunning. Going back and forth between HDR True Black and Peak Bright 1300, I found I preferred True Black because it had a tad more impact. On page five, I’ll explain the technical differences.
I’ve reviewed many 34-inch ultra-wide displays, and while I find them excellent for gaming, they lack the height I prefer for writing content. The 39-inch AW3926QW is perfect for getting work done. It is only half-an-inch shorter than the 32-inch 16:9 screen I use every day. So, it’s ideal for lining up two or three windows side by side when comparing copy or graphics. I loved it for Photoshop, where I could open and see multiple photos and still have room for toolbars. If you’re already a user of dual screens, the AW3926QW is the perfect replacement if you’re sick of that pesky dividing line.
The monitor proved to be flagship-worthy in every respect. The stand is solid; styling is premium and everything about the AW3926QW exudes quality. The inclusion of USB ports and KVM further extends its usability. And the selection of esports modes makes it flexible for a wide variety of gaming systems.
Takeaway: The AW3926QW is super useful in every way and excels as a gaming display. It delivers speedy and responsive performance at 165 Hz and impressive frame rates up to 330 Hz in the esports modes. The picture is gorgeous with vivid and accurate color and plenty of brightness. HDR has high impact and multiple picture modes to choose from, plus Dolby Vision support. The AW3926QW is a great all-around monitor that delivers a lot of bang for the buck.

articles.title: GTA 6: Fake-Demo lockt Gamer in die Malware-Falle
articles.text:
Demo zu GTA 6? Hacker locken Gamer in die Malware-Falle
Rockstar Games hat bei Grand Theft Auto 6 endlich die Karten auf den Tisch gelegt. Über Netflix und später auch auf Youtube gab es eine knappe halbe Stunde Gameplay-Material aus dem Open-World-Spiel zu sehen. Gamer:innen auf der ganzen Welt sind gehypt und können es kaum erwarten, ihre Hände an GTA 6 zu bekommen. Doch diese Vorfreude wird jetzt zur Gefahr.
GTA 6: Demo entpuppt sich als Malware
Wie Malwarebytes berichtet, tauchten schon vor der Gameplay-Enthüllung im Netz erste Webseiten auf, die eine Demo zu GTA 6 versprechen. Die Webseiten sehen dabei aus, wie die Seite des Entwicklerstudios Rockstar Games und werben für die Testversion mit offiziellem Promomaterial. Zudem wurde auf den Fake-Webseiten auch auf den großen Gameplay-Reveal auf Netflix hingewiesen, um den Anschein zu erwecken, es würde sich tatsächlich um eine Seite von Rockstar Games handeln.
Über einen großen Button mit der Aufschrift „Play Now“ könnten sich Gamer:innen angeblich eine Demo von GTA 6 sichern und erste Runden durch Vice City drehen. Hier sollten Gamer:innen schon ins Stutzen kommen. Denn Rockstar Games hat GTA 6 nur für PS5 und Xbox Series X/S angekündigt. Eine PC-Version ist bisher nicht offiziell und dürfte wohl noch eine Weile auf sich warten lassen.
Zudem ist die Datei „gta6_installer.exe“ lediglich 1,1 Megabyte groß. Das ist deutlich weniger Platz, als ein GTA 6 benötigen würde. In der Theorie könnte es sich noch um einen Launcher handeln, der dann die benötigten Dateien extra herunterlädt. Tatsächlich landet aber ein Infostealer auf dem PC der Gamer:innen, der es primär auf Browser und darin befindliche Daten abgesehen hat.
Laut Malwarebytes gehört der Infostealer zur Vidar-Familie und ist in der Szene recht bekannt. Das Tool sucht im Browser nach gespeicherten Logins, Session-Cookies und der Historie der besuchten Seiten. Insgesamt kann der Infostealer dabei 19 verschiedene Browser ins Visier nehmen, darunter Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Opera und Vivaldi. Für Gamer:innen, die auf die GTA-6-Demo hereingefallen sind, ist das oftmals gar nicht ersichtlich. Denn der Infostealer agiert unbemerkt im Hintergrund. Sie dürften sich lediglich wundern, warum die Datei nichts macht, wenn sie doppelt angeklickt wird.
Wer sich die falsche GTA-6-Demo auf den Rechner geladen hat, sollte das Gerät zunächst mit einem Anti-Viren-Programm scannen und auffällige Dateien in die Quarantäne verschieben lassen. Laut Malwarebytes sollte dann ein anderes, nicht infiziertes Gerät, genutzt werden, um sämtliche Passwörter und E-Mail-Adressen zu ändern und über Funktionen wie „Auf allen Geräten ausloggen“ aktive Sessions zu terminieren. Nach diesen Änderungen solltest du wichtige Accounts genau im Blick behalten, ob sie womöglich übernommen wurden. Wende dich dann an den verantwortlichen Support, um größere Schäden zu verhindern und dein Konto zurückzubekommen.

articles.title: Trump signs order to rename Lake Ontario to 'Lake America'
articles.text:
U.S. President Donald Trump has signed an order to rename Lake Ontario to “Lake America.”
At a conference held at the White House, Trump said this would take effect “immediately.” This comes after he said on Tuesday that he was giving “serious consideration” to the name change because “we don’t expect to be doing much business with Ontario any longer.” Naturally, he’s referring to the trade war that he started with Canada after making unreasonable demands that Prime Minister Mark Carney said “asked too much and offered too little.”
Holy shit — the purpose of this Trump event is to announce that he’s changing the name of Lake Ontario to “Lake America.” It will be interesting to see which if any institutions and companies go along with this
— Aaron Rupar (@atrupar.com) August 27, 2026 at 1:42 PM
Of course, Trump doesn’t have any real jurisdiction to rename Lake Ontario, the namesake of which came from First Nations peoples. “You cannot rename away our history,” said the Mississaugas of the Credit First Nation in a statement response to Trump’s latest announcement.
Indeed, while Trump is certainly free to sign an executive order in the U.S. requiring it to be called “Lake America” there, he has no authority to get anywhere else in the world, including Canada, to abide by that.
With that said, it remains to be seen how tech companies will respond. We saw in January when the ever-immature Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico to be renamed the “Gulf of America” that platforms like Google Maps spinelessly abided by this. Even in other countries like Canada where Trump’s order wasn’t binding, Google Maps has still been showing “Gulf of Mexico (Gulf of America).” Presumably, something similar will happen with Lake Ontario.
All of this comes amid a heated trade war between Canada and the U.S. Talks fell through for a new free trade deal after the U.S. made many demands, including for Canada to lift requirements on CanCon discoverability and bilingual labelling. The U.S. has since withdrawn those particular orders, even though Trump claimed he never made them in the first place.
In general, Trump has claimed that Canada has been taking advantage of the U.S. in free trade, even though he himself signed the previous CUSMA deal and the two nations have famously benefited from a close partnership. But naturally, Trump’s fragile ego has now destroyed many decades of kinship between Canada and the U.S. as he hits Canada with billions in tariffs and plans to enact many more on the automotive industry next year. Canada, meanwhile, is set to introduce its own retaliatory tariffs next month.
All the while, Trump has been throwing insults at Carney, calling him “a weak and ineffective Prime Minister.” The president also blasted Ontario Premier Doug Ford, saying he’s “the less charismatic, intelligent, and overall unimpressive brother of the late, great, Rob Ford.” While Carney has naturally avoided that kind of name-calling, Ford referred to Trump as a “loser” and the “king of bankruptcies” while telling him to “kiss my ass.”

articles.title: AI, athletes, and Keith Rabois: StrictlyVC is back in New York on September 10 | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Mark your calendars: on Thursday night, September 10, StrictlyVC — TechCrunch’s boutique evening series — is heading to New York’s West Village (the real one — brownstones, cobblestones, and all — not the Mission Bay stretch of San Francisco that’s earned the nickname “Vest Village” for all the Patagonia-clad VCs roaming around).
It’s our first New York event in two years, and after a run of great nights this year in San Francisco, L.A., and Athens, we couldn’t be more excited to be back — with a stacked lineup to match. What’s in store:
Keith Rabois. We’re kicking off the night with the inimitable Keith Rabois, who recently relocated East from Silicon Valley and, true to form, seems intent on shaking things up wherever he lands. Rabois has never been shy about what he thinks is working in venture and what isn’t — he’s backed Ramp four times and invested as often in State Affairs, a company using AI and local journalists to track statehouse-level news and policy data across all 50 states. He’ll share his strong opinions on founders who raise more capital than they actually need, just because they can. And we’ll get him talking about Khosla Ventures’ boldest AI bet yet: its early $50 million check into OpenAI back in 2019 when the outfit had no clear business model — plus what he makes of the narrative that OpenAI is facing more headwinds right now than its rivals.
Craig Shapiro and Jason Levien. After our sit-down with Keith, stick around for a conversation you won’t find anywhere else. Craig Shapiro’s venture firm, Collaborative Fund, is generously co-hosting the evening with us, and we’ll sit down with Shapiro and Jason Levien, CEO of D.C. United, to talk sports organizations as business investments — and the increasingly tangled intersection of sports, fandom, commerce, and community.
Tristan Walker. Staying on the theme of community, we’ll dig into a conversation with two founders building for a world where AI does more — but also takes something away. Tristan Walker, who sold his last company, Walker & Company Brands (maker of Bevel), to Procter & Gamble in 2018, is back with Heirloom Craft, a startup focused on reshoring American fine craftsmanship — training a new generation of artisans and rebuilding the supply chains behind them.
Brynn Putnam. Walker will be joined by Brynn Putnam, who sold her last company, connected-fitness startup Mirror, to Lululemon for $500 million, just three years after it was launched. Putnam’s newest venture is Board, a game company blending physical play with AI-powered creation tools — built as something of an antidote to the isolation tech has fueled, bringing people back together around, literally, a board.
Deven Parekh. Last but not least, we’re thrilled to catch up with Deven Parekh, who has co-run Insight Partners — the New York powerhouse investment firm — for more than 25 years. Insight doesn’t do a lot of press, but Parekh has agreed to pull back the curtain on how the firm is thinking about a landscape where it’s gotten harder to tell asset classes apart, as some of the biggest funds have grown exponentially larger. What we want to know: how does Insight compete in a world where capital itself is a commodity, but the potential returns on massive investments have also never been bigger?
Expect a fun night all around, with drinks, hors d’oeuvres, and plenty of networking before and after the fireside chats, including with Connie Loizos, Rebecca Bellan, and other TechCrunch writers (as well as our friends from other outlets).
Giant thanks again to the team at Collaborative Fund for making the night possible. More details and ticketing info right here. See you in the (real) West Village.

articles.title: NewPower Worldwide Expands Credit Facility to $750 Million to Support Global Growth and Customer Demand - EE Times
articles.text:
NASHUA, New Hampshire – NewPower Worldwide, one of the electronics industry’s fastest-growing distributors, today announced it has expanded its committed credit facility to $750 million, further enhancing its ability to invest in inventory, support customer growth, and capitalize on opportunities across the global supply chain.
The increase follows a period of exceptional growth for NewPower Worldwide. Since its founding in 2014, the company has rapidly expanded its global footprint, growing to 14 offices across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC, with $5 billion in annual sales, and managing more than $1 billion in inventory worldwide. The expanded facility provides additional financial capacity to support continued growth and evolving customer requirements.
In today’s rapidly changing supply chain environment, financial strength and access to capital play a critical role in securing inventory and maintaining continuity of supply. The expanded facility enhances NewPower’s ability to purchase strategically, support large-scale customer requirements, and provide greater flexibility around inventory and delivery programs.
“Our customers rely on NewPower to solve supply chain challenges quickly and at scale,” said Carleton Dufoe, Chief Executive Officer of NewPower Worldwide. “Expanding our credit facility to $750 million gives us additional capacity to secure inventory, support larger strategic programs, and respond faster when opportunities arise across the market. It further strengthens our ability to deliver solutions that help customers succeed in any market environment.”
The expanded facility strengthens NewPower’s ability to support larger and more complex customer programs while increasing the volume and scale of transactions the company can execute globally. By increasing its purchasing capacity, NewPower is better positioned to secure strategic inventory, capitalize on market opportunities, and deliver supply solutions to customers with greater speed, flexibility, and scale.
“Our expanded partnership with NewPower reflects our confidence in the company as it executes on behalf of its clients,” said Jason Upham, Senior Vice President at Citizens. “Our banking team led an increased credit facility designed to support NewPower’s goals and growth objectives.”
The expanded facility reflects NewPower’s continued financial strength and enhances its ability to convert market opportunities into tangible supply solutions for customers worldwide. Combined with the company’s global sourcing network and supply chain expertise, the added capacity positions NewPower to execute larger programs, secure critical inventory, and help customers respond to changing market conditions with speed, flexibility, and confidence.
About NewPower Worldwide
NewPower Worldwide is a leading independent distributor of electronic components and finished goods, serving OEMs, EMS providers, and supply chain partners worldwide. Privately owned and headquartered in Nashua, New Hampshire, the company is recognized for its advanced sourcing technology, global reach, and commitment to solving complex supply chain challenges.

articles.title: The Aussie Tech Tax: How to Buy Gadgets from the US and Actually Save - Tech Guide
articles.text:
You have probably noticed it. You read a review of a set of earbuds, look up the American price, then check the Australian one and find yourself paying noticeably more for exactly the same thing in exactly the same box.
It is not your imagination, and it is not only the exchange rate. Smaller market, longer supply chain, fewer competing retailers. Plenty of tech carries a premium here that has nothing to do with the product itself.
The American sale calendar is a different beast
Black Friday exists in Australia now, but the American version is the original and the discounts still cut deeper, particularly on audio gear, wearables and accessories. Cyber Monday follows immediately after, and Prime Day gives you a second run at it mid-year. US retailers also clear stock harder, so end-of-line earbuds and last season’s colourways get discounted properly rather than lingering near full price.
What is genuinely worth importing
The sweet spot is small, light and moderately priced, which happens to describe most of the tech people actually buy. Wireless earbuds and headphones, gaming headsets and controllers, wireless chargers, instant cameras, fitness trackers, and anything from a US brand that has never set up local distribution.
One planning note: there is a value ceiling on what can be sent to Australia in a single package, currently around AUD $1,000. In practice that shapes what you buy rather than stopping you, since it comfortably covers accessories and mid-range gear. A big haul is simply better split across two shipments.
Getting it to Australia
Most US retailers will not post here, which is where a forwarding service comes in. Parcel forwarding from the US to Australia gives you a real American address to use at the checkout. You shop as a local, your orders land at the warehouse, and they are sent on to you.
Stackry is one of the long-established operators, and a few things make it simpler than it sounds. Orders from different shops are combined into one box, so a Black Friday weekend spent buying from three sites still costs you one international shipment. GST is collected before your parcel is sent rather than sprung on you at the door. And Stackry operates from New Hampshire, which charges no American sales tax, so nothing is added at that end either.
Two technical points for anything with a battery. Keep the battery inside the device, since loose lithium batteries cannot be flown internationally. And you will need a Type I plug adapter, though almost all modern chargers are rated 100 to 240 volts, so no voltage converter is required.
Plan it backwards from the date you need it
International orders take weeks, not days. Buying in the American Black Friday and Cyber Monday window in late November puts your parcel here comfortably ahead of Christmas, and well before the school and uni year starts in late January.
A bit of forward planning, one free sign-up, and the gadget costs what the Americans pay for it.

articles.title: Mieux que des AirPods ? Plaud lance des écouteurs IA qui travaillent à votre place
articles.text:
L’an dernier, Plaud, une entreprise basée à San Francisco, s’est fait remarquer en commercialisant plusieurs appareils de prise de notes assistée par IA, dont le Plaud Note, le Plaud Note Pro, et le Plaud NotePin. Tous ces produits surfent sur l’essor de l’intelligence artificielle générative, et la multiplication des appareils estampillés IA.
Reconnue comme l’une des pionnières des outils de prise de notes IA, la marque vient de dégainer une nouveauté de taille, le Plaud One. Il s’agit d’une paire d’écouteurs taillés pour capter vos conversations et les comprendre à l’aide de l’IA. La première itération du Plaud One est évoquée sous le nom d’édition Explorer.
À lire aussi : J’ai testé le dictaphone du futur – traduction, résumé et voix clonée
Un agent IA qui passe à l’action
Contrairement aux précédents outils de la marque, le Plaud One se présente comme la première interface pensée pour l’ère des agents IA, explique Plaud. Les écouteurs écoutent toutes les conversations et comprennent l’intention de l’utilisateur, et ils passent ensuite à l’action. Plaud a en effet conçu les écouteurs pour agir directement dans les outils de travail du porteur.
Le fonctionnement de l’outil repose sur Plaud Intelligence, la plateforme conversationnelle de la marque, ainsi que sur le Plaud Agent. C’est cet agent qui est capable de traduire des informations entendues dans les conversations en actions à réaliser dans des outils du quotidien comme Gmail, Google Calendar, Notion, Slack ou Teams. Sur base des informations entendues, l’agent peut par exemple rédiger un compte rendu, préparer un e-mail de suivi ou générer un rapport de synthèse, sans que le porteur ne doive faire quoi que ce soit.
Parmi les cas d’usage mis en avant par Plaud, on trouve un commercial qui fait rédiger un compte rendu complet dès qu’il sort d’un rendez-vous client, un dirigeant qui obtient un résumé de sa dernière conversation avant d’entrer dans une réunion, ou encore un responsable qui reçoit chaque lundi matin un briefing automatique basé sur les échanges de la semaine précédente. Ces différentes fonctions reposent sur une bibliothèque de Skills et de plugins dédiés à des cas d’usage spécifiques. On trouve aussi une mémoire contextuelle qui s’enrichit à chaque utilisation des écouteurs.
Selon Plaud, c’est cette fonctionnalité qui distingue Plaud de la concurrence. À notre connaissance, c’est en effet la première fois qu’un accessoire IA est animé par un agent qui est en mesure d’écouter, de comprendre et ensuite d’agir dans l’interface d’outils. Les autres appareils sur le marché, généralement similaires aux autres outils de prise de note de Plaud, se contentent d’enregistrer, de résumer des conversations et de les mettre en forme.
« L’Édition Explorer est née d’une conviction : les meilleures interfaces se construisent sur le terrain, au contact de celles et ceux qui les mettent réellement à l’épreuve. Avec Plaud One, les agents se rapprochent du travail réel des professionnels, et Plaud Intelligence leur apporte le contexte nécessaire pour passer à l’action », explique Nathan Xu, cofondateur et directeur général de Plaud, à l’occasion du lancement du Plaud One.
A lire aussi : La CNIL s’alarme des lunettes connectées, Meta en rajoute avec un collier IA
Un boîtier avec microphones et eSIM
Pour écouter les conversations, le Plaud One embarque trois microphones et un capteur de vibration par oreille pour les appels. Le groupe mise aussi sur de la réduction de bruit active. Le boîtier de recharge comprend également quatre microphones, ce qui lui permet d’enregistrer seul, jusqu’à cinq mètres de distance, sans que l’utilisateur porte les écouteurs. Notez par ailleurs que les microphones de l’étui peuvent fonctionner sans que le smartphone du porteur se trouve à proximité. Plaud a en effet inclus une eSIM 4G LTE dans le boîtier. Grâce à la connexion offerte par l’eSIM, le boîtier peut transmettre les conversations en temps réel vers le cloud.
Sur le plan de l’autonomie, Plaud annonce jusqu’à six heures d’enregistrement de réunions et trois heures d’appels. Grâce à l’étui de recharge, l’autonomie des écouteurs peut atteindre les 36 heures. La marque américaine évoque aussi un système de recharge rapide. Celui-ci permet de récupérer deux heures d’enregistrement supplémentaires en dix minutes de charge.
Plaud précise que toutes les nouveautés logicielles de Plaud seront déployées sur l’ensemble des appareils de la marque. La mise à jour Plaud App 4.0, attendue au quatrième trimestre 2026, viendra enrichir les interfaces de Plaud avec de nouvelles fonctions héritées du Plaud One.
Prix et date de sortie
Côté prix, le Plaud One est proposé à 249,90 €, ce qui place les écouteurs parmi les appareils les plus chers de la marque. La société américaine offre aux acheteurs 176 euros de crédits d’utilisation de Plaud Intelligence, en plus des 300 minutes d’utilisation offertes tous les mois à tous les clients. Les écouteurs sont d’ores et déjà disponibles à la précommande, et seront commercialisés au cours du quatrième trimestre de l’année.

articles.title: Volkswagen dévoile l'ID. California Cruise, la version camping-car de l'ID. Buzz
articles.text:
Cela faisait plusieurs années que la question revenait sur toutes les lèvres des amateurs de vans aménagés : quand est-ce que Volkswagen allait décliner son van électrique ID. Buzz en version camping-car ? Eh bien, la réponse a été donnée dans un communiqué le 27 août 2026 : c’est maintenant.
À l’occasion du Salon de la Caravane 2026 de Düsseldorf (du 28 août au 6 septembre), la marque de Wolfsburg a enfin présenté l’ID. California Cruise, le premier représentant 100 % électrique du California et digne héritier du célèbre Combi Westfalia.
L’ID. Buzz des aventuriers
Construit sur la base de l’ID. Buzz Pro, l’ID. California Cruise — disponible en empattement court ou long — reçoit un système de couchage sur mesure pour deux personnes, avec un lit de 2,03 m de long sur 1,20 m de large sur lequel est posé un matelas pliant de 9 centimètres d’épaisseur.
À cela s’ajoutent des équipements classiques sur le California : grilles d’aération et stores occultants ainsi que deux chaises et une table de camping qui se rangent directement dans l’habitacle.
Autre nouveauté, le mode California a lui aussi été repensé pour l’électrique : une unité de commande dédiée gère l’éclairage, l’alimentation continue des ports USB et la climatisation. Volkswagen annonce que le système est capable de maintenir une température de sommeil confortable pendant 48 heures au maximum, selon l’état de charge de la batterie et l’écart entre températures intérieure et extérieure.
La batterie comme prise de courant géante
La motorisation 100 % électrique est particulièrement pratique pour la vie en autonomie grâce au système de chargeur bidirectionnel et notamment à la fonction Vehicle-to-Load (V2L). Sur l’ID. California Cruise, il est possible d’alimenter des appareils électriques (machine à café, bouilloire, plaque de cuisson, glacière…) à une puissance continue de 2 000 W et même temporairement à 3,6 kW en pic, en puisant dans la batterie haute tension (79 kWh ou 86 kWh selon l’empattement).
Côté recharge du véhicule lui-même, l’application dédiée California a été enrichie. Celle-ci affiche désormais les bornes compatibles directement sur l’itinéraire emprunté pour permettre aux conducteurs de planifier leurs trajets, en plus du planificateur embarqué.
Volkswagen n’a pas communiqué l’autonomie de l’ID. California Cruise. À titre indicatif, l’ID. Buzz Pro promet jusqu’à 481 km WLTP dans sa configuration la plus favorable. La déclinaison California, alourdie par son équipement, devrait avoir une portée logiquement moindre. C’est ici la limitation des camping-cars 100 % électriques.
Plus de 60 000 € pour l’ID. California Cruise
Reste la question du prix : le Volkswagen ID. California Cruise sera proposé à partir de 60 761 € en Allemagne, avec des premières livraisons attendues début 2027. Pour connaître les prix en France, il faudra patienter jusqu’à l’ouverture des commandes, annoncée pour cet automne.

articles.title: C'est parti, l'ESA signe ses premiers contrats pour financer les lanceurs européens de demain
articles.text:
L'ESA a signé les premiers contrats du European Launcher Challenge, son programme destiné à renforcer l'autonomie spatiale européenne. Trois entreprises, Rocket Factory Augsburg, PLD Space et Isar Aerospace, vont se partager plus de 540 millions d'euros pour rejoindre l'orbite avant 2028.
Trois entreprises européennes viennent de décrocher un financement conséquent de l'ESA dans le cadre du European Launcher Challenge. Il s'agit de Rocket Factory Augsburg et d'Isar Aerospace pour l'Allemagne, et de PLD Space pour l'Espagne. Au total, plus de 540 millions d'euros sont mis sur la table pour accélérer le développement de lanceurs capables d'atteindre l'orbite avant 2028, avec l'ambition de renforcer l'autonomie de l'Europe dans l'accès à l'espace et d'élargir l'offre de services disponible pour ses clients institutionnels et commerciaux. Un quatrième acteur, le Français MaiaSpace, devrait rejoindre la liste dans les prochaines semaines.
Rocket Factory Augsburg, PLD Space et Isar Aerospace décrochent plus de 540 millions d'euros de l'ESA
Commençons par Rocket Factory Augsburg, qui travaille sur son lanceur RFA One, une fusée à trois étages haute d'une trentaine de mètres et propulsée par neuf moteurs. Elle doit décoller depuis le pas de tir écossais de SaxaVord, dans les îles Shetland, avec un objectif de 500 kg emportés en orbite héliosynchrone, celle-là même qu'affectionnent les satellites d'observation de la Terre. Pour ce projet, la société empoche 186,9 millions d'euros, financés majoritairement par Berlin, avec un coup de pouce britannique.
Du côté espagnol, PLD Space capitalise sur l'expérience de son démonstrateur Miura 1, testé en 2023, pour développer Miura 5. Le lanceur, qui décollera depuis le Centre spatial guyanais, vise une capacité de 540 kg en orbite héliosynchrone, avec des ambitions revues à la hausse pour séduire les clients institutionnels et commerciaux. Le contrat signé s'élève à 158,9 millions d'euros, porté par l'Espagne et complété par l'Allemagne.
Une autre belle entreprise allemande, Isar Aerospace, développe Spectrum, un lanceur à deux étages doté de dix moteurs, qui avait tenu l'air trente secondes lors d'un premier essai en 2025 depuis la base norvégienne d'Andøya. Un deuxième exemplaire se prépare déjà sur le même pas de tir pour un vol de qualification, avec cette fois de vraies charges utiles à bord et l'ambition de placer jusqu'à 1000 kg en orbite basse. Isar Aerospace touche ici la plus grosse enveloppe : 197,8 millions d'euros.
Calendrier, critères, enjeux : ce qu'il faut savoir sur la suite
Ces contrats concluent la deuxième étape du European Launcher Challenge, lancé en 2025, dont les propositions devaient être déposées au plus tard au mois d'avril 2026, avant de passer entre les mains d'un comité d'évaluation de l'ESA. Entre le business plan, la qualité technique, les ressources, le calendrier et les questions de conformité, chaque dossier a été passé au crible avant validation. Reste un dernier acteur en lice, le tricolore MaiaSpace, dont le processus de contractualisation, déjà bien avancé, devrait reprendre dans les prochaines semaines.
Les fonds alloués aux trois premières entreprises, pour plus d'un demi-milliard d'euros au total, seront progressivement débloqués, à mesure que les entreprises franchiront leurs jalons techniques. Une manière pour l'ESA de sécuriser son investissement, tout en poussant aussi les industriels à avancer vite. La feuille de route fixée par l'agence est établie, avec un premier vol orbital attendu au plus tard en 2027, puis une montée en puissance des capacités de charge utile prévue pour 2028.
« Cette étape lance le European Launcher Challenge et stimule la concurrence entre lanceurs européens », a réagi Géraldine Naja, directrice du transport spatial à l'ESA. Un avis partagé par Lucia Linares, responsable de la stratégie et des lancements pour le transport spatial à l'ESA, qui rappelle que l'agence a posé le cadre. Reste maintenant aux entreprises à prouver qu'elles peuvent tenir leurs promesses.

articles.title: Workplace fraud monitoring startup Yardstik raises $30M to help employers keep tabs on their staff - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Workplace fraud monitoring startup Yardstik raises $30M to help employers keep tabs on their staff
Yardstik Inc., a workforce screening startup that monitors companies’ employees for potential fraudulent actions, said today it has closed on a $30 million growth round of funding that brings its total amount raised to date to $65 million.
Harbert Growth Partners led the Series B round, which also saw participation from existing backers such as Rally Ventures, MissionOG, Crosslink Capital, Grotech Ventures and Great North Ventures.
The startup is trying to fix what it says is a critical blindspot in most human resources departments. Founder and Chief Executive Andrew Johnson told SiliconANGLE that most companies typically conduct background checks on their employees only once, before they’re hired. But that doesn’t take into account the fact that humans change over time, and just because employees have been given the all-clear at the time they were hired doesn’t mean they won’t become a risk later.
In fact, Yardstik cites data from the Association of Certified Fraud Examiners, which shows that the average occupational fraud scheme runs for about a year before companies detect them. This’s why the startup built its Human Trust Platform, which aims to give employers greater visibility into what their employees are up to by combining background screening with identity verification, fraud detection and continuous monitoring. The platform essentially keeps tabs on employees for as long as they’re working at the company to ensure they’re playing by the rules and not getting up to no good.
Johnson said the problem is something he has personally experienced. While working at the financial technology firm Branch Microfinance Bank Ltd., he stumbled across a case where employees were using stolen Social Security numbers in order to work at the company under another person’s identity. The scheme went undetected until the victims began receiving tax bills for working at companies they’d never heard of. It was this episode that inspired him to create the technology needed to catch these kinds of scams before they get out of control.
“The legacy background check industry was built around a single moment in time, even though workforce risk changes every day,” Johnson said. “This investment allows us to move faster toward our goal of equalizing access to modern workforce protection. Fraud signals before a check runs, monitoring after someone is hired and real-time credential visibility should be the foundation of every trust program.”
Yardstik combines artificial intelligence-powered fraud detection algorithms with candidate screening, credential verification and ongoing monitoring within a single platform. It’s designed to integrate with existing applicant tracking systems and HR workflows via a REST application programming interface, which makes it simple for companies to embed trust infrastructure directly into the platforms they’re already using.
Alongside today’s funding news, the company also announced a new Fraud Insights feature that gives HR teams a live view of aggregated risk signals across their entire workforce. This adds to the Continuous Monitoring feature that automatically enrolls all new workers into ongoing, post-hire checks.
Johnson said the need for this kind of platform is clearly apparent, as Yardstik’s data shows that one in 30 job applicants fail a government identity verification. On average, its platform flags around 2,900 incidents each year of job applicants trying to use a flagged or duplicate Social Security number.
“If a motor vehicle report comes back with something disqualifying, you don’t wait for the next renewal cycle to find out,” Johnson said. “If a license lapses the day after someone’s hired, an employer should know about it that day, not at the next annual review. It’s like the difference between a photograph and a live video feed.”
Yardstik says it has sold a growing number of customers on the value it provides. In the last year, it has grown its revenue 149%, and during that time it has a 98% customer retention rate, plus a 99.4% customer satisfaction rating. Its biggest customers include gig economy firms such as TaskRabbit Inc., Gopuff and Liveops Inc. In the case of the latter, which connects businesses to outsourced customer service staff, it was able to flag between 10% and 15% of its job applicants as risks, because they were using fake identities or credentials.
On the back of this growth and funding, Yardstik is becoming more ambitious. It wants to expand its technology with the addition of new fraud prevention defenses that can detect expiring licenses and insurance policies. It also wants to build an Office of Inspector General exclusion monitoring system to detect individuals who are barred from federally funded healthcare programs like Medicare and Medicaid.
Harbert Growth Partners’ Brian Carney said the startup’s impressive growth makes it clear that employers need this technology, because they understand that risk doesn’t disappear the moment they hire someone. “Yardstik’s 98% account retention rate over the past three years shows that customers see real value in the layered protection it provides beyond the background checks at hire,” he said.
