articles.title: Ubisoft releases Heroes of Might and Magic III on Steam, forgets to include the actual game files
articles.text:
Facepalm: Soon after announcing an upcoming remake of its celebrated turn-based strategy game, Ubisoft finally brought the original version of Heroes of Might and Magic III to Steam. However, the first customers to purchase the classic title couldn't launch it for what is likely one of the most embarrassing reasons ever for a Steam release.
The original 1999 version of Heroes of Might and Magic III appeared on Steam for the first time on Tuesday. However, users had to wait an extra day to play the game because Ubisoft accidentally made it available on the storefront without uploading the necessary files.
Customers who installed the turn-based strategy game on day one received only about 23KB of files, including a dummy executable, even though the system requirements claim it needs 1GB of storage space. Warnings quickly spread on the Steam forums and in the game's negative reviews. One review called it 23.49KB of pure nostalgia and the best CMD prompt simulator of 2026. Ubisoft resolved the issue early the following day, responding to one review that simply contained the increasingly relevant quote, "You will own nothing and be happy."
Heroes of Might and Magic III became one of the most well-regarded turn-based tactical RPGs following its 1999 release. However, for years, the only version available on Steam was a 2015 remaster with a mixed reputation. Although its high-resolution graphics make the game more accessible on modern displays, it lacks the original game's two expansions, and some critics argued that free HD mods of the original were already sufficient. The new release, which includes the expansions, brings Steam's offering in line with what has long been available on GOG and other storefronts.
Ubisoft re-released Heroes of Might and Magic III soon after announcing a remake, set for launch sometime next year. While the HD mods and the 2015 version simply render the original 2D graphics at a higher resolution, the remake promises to rebuild everything in the Snowdrop engine that powers Ubisoft's modern games.
Gameplay-related enhancements include a new overhead view that zooms out to display more of the game's maps while simplifying player icons. Battles can also now be viewed from multiple angles while players read newly available tooltips.
Furthermore, players can now assign roles to heroes on the main map, allowing them to automatically perform tasks like collecting resources and transporting troops. Combat can also be automated, and a new wish list screen provides a long-term view of construction projects, while the inventory screen has been overhauled.
For new players, the remake also includes a prologue campaign, which acts as a tutorial. After finishing the campaign, users can generate new maps randomly or download community maps, including maps designed for the original version.
The Heroes of Might and Magic III Remake will be available next year on Steam, the Ubisoft Store, and the Epic Games Store.

articles.title: Resurrected RTX 3060 12GB price jumps 45% in the two months since it was revived
articles.text:
Resurrected RTX 3060 12GB price jumps 45% in the two months since it was revived — 2021-era GPU now costs nearly $500 across most retailers
An uphill battle cut short by a prevailing landslide.
Nvidia ostensibly brought back the RTX 3060 12GB in late June to help gamers cope with the ongoing component crisis. Since most of the world's memory is being routed to expensive AI chips, the RTX 3060 12GB offered gamers a 12GB VRAM pool for what was supposed to be a reasonable price... if only the price remained steady. As of today, this five-year-old GPU now costs almost $500 across the world, which is just as much as the RTX 5060.
MSI's Ventus 2X OC variant of the RTX 3060 12GB launched at just $300 on its online store and $340 on Newegg. It's now listed for $480 in both places. That's a 60% increase in less than two months, compared to its lowest price. Similarly, Asus' Dual V2 OC variant was released with a $330 MSRP, which quickly rose to $360 on Newegg, and the same card is now sitting at $500, constituting a 52% price hike from launch.
The cheapest RTX 3060 12GB right now, the Gigabyte Windforce OC Rev 2.0 model, currently costs $460, up 35% from the $340 it arrived at in late June. The same GPU is listed for 417 GBP on Amazon UK, which converts to $566. In Europe, the cheapest variant is once again Asus' Dual V2 OC, costing 386 EUR on Amazon Germany, or roughly $450; price aggregator Geizhals says it was just 330 EUR a month ago.
In comparison, the RTX 5060, which is two generations newer, can be easily had for around $450 from a bunch of different vendors. That GPU is not only significantly faster but also more efficient, while carrying the latest features such as DLSS multi-frame gen support. In our GPU hierarchy, the 5060 is actually just as powerful as the RTX 3070 at 1080p and 1440p, and it carries the same amount of VRAM, 8GB.
That VRAM capacity is the only thing going for the 3060 12GB at this point, and even with extra memory to utilize, the GPU isn't really capable enough to deliver better performance in games. Plus, you can find better deals on the used market, or even renewed offers from big retailers, so the re-launched RTX 3060 12GB just doesn't make sense from any angle right now, despite its still-decent 1080p chops.
The 3060 is cheaper to produce for Nvidia, thanks to its slower GDDR6 memory compared to the GDDR7 you get on the 5060. It's fabricated on the older, less in-demand 8nm node from Samsung, compared to TSMC's N5, which should also help with yield. But none of those manufacturing leniencies seem to be trickling down to the customer. Even the RTX 5050, which can be had for $300, is faster than the revived RTX 3060 12GB.

articles.title: Why connection is reshaping the next consumer economy | EU-Startups
articles.text:
A love of travel is nothing new in 2026, but it seems that so many people have never loved to travel quite as much as they do today. Travel is now an €9.57 trillion ($11 trillion) global industry, and demand remains remarkably resilient despite pressure on household budgets.
According to Skift’s 2026 State of Travel Report, 88% of travellers still expect to travel in 2026, even as rising prices lead many to adjust their plans. Across major markets, between 67% and 89% of travellers say travel is “extremely” or “very important” to their lifestyle.
The World Cup drove enormous numbers of travellers to North America, and “Euro summer” is now part of the contemporary vernacular. It’s a bona fide travel renaissance, and is pointing to a broader consumer shift.
Why connection is becoming a consumer priority
It’s worth asking why everyone is travelling. Travel has long been one of the strongest ways people create meaningful connections. Exploring new places, sharing unfamiliar experiences and overcoming challenges naturally bring people closer.
As digital interactions take over more of everyday life, and traditional sources of community decline, people seem increasingly intent on finding experiences that lead to real-world relationships. For startups, this creates an opportunity to design products and services around the human desire to belong.
Much of the consumer economy has been designed around convenience and efficiency first, then personalisation. These fundamentals aren’t in decline, but they are making room for a new, social dimension. People want to be brought together, and they’re willing to pay.
The opportunity is to think about community as retention infrastructure: something that gives customers a reason to return beyond the product or service itself. Participation can lead to relationships, relationships to repeat participation, and repeat participation to advocacy and community-driven retention. Experience design is the new feature innovation.
That’s not terribly surprising given the global loneliness crisis. The World Health Organization estimates that one in six people worldwide experiences loneliness, with young people among the most affected groups. At the same time, pervasive digital fatigue is driving a search for alternatives to online lifestyles and constant screen-time, often cited as a major cause of the loneliness epidemic. For founders, this creates space for businesses that provide social infrastructure alongside traditional products and services.
Travel as a model for connection
Travel provides a useful example of how this works. Its rapid post-pandemic recovery showed the resilience of demand, while forcing the industry to rethink what travellers want. The experience is becoming as important as the destination, with travellers increasingly looking for self-discovery, connection and belonging. The same Skift report supports this shift: 43% of travellers consider experiences the most important part of travel.
In travel, consumers are thinking well beyond where to go and asking themselves why they’re going at all. The answers increasingly have to do with a desire for connection.
McKinsey estimates that the global market for travel experiences is worth more than €2.6 trillion ($3 trillion), with domestic and international visitors accounting for roughly 30%, or €944 billion–€1.12 trillion ($1.1–$1.3 trillion) in annual spending. Paid, structured experiences represent around €215–€266 billion ($250–$310 billion) of that spending.
The experience economy moves offline
This shift builds on the “experience economy”, a concept coined by B. Joseph Pine II and James H. Gilmore in 1998, where experiences themselves become a source of value. Today, that value is increasingly social. Run clubs, supper clubs and hobby groups are becoming new social spaces, while businesses built around digital connection are moving offline.
Tinder, which has made more than 100 billion matches, began running IRL events in 2026 after Match Group found that singles are two to four times more likely to engage in low-pressure group experiences than traditional one-to-one dating. Airbnb is expanding Experiences, Strava has passed one million clubs, and in Europe, Timeleft brings six strangers together over dinner each week.
What these models have in common is structured participation. They give people something to do together, making connection feel more natural. None of these companies coordinated, yet they arrived at the same conclusion: people want shared, real-world experiences.
Designing for belonging
The next generation of consumer businesses will need to consider how they create belonging rather than focusing only on transactions. Encouraging participation, repeated interaction and shared experiences can strengthen customer relationships over time.
The wrong lesson is that every company must become a community platform if it wants to survive. That said, founders should ask whether their products create opportunities for connection and memories. A travel company can design group experiences. A fitness brand can build social rituals around activity. A hospitality business can create spaces where customers return for the community as much as the service.
The strongest communities come together through thoughtful experiences and consistent engagement, helped by leaders and facilitators who understand what brings people together. Genuine belonging cannot be manufactured through branding alone. Startups need to deliver real value and create environments where relationships can develop organically.
Europe’s community advantage
Europe already has a strong culture of local communities in diverse cities and experience-led consumer markets, giving its startup ecosystem an advantage. Founders don’t need to create the desire for community since people already appreciate its value in everyday life. From travel and hospitality to wellness, entertainment and social platforms, European founders are building businesses that reflect changing consumer priorities.
The startups that recognise that people aren’t just looking for better products but meaningful opportunities to participate and connect, will set themselves apart. Making belonging integral to the customer experience gives brands the power to turn participation into advocacy and strengthen retention.
This is a serious (and people-driven) competitive advantage.

articles.title: Where can you buy plug-in solar? Argos beats Amazon and Currys to first on-sale kits — as British Gas opens free competition to win £500 solar setups
articles.text:
British Gas starts free competition to win £500 plug-in solar panels — as Argos beats Amazon and Currys to stock the UK's first kits
The plug-in solar revolution is here
- Plug-in solar kits are now appearing for sale in the UK
- British Gas is also running a competition to win £500 kits
- You could save up to £110 a year with one of these kits
The plug-in solar revolution is now underway in the UK, after portable, mains-connecting solar kits became legal — and if you're keen to get involved quickly, British Gas is running a competition to give away 30 of these kits for free.
The competition is for a plug-in unit worth around £500. All you need to do is register your interest in buying a kit on the company's website before the September 16, and the winners will be picked out by the 30th.
"We want to help more people take that first step, which is why we're giving 30 households the chance to win a plug-in solar unit," says British Gas Commercial Director John Evans. "For us, it’s about giving people more choice and control over how they generate and use their energy."
If you're completely new to the tech, it allows you to set up solar panels on balconies and in back gardens, and plug them directly into the mains to offset some electricity costs. Official estimates suggest you could save up to £110 a year, depending on how much sunshine there is in your part of the country.
Now in stock
When it comes to products you can buy rather than win, Argos have been the quickest out of the blocks from what we've seen, and are already stocking options from UKSOL that will set you back from £599 for a 515W setup. Remember you can go up to 2000W with one kit under the UK regulations.
It looks as though other UK retailers won't be far behind. Amazon's UK & Ireland Country Manager John Boumphrey says "we're looking forward to helping customers benefit from this technology", while Currys director Michelle Gorringe-Smith says that the store is working "to make these products available to UK households as soon as possible".
David Wood, CEO at Wickes, says kits will be available online "in the coming weeks". "Making energy-saving technologies easier to access will be an important part of helping people reduce their energy bills and supporting the transition to a lower-carbon future."

articles.title: Traders brought Central American cacao to Georgia 1,000 years ago
articles.text:
A thousand years ago, feasts in what’s now northern Georgia state included cacao from Central America.
Potsherds discarded after an 11th-century feast at Etowah—an Indigenous city just north of what’s now Atlanta—contained traces of cacao, a raw ingredient of chocolate. The chemical residue and ancient DNA reveal that not only did the Mississippian people who built the city have excellent taste, they also had trade connections that reached at least 3,000 kilometers to Central America. And in a sense, chocolate may have helped build the Mississippian mounds.
Ancient dirty dishes
University of South Carolina archaeologist Adam King and his colleagues found fragments of ancient DNA from Theobroma cacao in the inner surfaces of potsherds from long-ago feasts at Etowah. Fruit from the cacao tree contains beans that, when dried and roasted, produce chocolate in all its glorious forms. Cacao only grows in the tropics, which means the nearest actual cacao trees would have been at least a 3,000-kilometer trek away from the woodlands of the eastern US. And that means the Mississippian people who lived in Etowah must have had continent-spanning trade connections.
Etowah was a major center of the Mississippian culture, which flourished in the southeastern US in the centuries before colonization. By 1350 CE, wooden palisades and guard towers ringed a trio of giant earthen mounds (and three smaller ones), the largest of which stood six stories high and covered three acres. Log temples atop the mounds overlooked wide plazas for ball games, ceremonies, and open-air markets. The feast that King and his colleagues studied dates to two centuries before Etowah’s heyday, during the building of the first big platform mound.
After digging up a huge quantity of dirt for that mound (a 19-meter-high mound with a base area of three acres has a volume of… math), people filled in a pit with refuse from community feasts, including a lot of broken pottery, much to the delight of future archaeologists, who categorically love broken pottery. And because nobody washed the dishes before tossing them into the feasting pit, King and his colleagues (in a 2017 study) could analyze the microscopic residue of ancient drinks that had soaked into the ceramic.

articles.title: Rockstar Responds to GTA VI Leaks After Legal Actions Fail
articles.text:
Thursday, August 27th 2026
	
		
	
	
	
Rockstar Responds to GTA VI Leaks After Legal Actions Fail
Take-Two, Rockstar's parent company and publisher of Grand Theft Auto VI, previously responded to the detailed leaks from Cyberleek by issuing subpoenas to Microsoft and Discord in order to identify and track down the anonymous leaker, although that doesn't seem to have helped, since the Cyberleek leaks have continued unabated. Following the legal route, Rockstar Games has publicly addressed the leaks in a recent post on X, stating that the leaks are "heartbreaking" to the team, and apologizing for the game's extended development time frame. 
The leaks shared by Cyberleek revealed much of the studio's closely held secrets about GTA VI, including some of the game's mechanics, the full map, driving and vehicle designs, as well as a number of NPC interactions, and, although there was doubt about the authenticity of the leaks, Rockstar and Take-Two addressing the leaks serves to lend credence to the leaker's claims. Rockstar says in the statement about the leaks that it hopes that "everyone will wait a bit longer to experience the game for themselves on November 19."The launch of Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to have a massive ripple effect on the gaming industry at large, with everyone from indie game developers and peripherals makers expecting changes in consumer buying patterns around November 2026 when GTA VI is slated to launch.

It would be an understatement to say that having videos of Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay leak in this way has been heartbreaking for our team, and this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time. We are very sorry that everything has taken as long as it has—from getting the game finished (nearly there!) to sharing more details and official gameplay, and providing the community with everything you want to know.
We are very excited for everyone to see the extended look tomorrow. It has taken longer than we wanted to get it ready, but as with everything we do, we know we need to exceed your expectations, and we are determined to deliver at the level you expect and deserve. While it is unfortunate that the intended game experience may now be impacted by some spoilers, we hope that everyone will wait a bit longer to experience the game for themselves on November 19.
We want to thank everyone in the community who has reached out with messages of support this past week—your words have meant more to this team than you can imagine. Ultimately, we are making this game for you, and without you, we would not have the privilege of making games.
We look forward to sharing more with you soon.
Sincerely, Rockstar Games

articles.title: Open-Source-Roboter von Hugging Face: Diese Ente läuft, kickt und fährt Rollerskates
articles.text:
25 Zentimeter klein, 800 Gramm leicht, ziemlich bunt und vor allem echt niedlich: Das ist Microduck, der neueste Roboter von Hugging-Face-Tochter Pollen Robotics. Der kleine Roboter, der optisch an eine Ente erinnert, soll den Einstieg in Robotik und KI erleichtern – für Kinder, aber auch für interessierte Erwachsene.
Von Laufen bis Skaten: Diese 7 Tricks beherrscht Microduck
Auf der quietschbunten Website zur Robo-Ente stellt Pollen Robotics das Projekt genauer vor. Microduck wird von 15 Motoren angetrieben und verfügt neben der Kamera über deinen LiDAR-Sensor zur räumlichen Orientierung. Zudem sind zwei weitere Sensoren zur Messung von Beschleunigung und Drehbewegungen verbaut.
Zum Start verfügt Microduck über sieben Fähigkeiten beziehungsweise Tricks, die direkt nach dem Auspacken Spaß versprechen sollen. Neben den ganz grundlegenden Fähigkeiten, zu laufen, zu stehen und zu sitzen und im Falle eines Sturzes wieder aufzustehen, kann der Mini-Roboter auch einen Ball kicken, mit seinem Schnabel Gegenstände greifen und aufheben sowie auf Rollerskates durch die Gegend düsen.
Da ist natürlich noch lange nicht Schluss, denn Microduck ist dafür gedacht, dass Nutzer:innen ihm eigene Tricks beibringen können. Das funktioniert ohne Programmierkenntnisse oder komplexes Setup.
Microduck: So trainierst du den Roboter im Simulator
Die einfachste Art, dem kleinen Roboter Neues beizubringen, ist der Microduck-Simulator von Hugging Face. Über den Browser lassen sich Bewegungsabläufe testen und festlegen, die dann auf Microduck übertragen werden können. Feintuning ist laut Pollen Robotics ebenso möglich wie das Teilen mit der Community. Das heißt, dass mit der Zeit wohl auch Tricks anderer Anwender:innen zur Verfügung stehen werden – vorausgesetzt, das Projekt findet Anklang.
So weit das Potenzial für Einsteiger:innen, zu denen beispielsweise auch Lehrer:innen gehören könnten, die mit ihren Schüler:innen praktisch mit Robotik und KI arbeiten möchten. Der Open-Source-Ansatz bietet aber natürlich noch mehr Möglichkeiten. Wer des Programmierens mächtig ist, kann den Code einsehen und verändern, also eigene Tricks schreiben.
Preise, Specs und Liefertermin: Das wissen wir über Microduck
Abgesehen von den bereits erwähnten technischen Details, stellt der Hersteller auch noch andere Angaben bereit. Verbaut ist ein Rockchip RK3566 mit KI-Accelerator; der Arbeitsspeicher ist ein Gigabyte groß, der Speicher umfasst 32 Gigabyte. Dank Mikrofon und Lautsprecher kann der Roboter akustisch kommunizieren. Die Verbindung mit dem enthaltenen Game-Controller und dem Computer erfolgt per Wi-Fi und Bluetooth. Der 2.600 Milliamperestunden große Akku verspricht rund eine Stunde Laufzeit, je nach Nutzung.
Microduck kann ab sofort in vier Farben über die Projekt-Website für 399 US-Dollar vorbestellt, wobei Pollen Robitics verspricht, dass der kleine Entenroboter noch vor Weihnachten 2026 ausgeliefert wird. Zunächst werden nur Nordamerika und Europa abgedeckt.

articles.title: Barret Zoph, the Thinking Machines co-founder ousted before joining OpenAI, is now at Google | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The game of musical chairs for AI executives continues. Barret Zoph, a co-founder of the AI startup Thinking Machines who left the company earlier this year to rejoin OpenAI, has found yet another job.
Zoph spent two years at OpenAI and left in October 2024 to co-found Thinking Machines with Mira Murati, who had left the AI lab the month prior. In January, Zoph and another Thinking Machines co-founder, Luke Metz, quite dramatically departed from the startup to return to OpenAI. It was later revealed that Zoph had been fired.
His return didn’t quite stick. Zoph spent only five months at OpenAI, where he was tasked with heading AI enterprise sales. He left the company in June. And now we know where he landed.
Zoph has taken a position as vice president of research at Google (which happens to be another company where he previously worked). “We look forward to Barret returning to Google and bringing his RL and post-training expertise to Gemini,” a Google spokesperson told the Wall Street Journal.
TechCrunch reached out to OpenAI and Google for more information.
It’s not always easy to divine why tech executives seem to be spending less time in their roles. The turnover rate in the AI industry is high, and it’s been especially high at OpenAI — a company that, despite readying itself for an IPO and being one of the most powerful presences in the tech world, has lost a lot of critical staff over the last eight months. The turnover of high-level executives — from the departure of its COO to the recent loss of one of its top data center execs — has left onlookers scratching their heads.
This story has been updated to include the fact that Zoph was fired from Thinking Machines.

articles.title: Agentic AI Success Relies On Excellent Human Scaffolding
articles.text:
Before deploying agentic AI into a chip design, engineers must define the domain ontology and agentic harness. Fundamental engines are still crucial.
Key Takeaways:
Experts At The Table: Semiconductor Engineering sat down to discuss recent developments and challenges when using agentic AI for chip design, with Matt Graham, senior group director of verification software product management at Cadence; Harrison Balistreri, head of business development and strategic partnerships at ChipAgents; Alexander Petr, senior director and portfolio manager at Keysight EDA; Sathish Balasubramanian, head of product for EDA AI at Siemens EDA; and Anand Thiruvengadam, executive director and head of AI product management at Synopsys. This roundtable discussion was held behind closed doors at the recent Design Automation Conference. What follows are excerpts of that discussion.
Fig. 1: L-R: Synopsys’ Thiruvengadam; Keysight’s Petr; Cadence’s Graham; ChipAgents’ Balistreri; and Siemens’ Balasubramanian.
SE: A lot has changed in the past year in terms of agentic AI capabilities. A year ago, people would say, ‘Agentic AI is going to be useful for this, but it can’t do this.’ Now, what people said it probably couldn’t do, such as full-flow design, it’s now doing to some extent. The points where humans are definitely needed are getting smaller and smaller. What are your thoughts on where the design industry is at with this?
Balasubramanian: Compared to last year, we are talking more about orchestration of different flows or sub-agents. Customers are getting a handle on what it is. I’m seeing a lot more automation on the front end — design, mainly RTL generation and sign-off, or debug. They are all creating sub-flow agents. The end goal is an end-to-end, push-button flow. Give us a spec, get a GDS II or a chip out. That’s the main end goal. I don’t think we are there yet, but customers are using agentic AI in production for specific pain points with a lot of manual intervention and small manual tasks. That’s getting much more automated with agents.
Balistreri: We’ve progressed quite a bit, but you have to deliver the agentic AI in a certain way to get that progression. We think a lot about full-flow autonomous outcomes, and we’ve delivered this for specific engineering flows. Think of us as push-button coverage closure with multi-agent swarms. This is quite different than the point acceleration that you saw last year, with an agent for this, an agent for that, and generic use of cloud flow. To get true full-flow autonomous outcomes, you need several layers. You need organizational context. You need to understand the flow specific to that customer and how they do that engineering flow, and map how you use agents to that flow. You need an agentic harness tuned for these chip-designed tasks; then you can co-optimize a model with that harness to run these flows efficiently and specifically to the harness. We’ll come back to this idea of critical errors, too. You cannot have a full flow, fully autonomous [system] without certainty that you’re not introducing critical errors. What we’ve progressed to now is delivering this full-flow autonomous outcome without critical errors. But it takes a lot, and we’re working very closely with each customer to map it.
Graham: One thing that’s the same from last year to this year at DAC that I’m really excited about is that we do see a very vibrant startup community in EDA. A few years ago, it was slim pickings, and this is fantastic. This is great for the industry in general. This is great for innovation, and historically this is how EDA has grown — both organically with the big guys and through startups, regardless of whether their technology advances the industry or gets absorbed by the big guys through acquisition. I’m happy to see that continue. As far as what’s different, last year we talked about agentic AI almost exclusively in the front end — RTL, test bench, and things like that. Certainly, that has advanced, but we’re now seeing it in analog and mixed-signal. We’re seeing it in full custom. We’re seeing it through digital implementation, even into circuit board and packaging. Last year’s push-button flows were primarily in the front end. This year we’re talking much more about genuine end-to-end flows and even expanding into multi-physics and beyond just the IC itself, or beyond just the ones and zeros. We’re seeing the entire industry grow, and agentic AI is now moving into the full chip-and-system flow.
Petr: The biggest change was around February this year, when OpenAI released a reasoning framework. Since then, we have been talking about super agents or agent swarms. Last year, we talked about building a single agent that can understand a unique domain. That is very time-consuming because it means tailoring engineering knowledge to a framework that understands what needs to be done. From what I see, a lot of effort is still in the digital domain, where you still have code as a base. The agents are horrendously good at coding. Period. They understand code. They speak Python naturally. As soon as you go into a domain where people still use UI and a mouse to do most of their work, this is where we still struggle. To Matt’s point, right now what we’re enabling is multiphysics. We’re trying to enable all our core simulation technologies, all the glue between the different tasks, which are still very engineering-heavy, to get to the multiphysics package solution. Everything we see nowadays — if you look where the investment goes, the CapEx goes —is multi-chip technologies. It’s the AI stack. It’s photonics. It’s not just a single chip anymore. It doesn’t scale. Moore’s Law on that side is flat, so the scale comes from integration. Enabling all those pieces that enable integration is the hard part now. We see a lot of design agents that go beyond RTL and other things. We see engines that were ultra slow in the past being enabled through AI technologies, and now we can put an agent on top and integrate it into an agentic framework. The call is still out on whether one will rule all, or if there will be multiple. A lot of people here are fighting over who will rule the world through super agents or frameworks. So are the startups. If you ask me what’s going to change next year, there will be an awakening at some point about how this will pan out. Will there be one, or will there be multiple, or will each company pick its own?
Thiruvengadam: From a broad industry point of view, there are multiple things happening. There’s marked acceleration in some of these trends that started a few years ago. Microsoft, Nvidia, and many other ecosystem players have essentially enabled four pieces of technology that have fueled some of the innovations that the others at this table are talking about. The EDA vendors have leveraged that. This year is pivotal because task-level automation is great right now. Workflow automation is great. But we are truly at the point where we see long-running agentic workflows or AI systems as a reality because we’ve demonstrated it. This is good for the broader industry because you can now think about fully autonomous execution with minimal human supervision — within human guardrails, as needed. We have end-to-end workflows that can run end-to-end in a secure environment. That’s happening as a reality. It’s a significant evolution. The second thing is business outcomes. We are talking about the technology, and it is great. Yes, long-running agentic workflows are here, but on the business outcome side we are starting to see that, as well. Last year, we talked about some very initial gains, early gains, early trials, in some very specific domains such as verification. Now we have fairly broad-based outcomes established by customers, including verification implementation. Analog, we’ve seen, as well. On the system side, with structures, CMT (common-mode transient), and thermal, we are seeing real, tangible gains for our customers. With these long-running capabilities, it’s not just point-level task automation. If you run a fairly complex end-to-end flow through a long-running system, you see the outcomes we expect from long-running agents, such as significant productivity gains and improved software quality. So technology has progressed, yes, but so has business — actual value outcomes for customers. We’re seeing positive ROI.
SE: What does the engineer need to do before deploying an agent? How is that changing the setup before a chip is designed, using the engineer’s preferred EDA tools?
Balasubramanian: Ontology is the key thing that an engineer needs to do right now. That is where we are seeing people spend more time. With agents, no one worries about scripting or automation. They’re thinking more about design and architecture. ‘How else can I improve a certain sort of architecture?’ Engineers are thinking more about, ‘What are my bounds on PPA?’ or whatever their metrics are, and what domain they are in. Then they’re figuring out, ‘What are all the different parameters that I want the agents to work on?’ Given that we talked about long-running agents and swarm agents, they’re letting the agents and LLM-driven automation explore a design space to find the best result and ROI for their particular design. The important starting point for the engineer is clear domain knowledge — not being constrained by the previous design where I want to add margin and so forth — but thinking about what really makes designs successful and how they fit into the bigger picture. After that, it’s all a matter of how you drive the agentic AI. We are seeing some companies use it in ways that deliver huge benefits. Instead of iterative design improvements, agents are delivering a big step function in implementation.
Thiruvengadam: In terms of the role of humans, there are two key things — humans will be specifying the design intent. That’s where specs come in. That’s a huge role that I still see happening. More important, with all this capable automation and long-running agents, is that humans are spending a lot of time on verification, as in verifiability and validating the outcomes. Those are the two big functions that will not go away. What I see is a marked shift toward human engineers spending a lot of time on verifiability, and that ties into how these systems are architected and designed. Verifiability can be done in different ways. A very intuitive user experience for verifiability is key. You need to present something that’s easy to digest and verify. Without that actual deployment, that’s an orthogonal point. Agentic flows have to be designed with the right checkpoints, user interface, and intuitiveness. All of that needs to be hand in hand. It’s not just somebody looking at a verbose report and saying, ‘Okay, what do I do next?’ Agents need to present outcomes in a way humans can quickly validate and move on. Otherwise, you’ll create yet another bottleneck.
Balistreri: I would frame it differently, because if you’re just producing things for humans to verify, you’re not delivering on the autonomous piece. That’s what is missing in ROI today for most agents and most flows. To deliver on the autonomous piece before engineers deploy a solution like ours, they have to trust the process’ outcomes. The gates aren’t put in the flows themselves. If you’re using a generic LLM, or you’re just piping an existing LLM into your solution, and that powers your agents, you’re using a very thin agent awareness in the agent loop that Anthropic or OpenAI has picked for you. We’ve put the trust in the agent loops themselves. We’ve reconstructed agent loops from scratch in a way that prevents critical errors with 100% certainty. When you deploy the agents, you know they will not produce certain classes of error. I want to share one example — waivers in your coverage model. We’ve found that most agents can decide to waive coverage when they shouldn’t, creating a massive human review burden. We’ve heard from one top-five customer at TSMC that their biggest pain point is when their engineers use Claude code, especially their junior engineers. They’re creating the equivalent of AI slop with all of these errors in it. But I’d say it goes even further into the harness you’re using and the agent loops themselves. In our full-flow autonomous coverage closure, we have to use gates built into the agent loops themselves to prevent you from waiving coverage on a cover bin, and to prevent you from saying you’ll never converge on coverage for this solution, or things like that.
Thiruvengadam: I completely agree. If you’re talking about fully autonomous long-running systems, then yes, the self-validation is built into the harness orchestration loops themselves. No disagreement there. The point is we are still early in broad-scale deployment of long-running systems — that’s the key. So verifiability will still be there. I’m not saying a fully autonomous end-to-end workflow, which you think of as a black box, will still have elaborate, laborious human checkpoints. That’s not the point. The point is that even if it’s a fully autonomous verification flow, which we have demonstrated, or a debug, or an implementation flow, critical checkpoints are still required for human engineers, and that’s the key because the trust factor isn’t there yet. At some point, it will hopefully evolve to remove all the guardrails and maybe have fairly discrete, less-frequent checkpoints.
Balasubramanian: That’s where the ontology matters. In terms of waivers, customers have been doing waivers for a long time. It’s nothing new for them, but we are trying to help them do it faster. That’s the whole idea for people who are doing tape-outs. For ontology, how are you going to tie up the harness with the existing ontology across the entire flow, not just one particular thing? For example, you can have coverage on one verification flow, but a separate IP team will be doing their own thing. A lot of new data and modifications are coming in, so you need a full picture. Ontology is very important. You can’t just be on one single domain and say, ‘Okay, I’m going to be just covering this one.’ It needs to touch everything, wherever all the key domains are that are going to be coming into that part, and also going downstream. That’s going to be key. On the verification side, I agree about AI slop. We call that design slop. The biggest challenge we see, even on the verification side, is it’s not just humans verifying. You still need the engines at some point. What we are seeing is customers get 10 scenarios coming in, and based on their domain knowledge, the verification team picks 5. But those 5 still need to go through the engine layer for sign-off because LLMs aren’t deterministic. You can add guardrails, skills, and everything else, but as you go down the stack toward the silicon, you really need to figure it out. That’s where the humans come into play to narrow down your scenarios, and then you’ve got to go through the sign-off engines and make it mathematically accurate, so that the chip doesn’t fail. At the end of the day, you’ve got to make the chip.
Graham: We can’t emphasize enough that the fundamental engines are still very deterministic and mathematically accurate. At some point, we need them because the cost of failure is too high. Whether it’s in verification, implementation, analog simulation, or signal integrity for the board and package, the integration between the AI and where [the engines] meet is still critical. That integration plays a major role in setup and preparation. Taking a slightly different direction, another difference I’m seeing more than last year — in terms of preparation before you deploy AI — is that token budget has suddenly become a meaningful line item for all of our customers and, I’m assuming, for all other companies as well.
Leave a Reply

articles.title: How Nigeria’s TechAble is bridging the digital inclusion gap for young people with disabilities - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigeria’s TechAble is a an inclusive digital skills and youth empowerment initiative focused on expanding access to technology, STEM education, and future-ready skills for young people in Africa, particularly those with disabilities and from underserved communities.
Formed in 2024 as an initiative of Deafzion Foundation, a Nigeria-based social impact organisation focused on disability rights, inclusive education, and youth empowerment, TechAble came about in response to growing digital exclusion among young people with disabilities.
Through bootcamps, workshops, and community-based programmes, TechAble equips learners with digital literacy, data and AI fundamentals, problem-solving, leadership, and employability skills, while also advocating for inclusive technology ecosystems in Africa.
We identified a major gap in disability-inclusive tech education. While many digital skills programmes exist, very few are intentionally designed to accommodate learners with disabilities or operate within inclusive learning environments,” Emmanuel Izuchukwu Osita, executive director of the Deafzion Foundation and TechAble lead, told Disrupt Africa.
“TechAble differentiates itself by embedding accessibility, inclusive pedagogy, assistive technologies, and psychosocial support into digital skills training.”
Currently funded through grants, partnerships, donations, and in-kind support, the initiative has already trained over 40 youths with disabilities across Nigeria in digital and AI skills, and secured partnerships with organisations such as LEAP Africa, Dow, Windows on America, and state disability agencies.
“Uptake has been strong and organic. We have recorded high interest from students, parents, schools, and partner organisations. Participation rates are high, with strong retention and engagement, particularly among girls with disabilities,” said Osita.
TechAble currently operates in Nasarawa State, Abuja, and Plateau State.
“We plan to expand across other Nigerian states and into selected African countries through partnerships with schools, NGOs, and development agencies,” Osita said.
“Key challenges include limited funding, accessibility costs, infrastructure constraints in underserved areas, and low awareness around disability-inclusive tech education. However, strong community support, partnerships, and demand have enabled us to overcome early-stage challenges and continue scaling.”

articles.title: Google Photos : vos photos supprimées pourraient bientôt disparaitre deux fois plus vite
articles.text:
Supprimer un souvenir par erreur sur Google Photos est toujours un peu stressant, mais le filet de sécurité de la corbeille est toujours là. Actuellement, les fichiers sauvegardés dans le cloud profitent d’une période de 60 jours dans la corbeille avant d’être effacés définitivement, tandis que les éléments non sauvegardés sur Google Photos (qui sont simplement sur le stockage de votre appareil) disparaissent au bout de 30 jours.
Bientôt plus que 30 jours pour tous les fichiers Google Photos ?
Google veut unifier le fonctionnement de sa corbeille. Le code de la dernière version de l’application indique clairement que le délai passera de 60 jours à 30 jours pour l’ensemble des contenus, y compris ceux que vous avez sauvegardés dans le cloud. Deux fois moins de temps donc, ce qui est déjà le cas des fichiers qui sont « simplement » stockés sur votre appareil, mais qui apparaissent également sur Google Photos.
Cette modification n’est pas encore active, car la découverte vient, une fois n’est pas coutume, d’une analyse d’un fichier APK de Google Photos. Aucune communication officielle n’a précisé le calendrier de déploiement, même s’il est fort à parier que l’entreprise préviendra ses utilisateurs bien avant de changer définitivement ce délai (comptez sur nous pour vous en informer le cas échéant).
Simplifier l’expérience et alléger les serveurs
Harmoniser cette durée de conservation des fichiers évite de jongler entre deux règles différentes selon le statut de sauvegarde des fichiers. En réduisant le délai à 30 jours pour tout le monde, l’application gagne en cohérence et évite aussi aux utilisateurs de s’emmêler les pinceaux, même si tout le monde ne connait pas forcément cette règle des 30 jours ou 60 jours pour la corbeille de Google Photos.
Réduire cette fenêtre pourrait aussi permettre à Google de grappiller de précieux espaces de stockage sur ses serveurs. À l’heure où les coûts du matériel et des composants pèsent lourd sur l’industrie, vider plus rapidement les corbeilles de millions de comptes allège mécaniquement la charge technique et financière de l’infrastructure. Si cette nouvelle règle est mise en place, vous n’aurez donc plus que 30 jours pour changer d’avis si vous souhaitez restaurer des photos ou vidéos que vous avez mises par erreur dans la corbeille.

articles.title: JEEViKA Sudha Bikri Kendra: Rs 60,000 Grant for Women in 8,053 Panchayats
articles.text:
JEEViKA Sudha Bikri Kendra: Rs 60,000 Grant for Women in 8,053 Panchayats
BRLPS will open JEEViKA Sudha Bikri Kendras in all 8,053 gram panchayats of Bihar under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana. Selected women get up to Rs 60,000 in assistance, add Rs 15,000 of their own, and run a Sudha dairy outlet with training and COMFED supply support.
In Bihar's villages, the picture is changing fast. It is no longer only about looking for employment, but also about building one's own business. The Bihar government's JEEViKA initiative has played an important role in this change. Now that same campaign is being given another major direction.
As part of this, the Bihar Rural Livelihoods Promotion Society (BRLPS) issued an order on 6 July 2026. Under it, JEEViKA Sudha Bikri Kendras (Sudha booths) will be opened in all 8,053 gram panchayats of Bihar. This initiative will be taken forward under the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana, in collaboration between JEEViKA and COMFED.
The special feature of this initiative is that village women are not just being given financial help. An effort is being made to connect them to a ready-made business model. They will have their own shop. They will have Sudha Dairy products. They will receive business training. And most importantly, the entire effort will move forward on the strength of JEEViKA's strong network of women.
The Bihar government will give a loan of Rs 60,000
The biggest aspect of this scheme is its large scope. Opening sales centres across Bihar's 8,053 gram panchayats means Sudha Dairy's network will reach closer to the villages. This can give rural customers better local access to milk and dairy products. At the same time, a new avenue of earnings will open up for women.
According to the BRLPS order, a selected woman beneficiary will be given financial assistance of a maximum of Rs 60,000 to open a Sudha booth. This money can be used for essential requirements such as a deep freezer, visi cooler, branding, preparing the shop, and purchasing products. In addition, a beneficiary contribution of Rs 15,000 has been set. That is, the beneficiary will have to put in this amount herself. This sum will be used as working capital. In this way, a total of up to Rs 75,000 may be spent on one centre.
In this model, along with the government's support, the woman's own participation has also been built in. That is why it can be seen not merely as an assistance scheme, but as an initiative to set up a small business. The woman will run the shop. She will handle sales. She will engage with customers. And as the business grows, she will also have the opportunity to increase her income.
The application and selection process has also been laid down. Interested eligible women will have to apply through the designated online portal. After that, documents and eligibility will be verified. To ensure transparency in the selection process, a provision for an online random lottery has also been included.
What is JEEViKA?
JEEViKA began in 2006 as a pilot project, with the support of the World Bank. At that time, poverty and economic exclusion were widespread in Bihar, and women's participation was extremely low. In 2011, it was expanded across the entire state under the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM), now known as DAY-NRLM. The scheme has now reached every block and every panchayat in Bihar.
A special feature of this scheme is its three-tier structure. In a Self Help Group (SHG), 10 to 15 women come together to form a group. These SHGs then come together to form a Village Organisation (VO), and these in turn form a Cluster Level Federation (CLF).
The responsibility of running and expanding this scheme has been taken up by BRLPS CEO-cum-State Mission Director Himanshu Sharma (IAS). In an interview with YourStory Founder and CEO Shradha Sharma, he explained how this scheme, which began as an experiment, has today become a rural economy of more than Rs 1 lakh crore, and that too under the leadership of women.
Himanshu Sharma said, "This is not a relief scheme. This is a story of self respect, economic strength and collective trust."
The most unique thing about JEEViKA is its trust based loan system. Here there is no paperwork, no guarantee required, and no need for a credit score.
Himanshu Sharma went on to explain, "A woman comes to an SHG meeting, asks for Rs 5,000, and gets immediate approval, because the group trusts her. This is not a model dependent on subsidy or CSR. Women are not asking for freebies. They are asking for loans and repaying them with pride. This is real empowerment."
According to the BRLPS CEO, the 99.5% loan repayment rate shows that women do not regard this as the government's money but as their own group's capital, and they protect it.
A network of 1.40 crore JEEViKA Didis
JEEViKA's greatest strength is its grassroots network of women. Over the past nearly two decades, this initiative has become a major means of connecting rural women in Bihar to economic activity through Self Help Groups (SHGs).
According to BRLPS's 74th Quarterly Progress Report, 11,88,130 SHGs had been formed in Bihar by March 2026. Women from 1.40 crore families had joined these groups. In addition, a network of 73,515 VOs and 1,684 CLFs had also been built.
This figure shows that JEEViKA does not merely have the administrative structure to implement a scheme. It has a large and active network of women present in the villages. This very network can become a major strength in bringing an initiative like JEEViKA Sudha Bikri Kendra to the ground. The organisation has also placed emphasis on promoting rural women led enterprises and community based enterprises. In other words, the story of the new Sudha booths is not starting from zero. Behind it lies a social and economic structure built up over years.
Bihar moving from women's employment to women's entrepreneurship
Among the Bihar government's women focused schemes, JEEViKA's role has grown steadily stronger. Through the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana, the emphasis has been on giving women financial assistance to start their own employment. Now JEEViKA Sudha Bikri Kendra appears to connect that same thinking to a structured business opportunity.
Its significance grows further because women do not just receive capital to start their own business. They get the chance to work with a well known brand. Sudha Dairy has long been a familiar name among people in Bihar. COMFED, the Bihar State Milk Co-operative Federation Ltd, began work on dairy development in Bihar in 1983 under the Operation Flood programme. Today it sells milk and many dairy products under the Sudha brand.
According to COMFED, its network includes a large number of cooperative institutions and retail points for milk collection and sales. This can create a strong foundation of supply and market for JEEViKA Sudha Bikri Kendra. COMFED's plans have also emphasised expanding the marketing network in rural and urban areas.
In that sense, JEEViKA and COMFED coming together is like combining the strengths of both institutions. On one side is a vast network of women. On the other is a strong dairy brand and supply system.
From the village shop to the village economy
The real strength of JEEViKA Sudha Bikri Kendra may be visible in its local impact. When milk, curd, paneer, ghee, ice cream and other Sudha Dairy products become easily available in a panchayat, customers will get convenience at the local level. At the same time, for the woman running the shop, an opportunity for daily sales and regular income will be created.
This means the sales centres will not remain limited to being small shops selling milk. With the right location, good sales and better management, these centres can become small but significant retail hubs for dairy products in the rural market.
The official BRLPS order also speaks of giving priority to locations where footfall is good and products can be sold easily. Arrangements have also been made for training beneficiaries and for monitoring the operation of the centre after it is set up.
This is what makes this initiative special. The government is not merely talking about opening shops. It is also preparing the path to give women the infrastructure, training and institutional support needed to run a shop.
In the end, JEEViKA Sudha Bikri Kendra should not be viewed merely through the number of 8,053 new shops. It is an example of advancing women's entrepreneurship in Bihar's rural areas.
The vast network of women that JEEViKA has built over the years is now being connected to new business opportunities, and this is an important step in that direction. COMFED's Sudha brand links this model to the market. The Bihar government's Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana gives it an economic base. And the gram panchayat level network takes it to people's doorsteps.
If this model succeeds as expected, a new picture could emerge in Bihar's villages. On one side will be a woman handling the responsibilities of home and family. On the other side, that same woman will have her own shop. That is, she will be the owner of her business. And she will have the opportunity to grow her income.
This is the very change that the Bihar government's women focused schemes are trying to bring to the ground. JEEViKA Sudha Bikri Kendra could become the next big step in connecting this change to everyday life in the village.

articles.title: Manchester Airports Group says hackers stole travelers' data
articles.text:
The Manchester Airports Group (MAG) disclosed that hackers breached its systems and stole customer data, including Wi-Fi sign-ups from Manchester, Stansted, and East Midlands airports.
The intruder did not access customer payment details, and the attack had no impact on airport operations, the company said.
A statement from the company today notes that the exfiltrated data also "relates to car park, lounge and Fast Track bookings." The list of compromised details includes customers' email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registration numbers, and postcodes.
“The incident has not resulted in any operational disruption,” assured the organization, adding that “Airport operations remain unaffected and customer parking services continue to operate normally.”
Out of an abundance of caution, MAG has temporarily suspended its online “Manage My Booking” service and is instead directing travelers to use its phone line.
MAG is the UK’s largest airport operator, and owner of Manchester, London Stansted and East Midlands airports, which together handle over 66 million passengers yearly.
The company employs 40,000 people and generates annual revenue of £1.5 billion.
After discovering the intrusion, MAG says that it moved quickly to contain it, restricting access to the affected systems, engaging with external experts, and notifying law enforcement.
Potentially exposed customers are advised to remain alert for suspicious communications and avoid clicking on links arriving via email or SMS.
MAG stresses that it will never ask customers for payment card information, banking details, or passwords. Customers should reject and report to the authorities any attempts to obtain personal, financial, or other sensitive information.
People are also encouraged to follow NCSC’s post-breach recommendations to stay safe.
The company says it has contacted impacted customers directly, but did not disclose the number of affected individuals.
Local media reported that data of up to 8.9 million travelers may have been exposed, citing private MAG statements; however, BleepingComputer has not been able to confirm the figure.
At the time of writing, no ransomware or data extortion groups have claimed the attack publicly.

articles.title: Galaxy S27 Pro : Samsung préparerait un "mini Ultra" pour faire mal aux prochains iPhone
articles.text:
Galaxy S27 Pro : Samsung préparerait un "mini Ultra" pour faire mal aux prochains iPhone
Samsung s’apprêterait à bousculer sa gamme Galaxy S avec un quatrième modèle. Plus compact qu’un Ultra, mais presque aussi ambitieux, le Galaxy S27 Pro a déjà commencé son effeuillage.
Alors que Samsung vient de dévoiler un Galaxy S26 FE solide mais au prix trop élevé pour être recommandable à son lancement, la série S27 pourrait marquer une rupture avec la formule répétée depuis 2020. En plus des modèles S27, S27+ et S27 Ultra, une nouveauté pourrait faire son apparition : un S27 Pro, plus compact et maniable que l’Ultra, mais dépourvu de S Pen.
Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra
Un Ultra qui tient mieux dans la main
Les rendus publiés par le célèbre informateur OnLeaks, basés sur des fichiers de conception, évoquent un boîtier de 154,06 x 73,77 x 7,95 mm, contre 163,76 x 78,25 x 7,97 mm pour l’Ultra. Son écran mesurerait environ 6,6 pouces, entre les 6,3 pouces du S27 et les 6,9 pouces du S27 Ultra.
Le changement le plus visible se trouverait au dos. Le Pro reprendrait le large plateau photo du futur S27 Ultra, un choix qui rappelle les derniers iPhone Pro, alors que les S27 et S27+ conserveraient une disposition plus classique. Les angles seraient aussi plus doux pour améliorer la prise en main. En dessous, Samsung aurait déplacé le haut-parleur et le microphone, tandis qu’aucun emplacement pour le stylet n’apparaît. Un anneau magnétique destiné à la recharge sans fil est également attendu. Quant au rouge cerise aperçu sur les rendus, rien ne garantit qu’il sera commercialisé.
Des performances presque sans compromis
Côté fiche technique, les rumeurs parlent d’un Snapdragon haut de gamme de nouvelle génération ou d’un Exynos 2700 selon les marchés, avec 12 à 16 Go de RAM et 256 Go à 1 To de stockage. La batterie atteindrait quant à elle 5200 mAh, possiblement avec un usage mesuré du silicium-carbone. Le volet photo resterait par ailleurs très ambitieux avec un capteur principal de 200 mégapixels. Le téléobjectif pourrait toutefois être moins musclé que celui de l’Ultra, avec un capteur 12 Mpx et un zoom x3 face à un 50 Mpx x5. Enfin, Samsung prévoirait d’étendre sa technologie d'affichage Privacy display aux quatre modèles de la gamme, dont le S27 Pro.
Concernant son positionnement tarifaire, la rumeur situe le Galaxy S27 Pro autour de 1300 $ avec une présentation des quatre modèles attendue entre janvier et février 2027. Bien entendu, le conditionnel reste de rigueur, rien n’étant officiel pour le moment : dimensions, composants, prix et même certaines fonctions peuvent encore évoluer.

articles.title: OpenAI Agents Exploited Linux Kernel Flaw on Company’s Own Systems
articles.text:
Around the time some OpenAI models escaped their testing environment and hacked Hugging Face, some agents exploited a Linux kernel vulnerability to escalate privileges on OpenAI’s own systems.
This was mentioned in a report published by OpenAI this week to detail the incident in which its models hacked Hugging Face in July. The AI giant’s investigation found that agents used an unauthorized makeshift message board to communicate and plan their actions, including encouraging one another to hack what they correctly guessed were real systems rather than test environments.
Rogue agents went beyond Hugging Face, hacking other organizations as well. However, OpenAI’s new report also details unauthorized actions conducted within its own network.
Shortly after the Hugging Face incident came to light, OpenAI revealed that its models had discovered and exploited a zero-day vulnerability in JFrog’s Artifactory package registry manager.
In addition, the new report reveals that on July 19, unrelated to the Hugging Face hack, some agents exploited a known Linux kernel vulnerability, CVE-2026-53362, to escalate privileges within an OpenAI environment.
Agents identified that the Linux kernel version on their underlying machine included a recent, public common vulnerability and exposure (CVE). The agents retrieved the exploit for that CVE (CVE-2026-53362), customized it to succeed on their underlying machine, and leveraged the exploit to escalate privilege. This allowed the agents to act outside one Artifactory container and to obtain root access on the underlying worker node. This then allowed the agents to move laterally throughout the connected environment.
CISA on Thursday added both the JFrog flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-66384, and the Linux kernel bug to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.
The JFrog product weakness should be patched by federal agencies by September 10, but CISA recommends that organizations patch CVE-2026-53362 by August 30.
There do not appear to be any other reports describing exploitation of the Linux kernel vulnerability in the wild. However, the OpenAI incident demonstrates its potential value to attackers, which may be why CISA has decided to add it to its KEV catalog.
CISA’s KEV list currently includes more than two dozen Linux kernel vulnerabilities.

articles.title: J'ai listé toutes les voitures de la vidéo de GTA 6 : des références mythiques et une absence qui m’interroge — Frandroid
articles.text:
À moins de vivre dans une grotte, vous avez évidemment entendu parler de l’arrivée prochaine de GTA 6, probablement le jeu vidéo le plus attendu de l’année.
Hier soir, Rockstar a diffusé un premier gameplay de 26 minutes sur Netflix puis sur YouTube (provoquant des pannes massives), de quoi avoir un premier avant-goût du nouvel épisode de la franchise.
De quoi inspirer à mes collègues des premiers retours et analyses ; de mon côté, j’ai joué à mon jeu favori : repérer les voitures présentes dans le jeu.
Une célébration de l’automobile américaine
Évidemment, GTA 6 ne déroge pas à la règle des précédents Grand Theft Auto : pour des raisons de droits et de licence, les voitures du jeu n’existent pas réellement. Pas de Mercedes ou de Ford, par exemple, mais des créations parfois très fortement inspirées de modèles actuels ou passés.
Débutons à la sixième minute où Jason et Lucia, les deux protagonistes du jeu, roulent à tombeau ouvert à bord de ce qui ressemble à une Chevrolet Chevelle de 1972.
Un peu plus tard, le couple décide de se rendre à une soirée au volant d’un ersatz de BMW Série 3 Cabriolet (E30), permettant au passage de découvrir un mécanisme fonctionnel de la capote. On reverra cette simili-BMW un peu plus tard.
Gaming ou études, pourquoi choisir ? Équipement tech, PC et écrans : profitez de jusqu’à -40 % pour la rentrée chez PcComponentes ! Livraison offerte dès 50 € et garantie remplacement 24 h jusqu’au 12 septembre.
Le long de cette promenade, des voitures contemporaines roulent dans la rue. Des grands pick-ups (inspirés de l’omniprésent Ford F-150 ou du Toyota Tacoma), des muscle cars (Chevrolet Camaro, Ford Mustang, Dodge Charger et Challenger) et des SUV full size (Chevrolet Suburban, Dodge Durango, Range Rover et BMW X5) sont visibles.
À 9:17, une voisine manifestement peu aimable abîme une muscle-car typiquement années 1970, puisant son inspiration dans les Buick Skylark ou les Chevelle (une inspiration qu’on retrouvera un peu plus tard, où un malheureux conducteur se la fera voler après un braquage de supermarché). Un clone de Honda CRX est visible en arrière-plan.
S’ensuivra une séquence de course-poursuite musclée au volant d’un mix de Mercedes-Benz, à l’arrière de Classe E de 2009 et à l’avant de CL de la même période. La police, elle, roule en RAM 1500 et en Dodge Charger, dont une grande partie finira assez mal.
La course-poursuite prendra fin grâce à un woody, ces grands breaks aux flancs ornés de bois, qu’on lie à un Chrysler LeBaron Town & Country, tandis que les trois personnages en cavale prendront fuite au volant d’un increvable Chevrolet Express, commercialisé aux États-Unis depuis… 1996.
Oh, et n’oublions pas la curieuse séquence où Lucia dérange un streamer en plein « trunk challenge » qui semble se tenir dans le coffre d’une Dodge Charger de 2006 – une poursuite avec la police embarquant ledit streamer toujours dans le coffre s’ensuit.
Un peu plus tard, une soirée très select est organisée. Jason et Lucia s’y rendent dans un immense SUV inspiré du Rolls-Royce Cullinan, accompagné d’un clone de Range Rover.
Notons enfin deux courtes séquences de course. Une sur circuit, où on pilote ce qui ressemble à une BMW M4 préparée pour la compétition, puis une course de rue au volant d’une simili-Nissan Skyline GT-R R32.
Encore des surprises à prévoir ?
Des pick-ups, des Ford, des Dodge et des Chevrolet : aucun doute, les créateurs de GTA 6 ont voulu fermement ancrer le jeu aux États-Unis (il se déroule dans l’État factice de Leonida, inspiré de la Floride).
Évidemment, le choix des voitures n’est jamais anodin et symbolise les différents mondes dans lesquels le couple évoluera tout au long de l’aventure. Les vieilles muscle-cars usées par la vie se retrouveront dans les quartiers populaires, tandis que les SUV opulents accompagneront les protagonistes dans les strates aisées de la ville.
La « car culture » semble en revanche toujours bien présente. Les références très ciblées (courses de rue au volant des légendes du JDM, la mythique Série 3 E30 cabriolet, le choix des gros SUV) prouvent que les voitures ont un rôle prépondérant dans la perception de l’univers du jeu.
Reste que, chez Survoltés, on reste évidemment sur notre faim : aucune voiture électrique n’est visible le long des 26 minutes de l’extrait. L’aventure prenant place de nos jours, faisons confiance à Rockstar pour insérer des éléments rappelant l’électromobilité.
J’imagine aisément des véhicules inspirés du Tesla Model Y (un Cybertruck aurait carrément sa place !) ou des stations de recharge disséminées çà et là, mais je reste extrêmement curieux de l’expérience de jeu avec ces voitures.
Pourra-t-on par exemple recharger les modèles ? Des courses-poursuites pourraient-elles tourner court si on vole une voiture avec peu d’autonomie ? En parlant de vol, des stratagèmes devront-ils être mis en place pour dérober ces véhicules extrêmement connectés ?
Encore beaucoup de questions, donc, qui trouveront leur réponse à la sortie du jeu prévue le 19 novembre 2026. Les précommandes sont déjà ouvertes.
Tout savoir sur GTA 6 (gameplay, trailer, précommandes)
Les choses accélèrent du côté de Rockstar depuis le début des précommandes pour GTA 6. Prix officiel en France : 80 euros. Surtout, la troisième bande-annonce de GTA 6 est enfin sortie sur Netflix et YouTube à la fin du mois d’août pour montrer de nombreux éléments de gameplay dans le cadre d’un aperçu large très attendu.
Nous avons d’ailleurs décortiqué les 27 minutes de vidéo pour vous résumer tout ce qu’il fallait retenir du gameplay de GTA 6.
Pour aller plus loin, voici, ci-après, quelques lectures intéressantes.
- Ce qui cloche avec l’aperçu étendu de GTA 6.
- Les multiples pannes provoquées par l’aperçu étendu de GTA 6.
- Pourquoi il vous faut forcément un compte pour regarder le trailer sur YouTube.
Rendez-vous enfin le 19 novembre pour la sortie officielle de GTA 6 qui n’a que trop souvent été repoussée.
