articles.title: Timia Capital expands B2B tech lending capacity with funding from SAF Group | BetaKit
articles.text:
Toronto-based Timia Capital has bolstered its lending capacity by $60 million CAD, giving it the ability to provide larger loans to more business-to-business (B2B) technology companies.
The news: Timia provides debt to B2B tech firms across Canada and the United States, focusing on B2B software-as-a-service and software-enabled companies with product-market fit, with between $2 million and $20 million in annual recurring revenue and gross margins of 50 percent or more. The lender announced on Tuesday that it has expanded its ability to lend to startups that fit this profile by $60 million, thanks to a $25-million credit facility from Calgary-based alternative investment and private credit firm SAF Group.
From the source: In a blog post, Timia CEO Michael Wallace said many tech founders “are deliberately combining equity and debt to reduce dilution and maintain control” amid uncertain venture capital market conditions. He said Timia has identified “a strong pipeline” of companies building sustainable businesses and seeking flexible capital to fuel their growth. “This facility allows us to support more of those founders with larger investments,” he said.
The context: Founded in 2015, Timia’s website claims the firm has provided more than $200 million worth of loans to 80 portfolio companies to date, making this expansion a significant one for the growing tech lender, whose current investments include Toronto-based digital marketing startup Webware AI and Mississauga telematics software company BrightOrder. Timia counts Vancouver-based permitting software provider Clariti, Calgary payroll tech company Wagepoint, and FinTech firm Beanworks among its exits. Toronto venture capital firm Round13 Capital acquired Timia in 2024 to round out its suite of financing options.
Final thought: The private credit industry is booming, and small but growing Canadian players like Timia and larger Vancouver-based peer Vistara Growth—which is raising a new fund of its own—are scaling up to meet demand from tech entrepreneurs.
Feature image courtesy Unsplash. Photo by Romain Dancre.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (August 27, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (August 27, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Thursday, August 27, 2026.
From Bill Gates' call for taxing AI and reserving jobs for humans to Deepinder Goyal-backed Temple's acquisition of Longevous, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured stories
Bill Gates calls for taxing AI, reserving some jobs for humans
Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates has called for governments to take concrete steps to manage the upheaval caused by artificial intelligence, saying that they should tax AI and robots, strengthen support for displaced workers and deliberately set aside some jobs for humans. His proposals come as AI advances rapidly and begins to take on tasks once considered dependent on human judgement. Gates warns that governments are not preparing quickly enough for a technology that could reshape employment, public services, security and everyday life.
Read more
SugarStrings.ai uses simple cheek swabs to identify thousands of genetic disorders
Bengaluru-based healthtech startup SugarStrings.ai has developed a non-invasive DNA test that screens users for more than 7,442 genetic disorders, and aims to make genetic testing more accessible and privacy-focused.
Latest news
Deepinder Goyal’s wearable startup Temple acquires London-based Longevous
Deepinder Goyal-backed Temple has acquired evidence-based Longevous as it builds its clinical and scientific capabilities ahead of its launch. As part of the acquisition, London-headquartered Longevous founders Dr Robert Mohr and Dr Avi Roy, along with their team, will join Temple full-time.
Funding news
Logistics tech startup TrucksUp raises $8.2M in growth funding
Gurugram-based logistics technology platform TrucksUp has raised $8.2 million in funding from institutions, family offices along with participation from the Co-founders, Sarthak Shah Elwadhi and Aviraj Singh Chadha.
Astrology platform InstaAstro raises $12M in Series A round
InstaAstro, a Noida-based online astrology platform, has raised $12 million in a Series A round led by Singularity AMC and Artha Venture Fund, with participation from its founders. InstaAstro will use the funding to build AI-led solutions, including sentiment analysis to help astrologers deliver more contextual consultations and multilingual support to improve the consultation experience across languages. It also plans to expand its pooja seva and spiritual commerce businesses.
InspeCity inches closer to orbit with Rs 100 Cr funding boost
Spacetech startup InspeCity has raised Rs 100 crore in a pre-Series A round of funding led by Speciale Invest, Ashish Kacholia, Antler India, Manish Gandhi, Shastra VC, and others.
Biryani Bees raises $1M from Vivek Oberoi Family office
Biryani Bees, a biryani and Indian meals brand, has raised $1 million from the Vivek Oberoi Family Office to accelerate its expansion across India’s Tier II markets. The company currently operates three outlets in Uttar Pradesh and plans to expand to 10 outlets across Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and other high-potential Tier II markets.
The funding will initially support the expansion to 10 outlets, strengthen central kitchen infrastructure, build the operating team and establish a repeatable expansion model. Biryani Bees said the investment will help it take its existing business model into new markets while strengthening the infrastructure required to scale across multiple states. Its long-term ambition is to build a national network offering standardised, affordable and quality daily meals.
OORJAA raises Rs 9.7 Cr in Series A funding
Technology-led logistics platform OORJAA has raised Rs 9.7 crore in a Series A round led by Equentis Angel Fund, with participation from Inflection Point Ventures. The company will deploy the capital towards technology and product development, scaling its proprietary AI/SaaS logistics stack Datashastra, and strengthening its control-tower and automation capabilities.
OORJAA will also expand its mid-mile and last-mile network across new cities and categories, take Datashastra into international markets beginning with the GCC, and hire talent across technology, operations and enterprise sales.
The company operates an asset-light, full-stack model combining hubs, fleet and manpower with its technology platform. It currently moves more than three million products and 50,000 last-mile orders daily across over 200 cities.
Edgeverse raises Rs 3 crore from GVFL
GVFL has invested Rs 3 crore in Edgeverse India, a deep-tech startup developing edge AI-based perception technology for mobility and other real-world applications. The investment will support Edgeverse's next phase of growth, including the development of India-specific road intelligence, camera and radar technology, and the commercialisation of its AI-powered perception solutions. Edgeverse previously received Rs 1.85 crore in seed funding from ARTPARK and was selected as one of the winners of the NASSCOM Mobility Innovation Challenge 2025.
Founded in 2023 by Arindam Ghosh, Subrata Debnath and Navaneeth A, Edgeverse is building a hardware-agnostic perception stack that combines edge AI with sensors such as cameras and radar. The technology is designed to help original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and Tier-I suppliers deploy advanced safety and perception capabilities across vehicles.
Velaan Mart raises Rs 1.26 Cr in funding
Velaan Mart Agritech has raised Rs 1.26 crore in funding from Next Bharat Ventures. This agritech startup is building an organised farm-to-institution supply chain designed to improve market access for farmers while providing fresh and quality-assured produce to institutional and commercial buyers.
The company currently operates across Tiruchirappalli, Thanjavur, Pudukkottai and Karaikudi, serving colleges, hostels, restaurants and other institutional customers through its integrated procurement and distribution network. Existing agricultural supply chain has several inefficiencies and Velaan Mart aims to address this gap by creating a direct connection between farmers and bulk buyers.
The company sources fresh produce closer to the point of origin and manages procurement, quality checks, processing, storage and distribution through an integrated supply chain. Its model is focused on reducing unnecessary intermediaries while creating greater transparency around pricing, quality and sourcing.
Other news
Swiggy’s Food on Train grows 12x in two years
Swiggy’s Food on Train service has grown 12-fold between August 2024 and August 2026, with adoption in Tier-2 and Tier-3 markets growing twice as fast as in metropolitan cities. The service has expanded to 201 railway stations, up from 66 in 2024.
Swiggy has also introduced two features to make train-food ordering easier. ‘Search by Train’ allows users to enter their train number or name to see food options mapped to their route and schedule. The ‘99 Store Widget’ provides passengers with quick access to budget-friendly meals.
Swiggy said food preferences among train travellers are also changing, with demand rising for lassi, buttermilk and mojitos, while traditional meals such as thalis account for more than 65% of orders. Sweet orders have increased 110%, led by rasgullas.
Flipkart Ads launches Saarthi for sellers and brands
Flipkart has launched Saarthi, an Ads Partner Program designed to provide sellers and brands with professional advertising support at zero cost. The programme combines an AI-powered campaign tool with a network of certified agency partners offering hands-on campaign management. Flipkart said sellers have identified campaign complexity, uncertainty over where to begin and difficulty understanding campaign performance as key challenges.
Saarthi aims to address these issues by helping businesses navigate digital advertising and improve campaign effectiveness. Agencies such as Accenture and Dentsu have been integrated into Flipkart’s ad-tech ecosystem and can guide sellers from campaign creation to sustained growth. Sellers and brands will be matched with agency partners based on their business stage, growth objectives and advertising readiness. The programme also offers campaign optimisation, knowledge and guidance.
T-Hub, Honda launch Innovation Challenge 2.0
T-Hub and Honda Digital Innovation India have partnered to launch Honda Innovation Challenge 2.0, a year-long programme aimed at co-building digital mobility and customer experience solutions with Indian startups. The programme features three new challenges and total funding of up to Rs 4.8 crore. Each challenge will select four startups eligible for up to Rs 40 lakh to develop proof-of-concept projects with Honda teams, significantly higher than the Rs 10 lakh available under the first challenge.
Selected startups will work directly with Honda engineering and business teams during a 12-week sprint and gain access to testing environments, operational insights and deployment support. Successful PoCs can progress to pilots and potentially be integrated into Honda products or services. The programme is open to startups across India.
Rodic Consultants partners with Nasscom for InfraAI Innovation challenge
Rodic Consultants, one of India's leading infrastructure and engineering consultancies, has partnered with Nasscom to launch the Rodic InfraAI Innovation Challenge, a first-of-its-kind initiative aimed at accelerating the adoption of artificial intelligence across India's infrastructure and strategic sectors. Supported by Startup India through outreach to DPIIT-recognised startups, the initiative seeks to bring together the country's rapidly expanding AI and deep-tech ecosystem to develop scalable, deployment-ready solutions for some of India's most pressing infrastructure challenges.
The Innovation Challenge marks the first milestone in a broader strategic partnership between Rodic Consultants and Nasscom to discover, nurture and deploy frontier AI technologies across live infrastructure projects in India. By combining Rodic’s extensive domain expertise, real-world project environments and infrastructure problem statements with Nasscom’s innovation ecosystem, while leveraging Startup India’s outreach to DPIIT-recognised startups.
VenturEdu launches zero-fee Emerging Founders Program
VenturEdu has launched the Emerging Founders Program, a zero-fee residential venture-building initiative for aspiring entrepreneurs aged 18 to 28. The programme is open to solo founders and teams of up to four members, with no previous startup experience required. Selected teams attending a two-day bootcamp in Gurgaon in September will be eligible for a stipend of up to Rs 50,000 per team, along with travel reimbursement of up to Rs 5,000.
There will be no programme fee or equity dilution. Twenty-five founders will subsequently be selected for a two-month residency from October 1 to November 30. They will receive mentorship and work on validating ideas, developing products and building business models. The top five startups will gain direct entry into the Fibonacci X accelerator.
Veranda K-12 expands AVINYA innovation challenge
Veranda K-12, a Veranda Learning enterprise, has announced the third season of AVINYA: An Innovation Hub, its flagship innovation challenge for school students. The programme encourages students to identify real-world problems and develop solutions aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.
After attracting more than 300 schools and 800 ideas in its first two editions, the 2026–27 edition will expand to over 100 cities and towns and reach more than one lakh students. Students from Grades 8 to 12 can participate. Online submissions will be followed by a presentation round, with 50–60 ideas shortlisted and the top 15 teams advancing to the national finale at IIIT Bengaluru on December 4–5, 2026. The finalists will receive mentorship and innovation training, while the top three ideas will receive special recognition.
LTM opens global delivery & AI centre in Kolkata
LTM has inaugurated a global delivery and AI competency centre in Kolkata, reinforcing the L&T Group’s long-term commitment to West Bengal as a technology and innovation hub. The facility is expected to support LTM’s growing global delivery capabilities and AI ambitions while creating opportunities for skilled professionals in West Bengal and neighbouring states.
Kolkata’s educational ecosystem, talent pool and expanding digital infrastructure were highlighted as key factors behind the company’s India growth strategy. The centre will serve as a hub for collaboration, innovation and delivery excellence, enabling LTM to support clients globally while contributing to the state’s economic development. The company said the new facility also strengthens its nationwide delivery network and reflects its continued investment in regional centres, digital infrastructure and employee experience.
Pensionbazaar launches Wealth 360 portfolio tracker
Pensionbazaar has launched Wealth 360, a unified portfolio tracking platform designed to give users a consolidated view of their investments and savings. With user consent, the platform brings together bank accounts, fixed deposits, mutual funds, stocks and the National Pension System in one dashboard.
Pensionbazaar said Indian consumers increasingly manage savings across multiple products and institutions, making it difficult to track overall wealth, returns, asset allocation and progress towards financial goals. Wealth 360 aims to address this fragmentation by providing a single view of a user’s financial portfolio.
Vishwajeet Goel, Head of Pensionbazaar, said investors do not need more products but “one clear view” of everything they have built. The platform also integrates retirement savings with everyday investments to provide a broader view of financial planning.
AMU targets Rs 400 Cr EV financing AUM by 2027
Accelerated Money for Upliftment (AMU), an electric vehicle financing company, is targeting EV financing assets under management (AUM) of Rs 400 crore by March 2027 and plans to increase this to Rs 600 crore by March 2028. The company expects its EV financing business to record 35–40% growth in disbursements, driven primarily by electric commercial vehicles. Commercial EVs currently account for 100% of AMU’s EV financing portfolio, reflecting its focus on the commercial mobility segment.
The company’s EV financing portfolio has recorded a CAGR of around 38%. AMU currently operates across Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal, Bihar and Haryana, financing electric commercial vehicles used for passenger and cargo mobility. It expects demand to remain supported by the lower operating costs and improving economics of electric mobility.
Binance launches Agent OS for AI-powered applications
Crypto exchange Binance has introduced Agent OS, a developer platform designed to provide standardised access for AI applications to Binance’s trading, market data, wallet, payment and on-chain capabilities. Built under Binance Intelligence, the initiative aims to provide AI builders, fintech developers and quantitative trading teams with a controlled foundation for developing applications and agents that interact with financial infrastructure.
Agent OS supports ready-made integrations as well as users’ own AI agents. Through tools including ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, users can authorise agents to access market data, view account information and conduct supported trading activities, subject to configured permissions and limits. Binance said users can also assign individual agents to dedicated subaccounts, allowing them to segregate funds and trading activity.
NABARD, NaBFID sign MoU on rural infrastructure financing
The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) and the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) have signed a memorandum of understanding to strengthen collaboration in financing infrastructure projects with significant rural impact. The partnership combines NABARD’s expertise in rural and agricultural infrastructure with NaBFID’s specialised infrastructure financing capabilities.
Under the agreement, the institutions will explore joint financing, knowledge sharing and innovative financing solutions aimed at expanding access to long-term and competitively priced funding for projects that can strengthen rural infrastructure and value chains. Their collaboration will cover project identification, appraisal, due diligence, credit structuring, pricing and joint monitoring. They will also work on project structuring, financial modelling and debt syndication, alongside joint capacity-building initiatives drawing on the training institutions of both organisations.
Tulu Health launches Longevity OS
AI-native healthcare company Tulu Health has launched Longevity OS, a platform designed to convert fragmented clinical, laboratory, wearable and patient engagement data into daily actions for improving patient retention, engagement and clinic revenue. The company has also announced plans to expand its presence in the US. Tulu Health said its AI systems have already automated more than 100,000 healthcare operational tasks, with year-on-year growth exceeding 90%.
Longevity OS creates a unified patient twin and uses AI Voice, SMS and other channels to identify patients who may be at risk of disengagement before renewal. The company said longevity and wellness clinics often collect large volumes of patient data but lack tools to turn that information into timely interventions. The new platform aims to bridge that gap by translating data into actionable insights.
IndiaFirst Life selects Salesforce Agentforce
IndiaFirst Life Insurance Company, a Bank of Baroda subsidiary, has selected Salesforce’s Agentforce to advance its enterprise-wide artificial intelligence transformation. The insurer plans to embed AI agents into critical processes to improve sales, streamline operations and enhance customer experience. The initiative builds on IndiaFirst Life’s unified Salesforce platform, which supports the insurance journey from lead generation through claims settlement.
The company serves customers across more than 90% of India’s pin codes and continues to expand its distribution network. IndiaFirst Life will deploy Agentforce across three priority areas: new business underwriting, customer service and claims processing. Salesforce said the initiative represents the next phase of its collaboration with the insurer and supports IndiaFirst Life’s ambition to develop a more intelligent and customer-centric life insurance experience through greater use of AI across key business processes.
GSM VinFast, ARC Electric partner for corporate EV mobility
GSM VinFast has partnered with ARC Electric, a B2B electric mobility platform, to strengthen electric vehicle-based corporate mobility services. Under the partnership, ARC Electric will facilitate electric cab services for ad-hoc travel, airport transfers and employee transportation services, initially across Delhi NCR.
The companies plan to expand the offering to other Indian cities. The partnership combines GSM VinFast’s EV ecosystem with ARC Electric’s corporate mobility expertise to provide businesses with premium and sustainable transportation options. Services will cover daily employee commutes, airport transfers, on-demand travel and other corporate requirements. The initiative forms part of GSM VinFast’s broader 2,000-cab collaboration and aims to help organisations integrate EVs into regular transportation while advancing sustainability and carbon-reduction goals.
WACKER sets up Global Capability Center in Pune with HCLTech
Wacker Chemie AG has established a Global Capability Center in Pune in collaboration with HCLTech. The centre will support WACKER’s engineering, IT and digital transformation initiatives while providing a flexible and future-ready delivery foundation. Fabian Seibold, Director, WACKER Excellence Hub Pune, said the centre would strengthen the company’s global delivery and digital execution capabilities, while HCLTech’s experience in building and scaling such centres would support agility, governance and long-term growth.
Dr Frank Fehler, Executive Vice President and Country Head-Germany at HCLTech, said the expanded engagement marks an important milestone in WACKER’s digital transformation. The new centre builds on the strategic partnership between the two companies and is intended to support WACKER’s long-term engineering and digital transformation journey.
Wipro expands Google Cloud partnership on Gemini Enterprise
Wipro has expanded its partnership with Google Cloud to accelerate enterprise-wide adoption of Gemini Enterprise and agentic AI. As part of the initiative, Wipro is scaling its internal deployment of Gemini Enterprise and plans to empower more than 10,000 AI-certified specialists, including 1,500 Forward Deployed Engineers, with advanced AI capabilities.
The company has also launched the LIFT (Launch-Ignite-Flywheel-Transform) framework to help enterprises accelerate AI transformation and operationalise agentic AI at scale. Powered by Wipro Intelligence, LIFT integrates Gemini Enterprise with Wipro’s AI-powered delivery platforms, WINGS and WEGA. The combined ecosystem is designed to help businesses move beyond basic task automation towards secure, autonomous AI agents embedded in multi-step workflows. Wipro is building a dedicated team of more than 1,500 certified FDEs to scale AI adoption.
Three medtech startups selected for Ginserv accelerator
Three Indian medtech startups have emerged as winners of HealthSprint 2026, a joint initiative of the Consulate General of Israel in Bengaluru and Bengaluru-based Techstartup Accelerator GINSERV, aimed at helping Indian healthcare innovators strengthen their businesses, investability and expand into global markets.
The three winners are: BioCipher Labs, Bengaluru, an AI-powered molecular diagnostics startup, Prodancy, Bengaluru, a medtech company that has developed an indigenous surgical helmet for joint replacement procedures, aimed at replacing imported consumables and Mykare.ai, Kochi, an AI-native patient management platform designed for clinics and smaller hospitals. The winners will receive a fully funded, one-week immersive programme in Israel, giving them an opportunity to engage with the country’s healthcare and innovation ecosystem and explore pathways to validate, scale and expand their businesses into global markets.
Kore.ai named Leader by three analyst firms
Enterprise AI platform company Kore.ai has been named a Leader by Gartner, Forrester and Everest Group in their latest evaluations of the enterprise AI market. The recognitions span five categories: agentic AI products, conversational AI platforms, customer service, employee services and enterprise search. Kore.ai said the recognition across three independent analyst firms carries significance because each evaluates the market using different criteria, perspectives and assessment cycles.
The company’s technology portfolio includes conversational AI, generative AI and agentic AI capabilities. Kore.ai also highlighted its patent portfolio covering areas such as agent definition language, constraint enforcement, multi-agent coordination, agent evaluation and governance.
Netscout enhances Arbor Edge Defense against DDoS attacks
Netscout has announced enhancements to its Arbor Edge Defense solution, aimed at helping enterprises protect mission-critical and revenue-generating applications from sophisticated distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks. The enhanced solution is designed to identify malicious sources concealed behind shared content delivery network infrastructure and apply service-specific countermeasures.
This allows organisations to block attacks while continuing to provide access to legitimate customers using the same CDN. The updated AED capabilities include revealing attack sources hidden by CDN proxies, stopping application-layer attacks and protecting applications through service-specific policies. Netscout said the solution can also preserve legitimate customer access, defend both direct and CDN-mediated traffic paths, and extend existing CDN investments.

articles.title: Oxmiq Labs HBF in AI Compute at Hot Chips 2026
articles.text:
Oxmiq Labs is presenting HBF in AI Compute at Hot Chips 2026, making the case for high-bandwidth flash as a capacity tier for AI inference. This ended up being a major discussion topic, so we wanted to get this one out and its own day to give it a bit more exposure.
We did this one live, but it got stuck in the queue.
Oxmiq Labs HBF in AI Compute at Hot Chips 2026
Oxmiq opens by laying out the HBF hardware specification across three grades. Maximum user bandwidth rises from 0.384 TB/s to 3.072 TB/s and UCIe rates climb from 8 GT/s to 32 GT/s, while capacity tops out at 512 GiB on a 16-high stack. This pitch is that HBF delivers 8 to 16 times the capacity of HBM at the same cost.
Oxmiq frames HBF within the memory technology landscape using alpha and beta, with beta tracking cost and alpha tracking bandwidth. A key point is that HBF is a capacity point on this landscape, not a cheaper version of HBM.
Next comes model personality, with a larger MoE model set against dense models in terms of batch size and tokens/s. MoE opens up a small batch capacity sub-phase, where the model is held in full and lower bandwidth is fine.
Oxmiq is now breaking down the cost of serving in terms of a token. They are arguing that the real metric is the cost of serving the token in terms of hold and feed (bandwidth).
Oxmiq lays out a few ways to deploy HBF, covering an HBM-only baseline, an all-HBF configuration, and a 2x HBF-6x HBM mix. All three sit in the same cost envelope, with the HBF options trading bandwidth for capacity. Peak bandwidth drops from 22 TB/s on the HBM baseline to 12.8 TB/s on all-HBF, while capacity jumps from 288 GB to 4 TB.
First, Oxmiq examines an all-HBF system with a short 256-by-256 context. HBF wins on cost at low batch, but with 85 percent “dead capacity.”
Moving to long context at 1M tokens in and 1K out, the picture shifts. Capacity wins only while the bandwidth demand remains low. Beyond that point, HBM is the better option.
The next case considers a mixed case in which HBM acts as a hot-expert cache. Expert popularity flattens across mixed queries, so caching pays off only at low batch sizes or when similar queries are batched together.
Oxmiq details its system and simulation setup at the rack level across a 72-GPU rack. Using a decode-centric Kimi-K2 1T model at FP4 with 1M tokens in and 1K out, the simulation finds that for the same rack and cost, HBF buys roughly 14x the capacity for about 0.6x the bandwidth.
A first sim check plots rack dollars per token against single-server capacity. Cheaper dollars per GB does not equal cheaper dollars per token. This is neat as the math exercise behind why not HBF, or maybe more where HBF is playing.
Going into that first chart they are mapping the same trade across batch sizes. HBM keeps its edge at the rack scale, while HBF fits best where capacity per box is the goal, a useful split for buyers choosing deployment scale.
Here is the other chart that zeroes in on the bandwidth-versus-capacity split within a single server. Matching memory to deployment scale matters as much as the sticker price per gigabyte.
Oxmiq then turns to the software constraints of HBF. Access happens in 64 KB chunks for maximum bandwidth, with roughly 24 hours of power-on data retention at 85 degrees Celsius and host-managed lifecycle handling. Since the memory is read-optimized and write-constrained, placement becomes a software problem.
The company walks through the inference engine ecosystem, ranging from production serving engines like vLLM and SGLang to vendor-optimized stacks such as TensorRT-LLM and AWS Neuron. Oxmiq treats vLLM as the production default and the focus for HBF.
Oxmiq then looks at where the memory actually goes in a model like Kimi-K3. Roughly 93 percent of bytes are MoE expert weights at 1.45 TB, so Oxmiq argues HBF suits the MoE expert pool and KV-cache offload, while HBM handles attention weights and hot data.
Inside vLLM, Oxmiq proposes a plugin that uses HBF in place of host CPU pinned memory for the KV cache and MoE expert pools. A GPU with 4x HBM and 4x HBF stacks would reach 2.2 TB with about 17.4 TB/s peak bandwidth, far more capacity than today’s offload paths.
Oxmiq sees attention sparsity as a genuine HBF fit. Sparse-attention models such as DeepSeek Sparse Attention and Compressed Sparse Attention play directly into HBF’s low-bandwidth capacity zone, though the fit stays conditional on that model style.
Oxmiq closes its case with expert parallelism. Cheap HBF capacity means fewer EP shards and less all-to-all communication, allowing 2 nodes to hold experts locally in HBF instead of sharding them across 8 GPUs and incurring all-to-all traffic at every layer.
Oxmiq wraps with a set of takeaways that frame HBF through a much narrower lens than some of the major NAND vendors. Really, it concludes that HBF wins only where bandwidth demand is low, such as MoE with small batch and long-context sparse KV.
Those observations are an interesting framing, to say the least, especially compared to many HBF promoters, who are less balanced in their messaging.
Final Words
HBF looks like a capacity instrument aimed at a narrow but real slice of inference work, particularly large MoE models where expert weights dominate. Matching memory type to workload and deployment scale matters more than raw dollars per gigabyte. On the software side, it seems like an HBF allocator and placement policy are the missing pieces before this becomes practical. That said, it is probably less of a lift than it would have been without AI-native coding tools to help. It was really neat to see a candid take like this.

articles.title: Cyberattack Causes Global Disruption at Boston Scientific
articles.text:
US medical technology giant Boston Scientific has been targeted in a cyberattack that has caused significant disruption to its global operations.
Boston Scientific develops and manufactures devices and therapies used primarily in cardiology, neurology, oncology, and other interventional medical procedures.
The company said it detected a cybersecurity incident affecting some IT systems on August 25. The attack caused a network outage and disrupted operations.
“The incident has impacted access to certain operating systems and business applications, including the ability to process and ship customer orders,” Boston Scientific noted in a statement shared on its website.
The company said it could not provide a timeline for full restoration of affected systems.
“The Company’s investigation of the cybersecurity incident is ongoing, and the full scope, nature and impacts, including operational and financial impacts, of the incident are not yet known,” Boston Scientific said in an SEC filing on Wednesday.
It’s unclear whether the incident has also resulted in a data breach. It’s not uncommon for intrusions that cause significant disruption to involve the theft of personal and other sensitive information.
No known cybercrime group appears to have taken credit for an attack on Boston Scientific.
SecurityWeek has reached out to the company to find out whether a ransomware or extortion group is behind the attack and will update this article if it responds.

articles.title: World’s first superconducting quantum heat engine could help unlock massive quantum computers
articles.text:
World’s first superconducting quantum heat engine could help unlock massive quantum computers
Scientists have built a tiny superconducting heat engine that turns quantum-scale heat into useful work—and could help make massive quantum computers far easier to build.
- Date:
- August 14, 2026
- Source:
- Aalto University
- Summary:
- A tiny superconducting engine has successfully converted heat near absolute zero into useful work, demonstrating the first cyclic quantum heat engine of its kind. Future versions could operate autonomously inside quantum computers, potentially eliminating huge numbers of costly, noise-producing microwave cables.
- Share:
A newly developed superconducting quantum heat engine could deepen our understanding of thermodynamics while helping advance technologies needed for quantum computers with very large numbers of qubits.
Scientists are getting a clearer picture of how thermodynamics behaves in the quantum world, and that progress could benefit both quantum technology and our understanding of familiar thermodynamic principles. Researchers at Aalto University have now taken an important step by demonstrating the first cyclic quantum heat engine built inside a superconducting circuit.
The experiment connects two areas of physics that normally describe very different scales. Quantum mechanics explains the behavior of matter at extremely small scales, even below the size of atoms, while thermodynamics describes how heat and energy behave in much larger systems, from collections of molecules to the universe itself. Bringing the two together raises a fundamental question: what happens to familiar thermodynamic processes when quantum effects such as tunneling, entanglement, and superposition enter the picture?
A Heat Engine Built for the Quantum World
Conventional heat engines turn heat into useful work. James Watt's steam engine is one famous example, but the same basic concept remains central to modern transportation and electricity production, powering cars, ships, planes and many power plants.
The researchers have now created the world's first superconducting quantum heat engine. The extremely small device combines a transmon qubit, a resonator and a quantum refrigerator.
Operating under ultracold quantum conditions, the engine was able to use the tiny amount of available heat to repeatedly produce positive work. Achieving this kind of cyclic operation has been an important objective for researchers working on quantum heat engines. The result provides a proof of concept for superconducting heat engines that could eventually contribute to improved quantum computing technology.
The study, led by Academy Professor Mikko Möttönen, was published in Nature Communications.
Recreating an Otto Cycle Near Absolute Zero
To make the engine operate, the researchers reproduced an Otto cycle inside a superconducting circuit. The Otto cycle is a thermodynamic process also used in car engines and other conventional machines.
"In our experiment, we built a nanofabricated heat engine using superconducting circuits and operated it in a cryostat near absolute zero. At its heart is a transmon qubit, one of the basic building blocks of modern quantum technologies," says Tuomas Uusnäkki, the study's first author.
The researchers connected the transmon qubit to a quantum circuit refrigerator, allowing them to control heat flow on the quantum scale and demonstrate that this heat could be transformed into measurable work. A conventional heat engine normally relies on separate hot and cold environments. In this system, however, the same quantum refrigerator can supply both heating and cooling.
"Our quantum-circuit refrigerator can be tuned to both heat and cool the qubit on demand. Using carefully timed control pulses, we drove the engine in an Otto cycle and monitored the qubit state as the engine ran," explains Uusnäkki.
Measurements showed that heat passing through the qubit during the cycle was producing positive work.
"This is the first experimental demonstration of a cyclic quantum heat engine in superconducting circuits. Using a single controllable quantum refrigerator as both the hot and cold environment of the engine makes it simpler and more versatile," says Uusnäkki.
Toward Autonomous Quantum Computer Hardware
The researchers are now trying to improve the design and eventually develop a fully autonomous heat engine. One possible use would be reading out qubits without having to carry a microwave pulse from millikelvin temperatures all the way to room temperature.
That capability could become especially valuable as quantum computers grow. Autonomous devices integrated directly into superconducting circuits could reduce both the cost and complexity of machines containing very large numbers of qubits.
"Finland's Quantum Technology Strategy envisions a quantum computer with one thousand logical qubits by 2035, which probably means hundreds of thousands of physical qubits. Doing that with current technology requires millions of microwave cables costing thousand euros each. The cables also introduce noise into the system. Using autonomous devices instead would mostly eliminate the need for those cables," Möttönen says.
Reducing the need for those microwave connections could therefore address two challenges at once: the enormous hardware requirements of large quantum computers and the unwanted noise that cables can introduce into quantum systems.
The pioneering experiment was carried out using OtaNano, Finland's national research infrastructure for nano, micro and quantum technology. Funding came from the Research Council of Finland and the Finnish Cultural Foundation.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Aalto University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Tuomas Uusnäkki, Timm Mörstedt, Wallace Teixeira, Miika Rasola, Mikko Möttönen. Initial demonstration of a quantum heat engine based on dissipation-engineered superconducting circuits. Nature Communications, 2026; 17 (1) DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-72651-x

articles.title: Speedo’s new smart goggles module can track all four swim strokes
articles.text:
Speedo is launching a removable smart module for its Vanquisher goggles that can analyze a swimmer’s performance across all four swim strokes: freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, and butterfly. The new Speedo iQ system uses swim-specific sensors to analyze head movement in the water, time breaths, and track distance per stroke.
Speedo’s new smart goggles module can track all four swim strokes
A removable Speedo iQ module tracks swim strokes, head movement, breaths, distance, and more.
Unlike other smart goggles, such as those from Form, Speedo’s iQ system doesn’t come with a built-in display. Instead, the Speedo iQ module automatically transmits data to its accompanying app, allowing swimmers to see their performance when they get out of the water. Additionally, Speedo notes that you can simply transfer the module to another pair of Vanquisher goggles if they need to be replaced.
The Speedo iQ system doesn’t require a subscription, and it’s also legal to use during World Aquatics competitions. The Vanquisher goggles with the iQ module included cost $189. They’re available to order now in a variety of colors.

articles.title: « Inepte » : le patron de Nvidia vient de pulvériser le plus grand fantasme de l’intelligence artificielle
articles.text:
C’est probablement la fin d’un concept marketing qui a largement porté le secteur de l’intelligence artificielle ces dernières années. Lors de la présentation des résultats trimestriels de sa firme, le 26 août, le patron de Nvidia a négligemment dégonflé toute la hype qui restait encore liée au concept d’intelligence artificielle générale, explique The Verge.
Il explique que l’entreprise a atteint ce stade supposément suprême de l’évolution de l’IA, avant de juger « inepte » la situation dans laquelle se trouve l’industrie. Une manière de mettre derrière lui un terme qui avait de toute manière été largement vidé de son sens ces dernières années.
L’IA générative crée du contenu en quelques secondes, mais souvent au prix de vos données personnelles. Avec Lumo AI, l’assistant européen de Proton, vos conversations restent 100 % confidentielles.
Une expression galvaudée
Emprunté à la science-fiction, ce terme désignait à l’origine l’idée d’un modèle d’intelligence artificielle aussi intelligent et capable que le cerveau humain dans toutes les tâches. Une espèce de stade ultime de l’évolution de la machine en quelque sorte. Il a cependant été très rapidement galvaudé par différents acteurs du secteur.
La charte d’OpenAI définit, par exemple, l’intelligence artificielle générale comme la capacité d’un modèle à « dépasser les capacités humaines dans la plupart des tâches économiquement pertinentes ». Dans l’accord noué entre la firme de Sam Altman et Microsoft, le cap est encore plus explicite : l’AGI serait atteinte quand OpenAI aura dégagé 100 milliards de dollars de bénéfices.
En parallèle, bon nombre d’entreprises ont annoncé l’avènement de l’AGI pour 2026, 2030 ou 2035. Ce n’est même pas la première fois que Jensen Huang affirme avoir atteint ce stade de développement ultime de l’IA, puisqu’il faisait des déclarations similaires en mars dernier déjà.
Cap sur la rentabilité
Au fur et à mesure que la définition et les dates butoirs devenaient de plus en plus floues, les langues ont commencé à se délier, Dario Amodei, patron d’Anthropic, allant jusqu’à avouer en janvier 2025 que cette idée n’était plus qu’un simple terme marketing.
    Pour aller plus loin
            C’est quoi un token dans l’IA ? Tout comprendre à une notion primordiale
            
Usée jusqu’à la corde, cette idée vient donc d’être enterrée par Jensen Huang, qui pense que l’IA devra désormais se concentrer sur « la réalisation de tâches utiles et productives » en « générant des tokens rentables ». Un objectif bien plus terre-à-terre et bien plus concret.
Ces déclarations tombent alors que Nvidia vient de signer un trimestre record : 96,2 milliards de dollars de chiffre d’affaires sur les trois mois clos fin juillet, en hausse de 106 % sur un an, bien au-dessus des attentes des analystes. De quoi comprendre pourquoi Jensen Huang préfère désormais vanter des tokens « rentables » plutôt que de brandir la promesse d’une AGI.

articles.title: Welche KI-Modelle laufen auf deinem PC? So findest du es heraus
articles.text:
Lokale KI: So findest du heraus, welche Modelle auf deiner Hardware laufen
Es gibt viele gute Gründe, KI-Modelle herunterzuladen und lokal auf dem eigenen Computer zu betreiben. Ihr behaltet die Hoheit über eure Daten. Nichts wandert in die Cloud eines US‑Anbieters. Weil die Künstliche Intelligenz direkt auf dem Gerät arbeitet, braucht sie schließlich keinen Zugang zum Internet, um zu funktionieren. Und für den vollumfänglichen Zugriff müsst ihr auch kein Abo abschließen.
Je nach Modell kann euch die KI direkt auf dem Speicher wie gewohnt beim Formulieren von Texten, beim Coden oder bei der Bilderstellung zur Seite stehen. Verknüpft man das Modell mit agentenbasierter Software wie Hermes, kann es auch Aufgaben auf dem Computer erledigen, etwa den Download-Ordner aufräumen.
All das klingt gut, ist aber nicht immer ganz trivial. Denn wie gut so ein lokales Modell läuft, hängt entscheidend von der Hardware ab, die euch zur Verfügung steht – oder vom Budget, falls ihr einen Neukauf plant.

articles.title: 26 minutes de GTA 6 : le résumé de la présentation historique sur Netflix et YouTube
articles.text:
996 jours après une première bande-annonce qui a éclaté tous les records et 478 jours après un trailer 2 resté sans successeur, Rockstar Games a levé le voile sur GTA 6. Pas un trailer, mais une vidéo de 25 minutes et 55 secondes intitulée « Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look », intégralement capturée sur PS5.
L’affluence a eu raison de la plateforme : Netflix est tombé en panne pile à 21 heures, au moment du lancement, avant de revenir à la vie quelques minutes plus tard. La présentation arrivait dans un contexte particulier pour le studio, victime d’une série de leaks pendant dix jours. Elle balaie l’essentiel de ce que les fuites avaient montré : GTA 6 est encore plus beau et son histoire donne envie d’être jouée. La vidéo a été publiée sur YouTube gratuitement à 3 heures du matin.
GTA 6 s’annonce magnifique et dévoile plusieurs missions
Premier constat : GTA 6 est très beau. Le niveau de détail des décors, la gestion de la lumière et les animations placent la barre nettement au-dessus des extraits qui ont fuité ces derniers jours. Reste la question habituelle avec Rockstar : la version finale sera-t-elle à la hauteur de cette démonstration ? Le studio parle d’une captation sur PS5, sans dire si l’on parle de la console standard ou de la PS5 Pro. Le premier serait encore plus incroyable.
La grande nouveauté est le fonctionnement en duo. Jason et Lucia s’échangent des messages, se donnent rendez-vous et opèrent ensemble : on bascule de l’un à l’autre lors de certaines missions.
C’est une vraie évolution par rapport aux trois personnages cloisonnés de GTA 5 : la mécanique est pensée pour que les deux protagonistes agissent ensemble. Leur histoire est totalement liée et, au vu des risques pris, semble condamnée à un destin tragique.
On découvre aussi des missions qui se déclenchent différemment. Fini le point de rendez-vous qui lance immédiatement une cinématique : on entre dans le bâtiment, on avance, on cherche les bons interlocuteurs. Le vol de véhicule se complexifie lui aussi, avec du piratage électronique ou du bris de vitre selon les situations. Rockstar a montré plein de missions différentes : la diversité donne très envie de jouer.
Autre changement : le système de police évolue en profondeur. Le niveau de recherche grimpe désormais jusqu’à six étoiles, et les forces de l’ordre mémorisent vos vêtements comme votre véhicule. Sur ce point précis, les leaks des derniers jours avaient vu juste.
Rockstar a aussi déroulé un aperçu des activités secondaires : musculation, plongée, jet-ski, natation, kayak, basketball, trottinette électrique, courses de voitures, stand de tir, motocross, parachute ou simple bronzette. Certaines sont liées à l’histoire, d’autres relèvent du pur plaisir.
Côté ambiance, l’humour de la série est intact et les séquences nocturnes sont parmi les plus réussies de la vidéo. Une mission se déroule lors de l’inauguration du siège d’une compagnie pétrolière, qui tourne évidemment au carnage. Reste à comprendre comment Jason et Lucia s’y retrouvent mêlés. On note que certains aspects caricaturent les États-Unis et la Floride : celles et ceux qui craignaient un Rockstar plus lisse peuvent souffler.
La présentation s’est terminé sur une série de cinématiques et sur un rappel: GTA 6 sort le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series. La date n’a pas bougé : tous les feux sont verts.
Nos commentaires en direct pendant la présentation Netflix
Numerama a suivi la présentation minute par minute, avec des captures d’écran et nos réactions à chaud. Voici le déroulé complet de la soirée :
Rendez-vous à 21 heures sur Netflix
C’est le grand jour pour Rockstar Games : le jeu sera dévoilé à 21 heures sur la plateforme de streaming Netflix. La vidéo sera ensuite diffusée gratuitement vers 3 heures du matin sur YouTube :
La présentation de GTA 6 durera 26 minutes
Netflix vient d’ajouter des métadonnées à sa vidéo GTA 6 : elle durera 26 minutes et sera tournée exclusivement sur PS5.
Plus que 1 heure pour GTA 6 !
Twitch propose une catégorie spéciale, tous les YouTubers ont commencé des directs, les réseaux sociaux s’emballent… Dans un peu plus d’une heure, la présentation de GTA 6 débutera !
Début dans 10 minutes
L’impatience monte sur le canal Slack de Numerama : que va-t-on apprendre ce soir ? Préparez les popcorns, ça commence bientôt !
Le lien pour accéder à la vidéo sur Netflix
À 21 heures, GTA 6 Un Large Aperçu sera disponible sur Netflix à cette adresse. Nous vous commenterons les grandes découvertes ici avec des captures d’écran.
NETFLIX EST EN PANNE
L’effet GTA 6 : les serveurs de Netflix ont lâché pile à 21 heures. On attend un retour le plus vite possible !
Ok c’est bon, Netflix est de retour
Rafraichissez : Netflix fonctionne. C’est parti pour la présentation de GTA VI qui commence avec une mission de Lucia et Jason. Il n’y a pas de live : c’est une vidéo de 25 minutes et 55 secondes.
On vous redonne le lien :
Des missions beaucoup moins automatiques
Première information : le déclenchement d’une mission prend du temps. Ce n’est plus comme GTA 5 avec un point de rencontre qui lance une cinématique, on peut avancer dans le bâtiment jusqu’à trouver les bons interlocuteurs.
Après une mission en intro, Rockstar montre de nouvelles images du jeu
Le duo entre Jason et Lucia, les scènes de tir, le vol de véhicule plus réaliste avec du piratage ou du bris de vitre… On découvre petit à petit certains aspects de GTA VI, notamment le lien inédit entre les deux personnages principaux qui fonctionnent en duo plutôt qu’en personnages distincts, comme GTA V.
On retrouve l’humour de GTA avec des décors ultra-réalistes qui donnent juste envie d’être le 19 novembre ! C’est beau.
La folle des marteaux est de retour !
Déjà très remarquée avec le premier trailer, la dame aux marteaux fait une apparition sur Netflix.
C’est vraiment très très beau
La vidéo est très décousue : difficile de suivre l’histoire, on enchaîne plusieurs scénettes en apparence sans lien. Mais entre la beauté des graphismes et la complicité entre Jason et Lucia, difficile de ne pas tomber sous le charme. L’attente va-t-elle être à la hauteur ?
Tellement de détails et de réalisme
« Ça transpire de dingue les détails », me dit ma collègue Lisa sur Slack. Et difficile de ne pas être d’accord : le jeu est d’un réalisme assez fou dans cette bande-annonce, c’est nettement supérieur aux leaks des derniers jours. Espérons que la version finale soit aussi belle.
Une nouvelle image juste pour le plaisir
De nouveaux indicateurs pour la police
6 étoiles, des vêtements connus de la police, une voiture connue de la police : les leaks ont eu raison sur le nouveau système pour seumer les flics.
GTA 6 a de nouvelles activités secondaires
Musculation, plongée, jet ski, natation, jumelles, kayak, basketball, trottinette électrique, courses de voitures, stand de tir, bronzette à la plage, motocross, parachute… Rockstar dévoile un aperçu des nouvelles choses que l’on va pouvoir faire dans GTA 6, parfois dans l’histoire, parfois pour le plaisir. Et il y a évidemment beaucoup d’humour.
Une nuit magnifique
Les images des missions nocturnes se révèlent particulièrement magnifiques. Une nouvelle fois, l’attention du détail est au rendez-vous !
Des tueries de milliardaires : GTA est de retour
Une des missions se passe lors de l’inauguration d’un siège d’une entreprise pétrolière : évidemment, ça vire au drame. On a hâte de savoir comment l’histoire de Lucia et Jason les relie à ces événements.
Lucia et Jason peuvent communiquer
Des messages entre les personnages, des passages de l’un à l’autre… La mécanique est vraiment différente de GTA 5 : les personnages sont conçus pour faire des choses ensemble.
Rendez-vous le 19 novembre 2026
Après des aperçus de plusieurs missions, la présentation de GTA 6 se conclut par plusieurs cinématiques du jeu. Rendez-vous le 19 novembre 2026, la date est une nouvelle fois confirmée.
On a beaucoup envie d’y jouer
La hype était déjà forte : elle est stratosphérique après cette présentation Netflix. GTA 6 s’annonce à la hauteur de l’attente : on a tellement hâte d’y jouer.
Les médias invités par Rockstar sortent leurs articles
L’embargo est levé : les journalistes et créateurs invités par Rockstar peuvent donner leur avis sur GTA 6. Voici quelques articles repérés par Numerama :
- IGN : https://www.ign.com/articles/gta-6-new-gameplay-details
- Eurogamer : https://www.eurogamer.net/gta-6-revamping-wanted-system-adding-criminal-profiles
- New York Times : https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/27/arts/grand-theft-auto-vi-trailer-extended-look-rockstar.html

articles.title: Sprains, pain, and whiplash: Waymo and Zoox test drivers are getting hurt as robotaxis scale | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The rapid scaling of robotaxis over the last two years has come with a hidden human cost.
Test drivers for Waymo and Zoox sustained more than two dozen injuries in 2024 and 2025 from hard braking or other sudden movements made by the autonomous vehicles, according to a TechCrunch review of data submitted to the Occupational Safety and Health Administration.
These test drivers, who put autonomous vehicles through their paces on public roads, have suffered sprains, strains, whiplash, and more, according to OSHA data and interviews with former and current workers. Some have been sidelined for weeks or months.
Transdev, which employs and manages Waymo’s test drivers, reported 16 injuries tied to Waymo depot locations in three cities that were caused by the autonomous software braking hard or swerving suddenly. Zoox reported as many as eight worker injuries linked to hard braking.
Other autonomous vehicle companies do not appear in the dataset, though it’s possible they’re exempt. The Zoox and Waymo injuries appear because the companies classify themselves as taxi, limo, or transit services, which OSHA subjects to greater disclosure because they’re “higher-hazard” industries. OSHA also only requires establishments with 100 or more employees in these industries to make this information public, meaning test drivers in newer cities where operations haven’t scaled may have been injured on the job without appearing in this dataset.
TechCrunch was unable to learn whether Waymo or Transdev logged any new injuries in 2026. OSHA does not require companies to submit annual data until the following year as part of the agency’s Injury Tracking Application.
In Zoox’s case, injuries are still happening, according to sources who spoke to TechCrunch on condition of anonymity.
Two current and three former Zoox contractors told TechCrunch that the company’s test fleet vehicles — modified Toyota Highlander SUVs equipped with its self-driving system — were still braking hard and abruptly as recently as July. Three of those contractors said workers are still getting hurt. The workers were granted anonymity to discuss private operations.
Zoox declined to answer specific questions about the injuries it reported last year or the claims contractors made to TechCrunch about the continued hard-braking issues. The company said it follows necessary reporting requirements and takes injuries seriously.
Zoox also said hard-braking incidents are sometimes unavoidable and that the injuries reported last year represent a small percentage of the millions of miles its test fleet traveled.
Waymo also declined to answer questions about the injuries reported to OSHA.
“The safety of our riders, road users, and team is of paramount importance,” Waymo told TechCrunch. “As part of the process of responsibly deploying fully autonomous vehicles, we have driven tens of millions of miles with human operators behind the wheel. This is part of our ongoing validation process and learnings from these trips are integrated into the service.”
Transdev declined to comment.
More miles, more injuries
While Waymo has spent more than a decade developing its self-driving cars, it wasn’t until 2025 that it really started to scale. The company started offering rides in new cities and began mapping and testing in others, growing its commercial fleet to more than 1,500 vehicles by May 2025. Today, that fleet is more than 3,500 vehicles.
Waymo doesn’t break out how many vehicles it uses just for testing. But the amount of autonomous vehicle testing almost certainly increased as the company expanded its service areas and started to familiarize itself with entirely new locations.
Test driver injuries increased, too.
Transdev reported five Waymo test driver injuries in 2024 across San Francisco, Los Angeles, and Phoenix. One was related to hard braking, while the other four were related to erratic vehicle behavior.
In one case, a test driver reported that the car “suddenly backed up” while parking itself and “whipped the steering wheel,” catching his left hand and bending it “to the point he heard a crack in his wrist.” The employee spent more than two months away from work as a result.
The number of injuries jumped to 11 in those three markets in 2025, and hard braking was the cause of nearly all of them. Last September, a test driver in Phoenix wound up having to spend 157 days away from work after their vehicle “made an exaggerated breaking [sic] event without any obstruction.” At least two other injury reports specifically mention that the hard braking happened for no apparent reason.
The only injury report from 2025 that offers a reason for a hard-braking event involved an incident that happened in August in Los Angeles. The employee reported that “some kids were playing in the pathway.” The Waymo robotaxi stopped hard enough that the worker spent 175 days away from their job.
“Software braked harshly”
The Zoox contractors said hard braking — or “brake jabs,” as they are referred to internally — can happen multiple times on a single test drive, sometimes in the same location. They can happen at any speed, though higher-velocity braking incidents typically take a harsher toll on the body, the workers said.
The braking often happens when the autonomous driving system detects — or mistakenly detects — debris of some kind on the road, they said.
The scariest incidents, the contractors said, are when a test vehicle experiences a “nogo” — internal code for an entire system shutdown that often leads to a brake jab.
“You could be going 45 miles per hour and the car will enact a nogo, and suddenly you’re being whipped forward in the middle of the street, in traffic, and you need to be able to take over quickly,” one said.
This behavior shows up repeatedly in the injury reports Zoox submitted to OSHA.
On January 5, 2025, a Zoox test vehicle was driving autonomously in San Francisco when it abruptly slammed on the brakes. The “harsh” stop, as Zoox described it, injured the shoulder and upper arm of a contractor who was inside the SUV, leaving the worker on restricted duty for 16 days.
Later that month, another driver was hurt after a Zoox test vehicle made an “unexpected” stop, injuring their neck and leaving them with a swollen shoulder. It took the contractor eight days to return to work without restrictions.
Most of the Zoox-reported injuries appear to have happened to workers who sit in the driver’s seat of the SUVs. The company also reported an injury to an instructor who trains the test drivers. That injury took place on June 3 in San Francisco, when the test vehicle’s “software braked harshly,” causing the instructor in the back seat to report “sharp pain in lower right ribs and tightness in left shoulder upon returning to base.”
The injured instructor reported additional injuries to the spine and pelvis, though their work restrictions lasted only four days, according to the data.
Seven of the eight entries explicitly mention hard braking, nogos, or brake jabs. The eighth injury involved a worker who was sidelined for the longest amount of time — 46 days — and who reported “extreme back pain” after operating a test vehicle in Las Vegas in May 2025. Zoox wrote that the worker said they “were not sure if it was related to the behavior of the vehicle in autonomy or not but they said it hurts them to drive as well as take deep breaths,” and attributed the injury to a “vehicle maneuver.”
Zoox is dealing with these hard-braking issues as it finally begins offering a true commercial robotaxi service in a bid to compete with Waymo. The Amazon-owned company started charging for rides in its purpose-built robotaxi for the first time this month in Las Vegas. It offers free rides in San Francisco and is testing in Atlanta, Austin, Dallas, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Seattle, and Washington, D.C.
Four of the injuries Zoox reported in 2025 happened after the company issued a recall meant to resolve a year-long federal investigation into the tendency of its autonomous vehicles to brake unexpectedly. Zoox told TechCrunch the recall addressed an extremely narrow braking behavior and said the later incidents — and any resulting injuries — are unrelated to the software fix.
Two of the people who spoke to TechCrunch said that braking can be challenging even when manually driving the Zoox test cars because of the extra weight of the self-driving sensor suite. Test drivers are trained to brake with the extra weight, they said, though they added that minor injuries can be sustained even during that training process.
It’s hard to know if Zoox is experiencing hard-braking incidents with any regularity in its purpose-built vehicles, which do not have traditional controls such as a steering wheel or pedals. They either operate unoccupied or carry passengers who mostly aren’t employees — meaning any injuries wouldn’t be reported to OSHA.
Zoox has reported two robotaxi crashes to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration in the last eight months in which hard braking for debris resulted in the purpose-built vehicles being rear-ended. The company’s descriptions of the crashes don’t specify what debris was spotted in either case.

articles.title: Samsung dévoile son Galaxy S26 FE : avec un prix en hausse, le Galaxy S26 devient son pire ennemi
articles.text:
Samsung dévoile son Galaxy S26 FE : avec un prix en hausse, le Galaxy S26 devient son pire ennemi
Samsung remet le couvert avec un Galaxy S26 FE censé offrir l’essentiel du haut de gamme à un prix plus raisonnable. Nous avons pu le prendre en main. Sur le papier, l’appareil coche presque toutes les cases, mais reste un problème : son positionnement tarifaire peine à le rendre suffisamment désirable.
Je dois l'admettre, j’ai une fascination pour ce qu’on a coutume d’appeler les flagship killers. Rendu célèbre par OnePlus, ce terme désigne un smartphone à la fiche technique sans compromis, sans pour autant faire grimper la facture.
Évidemment, les modèles ultra-premium savent aussi piquer ma curiosité, mais rien ne vaut, à mes yeux, un appareil au positionnement vraiment agressif, capable de tenir tête à des terminaux vendus plus cher, qui peinent ensuite à légitimer le montant affiché sur l’étiquette.
Samsung Galaxy S26 FE
C’est donc avec une certaine excitation que je suis allé découvrir, avant même sa sortie, le nouveau Galaxy S26 flanqué de l’estampille Fan Edition. Chez Samsung, cette dénomination désigne des produits dont les caractéristiques techniques conservent l’essentiel de ce que les aficionados ont apprécié sur les modèles premium, tout en rognant discrètement sur d'autres aspects pour atteindre un tarif plus acceptable.
Si le S25 FE sorti en 2025 brouillait déjà les pistes face au S25+, la firme sud-coréenne recommence cette année avec un modèle très proche de ses grands frères, alors même que la série S est devenue plus chère.
Un clone du Galaxy S26+, à quelques détails près
Avec son gabarit de 161,6 x 76,9 x 7,4 mm pour 193 g sur la balance, le Samsung Galaxy S26 FE est un grand smartphone, quasiment identique à son prédécesseur (161,3 x 76,6 x 7,4 mm, 190 g) et légèrement plus encombrant que le S26+ (158,4 x 75,8 x 7,3 mm, 190 g).
Son look bicolore, typique des modèles FE, avec un cadre métallique et un dos en verre brillant, ainsi que son bloc photo inspiré des S26 présentés en début d’année, lui donnent une allure haut de gamme. Cependant, il a tendance à glisser des mains et retenir les traces de doigts. Trois coloris sont proposés : graphite, bleu et vert d’eau, avec une certification IP68 bienvenue contre l’eau et la poussière.
Son écran Amoled FHD+ de 6,7 pouces est, comme la face arrière, protégé par un verre Gorilla Glass Victus+. Au rayon des concessions, les bordures entourant l’afficheur paraissent moins fines que sur le S26+, tandis que le taux de rafraîchissement oscille entre 60 et 120 Hz (faute de dalle LTPO). Enfin, la marque annonce un pic de luminosité à 1900 cd/m², quand les Galaxy S26 et S26+ promettent jusqu’à 2600 cd/m².
Sous le capot, on retrouve l’Exynos 2500 du Galaxy Z Flip 7, accompagné de… seulement 8 Go de RAM. Samsung garantit néanmoins des gains de 11 % sur les performances CPU, 24 % en jeu mobile et 51 % pour l’IA par rapport au S25 FE.
On peut toutefois s’interroger sur cette quantité de mémoire vive, notamment en matière de durabilité, d’autant plus que le smartphone bénéficie lui aussi d’un suivi logiciel étalé sur sept ans. La batterie de 4900 mAh serait, selon le constructeur, capable de tenir 29 h en lecture vidéo et profite d’une charge rapide à 45 W, lui permettant d’atteindre 70 % en 30 min. S’y ajoutent la charge sans-fil à 15 W et la recharge inversée.
Côté photo, on trouve un capteur principal de 50 mégapixels (OIS) ouvrant à f/1,8, un ultra grand-angle de 12 Mpx (f/2,2) et un téléobjectif x3 de 8 Mpx (f/2,4). La caméra selfie de 12 Mpx (f/2,2) élargit son champ de vision, qui passe de 80 à 85°. Samsung ajoute également My FanCam, qui adapte automatiquement le cadrage aux vidéos verticales, ainsi que la Super stabilité, capable de fonctionner même lorsque le terminal tourne sur lui-même. Enfin, la marque propose un mode nuit amélioré et différentes fonctions de retouche assistées par IA.
Une expérience quasi complète à un prix difficile à défendre
Sous One UI 9, Samsung gratifie évidemment son dernier-né des outils Galaxy AI afin d’offrir une expérience proche des modèles les plus onéreux de la firme. Cela comprend Studio création pour générer images et stickers, la gomme audio, le scan intelligent de documents, Now Brief, Quick Share et Smart Switch.
Circle to Search gagne Find the Look pour retrouver d'un coup les différentes pièces d’un outfit, Now Nudge comprend les conversations et suggère des actions, tandis qu’un assistant IA peut répondre aux appels téléphoniques pour en filtrer l’importance.
Disponible dans nos contrées dès aujourd’hui, le Samsung Galaxy S26 FE s'affiche à 799 € pour son lancement dans sa version 8/128 Go, et 899 € pour passer à 256 Go de stockage, avec six mois de Google AI Pro offerts.
Au moment où j’écris ces lignes, c’est 100 € de plus que le S26 standard, certes plus compact, mais mieux doté en RAM, en stockage, en photo et au niveau de l'affichage. Il reste toutefois 370 € moins cher qu’un S26+ à stockage équivalent, mais au prix de moins de mémoire vive et davantage de sacrifices.
Et c’est là que son positionnement coince. Bien que ce Galaxy S26 FE semble être un très bon smartphone — nous ne manquerons pas de le vérifier en laboratoire —, sa raison d’être me paraît plus floue que jamais. D’autant qu’à moins de 600 € aujourd’hui, le S25 FE semble déjà plus intéressant, sans être finalement si éloigné techniquement.
Outre le fait qu’il me paraît aberrant de proposer en 2026 un terminal avec 128 Go de stockage sans extension possible, difficile de considérer cette nouvelle itération comme un bon plan à sa sortie, voire comme le flagship killer qu’elle espère incarner. À 799 €, l’augmentation de 50 € par rapport au S25 FE aurait été plus facilement acceptée si elle s’était accompagnée d’une capacité de stockage doublée.
Si vous souhaitez changer d’appareil en cette rentrée, je ne peux donc que vous conseiller de vous tourner vers un S26 bien mieux doté, désormais vendu moins cher et pourtant très récent. Si votre budget est vraiment serré, mais que vous souhaitez à tout prix un smartphone Samsung pour son côté rassurant et pérenne en ces temps incertains, face à des constructeurs plus en difficulté, mieux vaut opter pour un Galaxy S25 FE, voire un Galaxy A57.
Cependant, Samsung nous a habitués à baisser assez rapidement le prix de ses terminaux : la patience peut aussi être une solution si ce S26 FE vous fait de l’œil. Car en 2026 plus que jamais — on l’a vu avec les récents Pixel 11 —, le meilleur bon plan de l’année pourrait bien être le modèle de la précédente… au moins jusqu’aux premières promotions.

articles.title: India’s data center boom is leaving the people it displaces with nothing
articles.text:
When Osama Manzar started the nonprofit Digital Empowerment Foundation in 2002, just 1.2% of India’s population was online. Now, more than 70% is. But Manzar’s mission statement — helping poor and rural communities come out of the digital dark to access information, literacy, and livelihoods — still holds.
In the age of artificial intelligence, Manzar senses the risk of another extractive technology, with the benefits and control concentrated among powerful actors both at the algorithmic level and in terms of land and water.
As protests erupt from India to Malaysia to Chile, Manzar — who has served on several Indian government and international policy committees dealing with internet access, digital inclusion, and infrastructure — not only questions how and where the data centers are being built, but also why. Especially when they’re on track to consume water equivalent to that of 1.3 billion people’s annual domestic needs, and require electricity matching the energy demand of 650 million people by 2030.
The conversation has been edited for length and clarity. A recording of the live Rest of World event is available here.
What is the role of local communities in how data center development is happening?
In the U.S., people have come out to ask the government to ban data centers or shut some. In India, we are looking at a government that is viewing data centers as a developmental activity. We need to ask whether it is really development.
You are coming to us to seek our land, our climate, and our space. You need to consult us. You need to consider the community. If you’re taking my land, what are you giving back? I am not even a stakeholder in your data center. You are giving me the promise of creating a lot of jobs. In this case, corporations are not even sure that the local community can be employed in a data center, as it is an automated system.
Could you talk about the awareness and ability of affected communities to fight back?
The government, usually a representative of the people, is shaking hands with data center companies without consulting with their own people. We are already seeing a lot of campaigning happening in the Visakhapatnam area where Google is building a data center. You are giving tax exemption, you are giving land at a very low cost — there are so many questionable approaches taken by the government. At the moment, there’s not much awareness until construction or clearance activity starts. “Data center” is not a term understood by people. People are kept in the dark, and suddenly there is activity in the neighborhood. The reaction could be harsh.
How do you compare the reaction to data centers with other kinds of industrialization?
Factories employ a lot of people. Even if land is taken, there are lots of jobs that are created. In the case of data centers, we are seeing that even the people involved in data creation are getting replaced by AI. Even the artisans are putting a camera on their head and creating data, which will replace them tomorrow.
How do you think the voices of local communities can be included in this conversation?
At a village council level, at a district level, there are people’s representatives available. Locals can be divided into landowners, tillers, agriculturists, and women’s groups. I haven’t heard that any of the groups have been consulted.
In fact, in Telangana, where Microsoft is building a data center hub, we found out that some of the acquired land has been under dispute. Some owners are wondering how they can take back their land. This happens many times when the government is creating sovereign infrastructure like roads or rails, but this is not a sovereign act. These data centers are owned by private entities.
What does “responsible” data center development look like?
Can we not have hyperlocal, multi-distributed data centers? I am happy to have a data center if it’s for the local people. Some people can have a farming need, governance need, business need — this local area needs its own decentralized data centers. Maybe you can divide the country into 250,000 village-level council data centers, or you can have district-level data centers serving their districts only.
Developing countries should not become data waste centers, serving the elite of the world. If you are coming to my neighborhood, first serve us. And if you’re not serving us, go to the place where you will serve them.
Can data centers using renewable energy and less water from natural sources help alleviate the pressure on local communities?
Companies can say that they will not use groundwater or they will extract water from moisture. But that’s their personal problem for which they are going to innovate. It’s for their benefit in terms of efficiency.
At the moment, they are taking land. But what are they giving to the community for the pollution they will create, for the noise they will make? Also, the promises they are making are not on paper.
What is being taken as guaranteed is that the existence of a data center is not negotiable. “Now, let’s discuss energy efficiency, let’s discuss the efficiency of it, let’s choose a location which is not bothering anyone” — but nobody is asking about the existence of the data center itself. That question needs to be asked because it is directly related to the community.
